articleTitle: GameVLM: A Decision-making Framework for Robotic Task Planning Based on Visual Language Models and Zero-sum Games
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: With their prominent scene understanding and reasoning capabilities, pre-trained visual-language models (VLMs) such as GPT-4V have attracted increasing attention in robotic task planning. Compared with traditional task planning strategies, VLMs are strong in multimodal information parsing and code generation and show remarkable efficiency. Although VLMs demonstrate great potential in robotic task planning, they suffer from challenges like hallucination, semantic complexity, and limited context. To handle such issues, this paper proposes a multi-agent framework, i.e., GameVLM, to enhance the decision-making process in robotic task planning. In this study, VLM-based decision and expert agents are presented to conduct the task planning. Specifically, decision agents are used to plan the task, and the expert agent is employed to evaluate these task plans. Zero-sum game theory is introduced to resolve inconsistencies among different agents and determine the optimal solution. Experimental results on real robots demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed framework, with an average success rate of 83.3%. Videos of our experiments are available at https://youtu.be/sam-MKCPP7Y.

articleTitle: An Improved Goal-bias RRT algorithm for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Path Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of Rapidly-Exploring Random Tree (RRT) algorithm for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) path planning, such as inefficient searching, no local planning, and unable to avoid dynamic obstacles effectively, an optimized Goal-bias RRT algorithm is proposed. Firstly, a probability factor is introduced to optimize the sampling method and reduce the global path planning time. Secondly, local path planning idea is introduced to avoid dynamic obstacle. Finally, a node selection strategy is used to re-planning local path so that the running speed and success rate are improved. Combined with the UAV body constraints, trajectory smoothing is carried out using cubic spline interpolation. The simulation experiment results show that the proposed method not only shortens the planning time in comparison with the Goal-bias RRT algorithm, but also has the ability to efficiently deal with dynamic path planning.

articleTitle: Enhancing Predictive Maintenance Hyperparameter Optimization and Adopted Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Maintenance operations constitute a substantial cost element within the manufacturing sector, typically representing 15% to 60% of the plant conversion budget. The optimization of these operations is paramount in reducing costs and avoiding the traditional "Run to Failure" methodology. This research paper investigates machine learning techniques, specifically Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, to enhance the efficacy of predictive maintenance strategies. Utilizing C-MAPSS, NCMAPSS, and the NASA battery dataset, our investigation focuses on predicting machinery's Remaining Useful Life (RUL) and the State of Health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries.Our findings not only demonstrate the effectiveness of models employing a Parallel CNN-LSTM architecture, further optimized through Genetic Algorithms (GA), but also highlight their potential to significantly enhance prediction accuracy compared to conventional models. For instance, an optimized Parallel CNN-LSTM model applied to the C-MAPSS dataset achieved a Test Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 14.98 and an RMSE of 0.047 on the NASA battery dataset. These results underscore the potential of integrating CNNs with LSTMs to improve predictive maintenance outcomes, thereby reducing maintenance frequency and associated costs while enhancing machine and plant availability. This research opens up exciting possibilities for a more efficient and cost-effective future in the manufacturing sector, offering a promising outlook.This paper's contributions to the academic and practical domains are twofold: It not only illustrates the effective application of machine learning in predictive maintenance, a topic of immediate relevance, but also offers a viable approach to cost reduction and efficiency improvement in manufacturing operations. These practical implications highlight the immediate benefits that can be derived from our research, making it highly applicable in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: A Smart Wheelchair Supple Control System Based on Hall Rocker
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Aiming at the current smart wheelchair that still has room for improvement in terms of supple control and safe driving and needs further optimization to enhance its performance, a supple control system for smart wheelchair based on Hall rocker is proposed.The control system uses a fitted elliptic model to optimize the position data of the Hall rocker to achieve precise control of the smart wheelchair. For different traveling directions and turning situations, different speed processing strategies are used to ensure that the user can reach the maximum speed when traveling straight forward and adjust the speed accordingly to the size of the turning angle. In order to achieve precise motor speed control and maintain its operation in a stable state, a closed-loop control system is adopted. Specifically, an incremental PID (Proportional-Integral-Differential) control algorithm is used to adjust the motor speed in real time. This smart wheelchair safety control system provides an effective solution for the current smart wheelchair in terms of supple control and safe driving, which has potential application prospects.

articleTitle: Design of a magnetic hemispherical wheeled pipeline robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The paper designed a wheeled pipeline robot with a magnetic hemispherical wheel for pipeline with various curvatures. The magnetic hemispherical wheel can adapt to pipes with different curvatures. By changing the direction of the magnetic hemispherical wheel’s spherical surface, the robot can crawl inside or outside the pipe. Two different magnet holders suitable for the hemispherical wheel were designed. Parametric simulations were conducted to analyze the magnetic force magnitude at different angles of the magnet holder. The pitch angle of the swing arms of the robot was analyzed when turning angles changed. Finally, a prototype was built, and motion performance tests were conducted to show its performance.

articleTitle: A Novel Force/Position Control for the Flexible Lower Limb Exoskeleton with Hybrid Actuators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Lower limb exoskeletons can assist or augment human performances for various applications. Flexible lower limb exoskeletons have gained attention due to their light weight, comfortable wearability and other advantages. This paper presents a hybrid active-passive drive flexible lower limb exoskeleton to minimize energy consumption for human walking with the same external energy input. A novel force/position control for hip assistance is proposed with the exoskeleton. The controller accurately tracks and adjusts the actuator profiles in real time to achieve precise assistance to the wearer. The exoskeleton integrates IMUs and load cells to detect the wearer’s states. This paper models the human and exoskeleton coupled to generate the actuator profiles corresponding to the hip assistance force required during walking. Three individuals walk on a treadmill at a speed of 1.25 m/s to evaluate the controller’s performance. The results show that the average transmission force starts simultaneously with the peak angle of hip flexion, and the peak force error is within 5.25% for the given actuator profiles, indicating that the controller can effectively assist the wearer with the exoskeleton.

articleTitle: Forward Kinematics Analysis of 6-PUS Parallel Mechanism based on Optimized BP-NR Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This paper analyzes in detail the forward kinematics of 6-PUS parallel mechanism using MATLAB , SolidWorks and Adams software. The proposed algorithm combines the BP Neural Network with the Newton-Raphson method to form BP-NR algorithm. The BP neural network computes an approximation of the kinematic forward solution of the mechanism, which is used as the initial value of Newton-Raphson method for iterative computation to obtain the exact solution. Simulation verification shows that the BP-NR algorithm can simultaneously achieve high accuracy and real-time performance.

articleTitle: Rolling bearings fault diagnosis method based on NRBO-SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: A fault diagnosis model is proposed for the analysis of rolling bearing vibration signals, aimed at overcoming challenges related to fault identification and low classification accuracy. The model leverages a Newton-Raphson-based optimizer (NRBO) to optimize the parameters of the Support Vector Machine (SVM). By integrating the NRBO algorithm into the optimization process of SVM parameters, an NRBO-SVM fault classification model is constructed, enhancing the adaptive capability and classification accuracy of SVM. This model processes fault features for both fault identification and classification purposes. Notably, experimental results demonstrate that the NRBO-SVM algorithm achieves a satisfactory classification performance, outperforming traditional SVM algorithms in terms of classification accuracy.

articleTitle: IDD-YOLOv5: A Lightweight Insulator Defect Real-time Detection Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In order to achieve real-time detection of insulator defects in transmission lines, this paper proposes an improved insulator defect detection algorithm based on the YOLOv5s model, named IDD-YOLOv5. Firstly, to enhance the detection speed and reduce the model size, we introduce the GhostConv module and C3Ghost module into the backbone network. Secondly, the neck network employs a combination of C3Ghost and GSConv to further reduce the model’s parameter count, combined with the adaptive upsampling operator CARAFE to improve model accuracy. Finally, we adopt the EIOU loss function to accelerate model convergence and enhance detection precision. Experimental results show that IDD-YOLOv5 improves the mAP@0.5 by 2.5% over the original YOLOv5s, with accuracy and recall also increasing by 1.9% and 2.5%, respectively, while reducing parameters by 45.54%. Therefore, this improved model can rapidly and accurately detect insulator defects, aiding in the stable operation of electrical equipment. The related code, dataset, and model can be accessed through the following link: https://github.com/LuYang-2023/ICMA2024.git.

articleTitle: Application of artificial intelligence in magnetic performance prediction of sintered Nd-Fe-B magnets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This study aims to accurately predict the magnetic properties of sintered NdFeB magnets using artificial intelligence technology. Specifically, a BP neural network was adopted to build a prediction model. In the process of model construction, we specifically considered the complexity of sintered NdFeB magnet compositions and the influence of processing on the residual magnetization (Br) and coercivity (Hcj) magnetic properties. Therefore, we selected element compositions and processing parameters as feature variables. Through optimization of model hyperparameters, we successfully obtained a BP neural network prediction model with high prediction accuracy. The research results demonstrate that the proposed prediction model can effectively predict the magnetic properties of sintered NdFeB magnets, providing important guidance for process optimization and magnet composition design.

articleTitle: Motion Control of A Noval Bipedal Wheeled Robot:VC-I
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Although the integration of wheeled and legged functionalities in robot designs, known as wheel-legged systems, enables operation across diverse environments, the demand for handling increasingly complex tasks necessitates wheel-leg systems equipped with a broader array of movement capabilities. In this paper, we have developed and implemented a motion control system on a novel tandem bipedal wheeled robot named VC-I. Within this system, addressing the robot’s inherent static instability and the dynamic characteristics of its model, we have adopted the State-Dependent Riccati Equation (SDRE) method as the robot’s balance controller. Additionally, tailored to meet the demands of specific tasks, we have designed controllers that manage a range of functions, including attitude angle and jumping capabilities, thereby enhancing the robot’s operational versatility and effectiveness in varied environments. In conclusion, the effectiveness of the designed control system was validated through a comprehensive series of simulations and real-world experiments, confirming its viability and performance.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Modular Flapping Wing Robot with a Swappable Powertrain Module
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Flapping-wing robots (FWR) have domain-specific applications, where the lack of a fast-rotating propeller makes them safer when operating in complex environments with human proximity. However, most existing research in flapping-wing robots focuses on improving range/endurance or increasing payload capacity. This paper proposes a modular powertrain-based flapping-wing robot as a versatile solution to a mission-specific priority switch between payload or range for the same FWR. As the flapping frequency and stroke amplitude directly influence the flight characteristics of the FWR, we exploit this relation when designing our swappable powertrain with different motor-gearbox combinations and 4-bar crank lengths to obtain the desired frequency and amplitude. We calculate initial estimates for default configuration and simulate it using pterasoftware. We then fabricate two powertrain modules - a default configuration with a higher flapping frequency for payload purposes and an extended-range configuration with a tandem propeller for higher flight velocity for longer range and endurance. To verify the results, we compare the flight test data of both power train configurations using the same FWR platform.Video-https://youtu.be/vqJ58n77Bsc

articleTitle: Kinematic Simulation of Serpentine Soft Robotic Arm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In order to meet the demands of complex spatial environments, a novel design of a linear-driven continuous-type robotic arm was proposed. Based on geometric analysis, a simple modeling approach for the linear-driven continuous-type robotic arm was proposed, analyzing the kinematic mapping relationships among joint units, actuation units, and operational units. Additionally, a decoupled kinematic algorithm for flexible joints was provided. The motion model of the robotic arm was established using an improved Denavit-Hartenberg (D-H) parameter method, and a motion simulation model of the robotic arm was constructed using Matlab. The snake-like soft robotic arm could accomplish the expected motion trajectory. Therefore, in this paper, we modeled and decoupled the soft body robotic arm by using the improved D-H parametric method. This method can simplify the modeling process compared with the traditional D-H parametric method and is more suitable for flexible structure robots. The kinematic solution and control process of the snake-shaped flexible robotic arm is more stable and reliable, which lays the foundation for further investigation of the motion control and practical application of the robotic arm.

articleTitle: Position Sensorless Control of PMSM Based on EKF Current Noise Compensation and MRAS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: A position sensorless PMSM control method based on model reference adaptation system (MRAS) and current noise compensation is proposed in this paper. Firstly, a rotor speed and position estimation method based on MRAS and proportional-integrated (PI) adaptive control is designed. Then, in order to solve the problem that PMSM control performance is easily affected by current loop noise, a compensation approach based on extended Kalman filter (EKF) is developed. The sensorless control method based on MRAS and EKF current noise compensation proposed in this paper can accurately estimate the motor speed and position, and significantly eliminate the negative effect of current loop noise. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through simulations under different speeds and external loads.

articleTitle: FGNet: Faster Robotic Grasp Detection Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In unstructured environments, achieving fast and accurate object detection and successful grasping presents a significant challenge. Current grasping detection networks primarily focus on reducing the network's floating point operations (FLOPs) to improve network speed. However, we found that the effectiveness of this method is not particularly significant. To address this issue, we employed partial convolution (PConv) in place of regular convolutions to significantly enhance the network's detection speed. Additionally, we implemented a parallel structure for the network to fuse low-level and high-level features, reducing the loss of detail information during the decoding process. Our proposed faster grasp detection network (FGNet) achieved a performance of 96.74% (ow) and 98.66% (iw) on the Cornell dataset, with a detection speed of only 11ms. The grasping success rate was 96.5% in single-object scenarios and 92% in cluttered grasping scenarios.

articleTitle: A High-sensitivity Three-Dimensional Force Sensing Sensor for Minimally Invasive Cardiac Ablation Surgery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This paper introduces a high-sensitivity distal three-dimensional force sensor designed for cardiac ablation surgery. The sensor combines a force-sensitive structure with fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs) for the measurement of triaxial forces. At the tip of the sensor, an elastic flexure structure is designed, with four pairs of symmetrically arranged U-shaped slots for axial force perception and a modified I-beam structure for lateral force measurement. Five FBG elements are embedded into the elastic flexure structure, with each FBG placed in a tightly suspended manner and fixed at both ends using an adhesive to detect micro-strain and ensure sensitivity. The theoretical force-strain relationship is derived, and decoupling methods are provided. Simulation experiments based on finite element modeling are conducted for static calibration analysis. Simulation results indicate that under axial forces ranging from 0 to 2N, the axial force resolution is 4.46mN, and under lateral forces ranging from -1 to 1N, the lateral force resolutions in the two directions are 0.294mN and 0.293mN, respectively. These findings demonstrate that the sensor exhibits high sensitivity, validating the effectiveness of the design.

articleTitle: Optimal Dimensional Design of Parallel Mechanical Leg
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In order to expand the configuration of the leg mechanism of a legged robot, a Parallel Mechanical Leg (PML) with two rotational and three translational degrees of freedom (DOF) is proposed, and the structural parameters are optimized and designed based on the dexterity of the mechanism. Firstly, the mechanism configuration of the 5 DOF PML is described and its degrees of freedom are analyzed; secondly, the velocity, workspace, and Jacobi matrix of the mechanism are analyzed; finally, the inverse of the Jacobi matrix condition number is used as the index of dexterity, and the structural parameters are optimized by using the limited normalization method and the ternary plot.

articleTitle: Study on the Backstepping Sliding Mode-Based Tracking Control Method for the SUR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: To improve autonomous and tracking capabilities when the spherical underwater robot (SUR) performs complex tasks such as inspection, patrol and aquaculture, etc. This paper presented a path tracking method rooted in backstepping sliding mode control (BSMC) for the SUR. Through the derivation of the robot’s kinematic and dynamic models, a novel control scheme for the SUR was developed. Then, the Lyapunov function was applied to enhance the stability and robustness of the BSMC in unknown environments. Ultimately, this paper utilized Matlab to carry out the path tracking simulation of the SUR, thereby validating the effectiveness of the proposed method. The experimental results demonstrated that the proposed BSMC method boosted the SUR’s path tracking capabilities and met the task’s requirements.

articleTitle: Research on a Novel Hand Exoskeleton Rehabilitation Training System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Stroke is one of the common causes of the limb dysfunction, particularly in the elderly. Hand dysfunction severely affects patients' daily activities, so making the recovery of hand function is crucial for improving their quality of life. This study aims to develop an hand exoskeleton based on the underactuated technology to assist in the hand rehabilitation training of stroke patients. A novel underactuated hand exoskeleton is designed by using push-rod motors and 3D-printed gear-rack transmission mechanisms. The exoskeleton can simulate the natural movement of the patients' fingers, simplifying the control system by reducing the number of actuating components, while enhancing the portability and adaptability of the hole system. The 3D model and motion analysis of the hand exoskeleton are established in SolidWorks to verify its kinematics characteristics. At the same time, ensure that it meets the needs of rehabilitation training. The prototype consists of the actuation module, the main control module, and the human-computer interaction module, pressure and bending sensors. These sensors can monitor and provide the feedback on the force and joint angles during training in real-time. Additionally, a human-computer interaction interface based on Bluetooth communication allows patients and therapists to conveniently control and monitor the system status. Experimental results indicate that the hand exoskeleton system can effectively assist patients in rehabilitation training, meeting the requirements for joint degrees of freedom and range of motion. The system's actuating force is sufficient to support the correction of hand joint movements. The hand exoskeleton developed in this study shows great potential in rehabilitation training, not only improving rehabilitation efficiency but also reducing the workload of therapists, providing more personalized and precise rehabilitation services for stroke patients.

articleTitle: Combined Rigid-Flexible Weight-Bearing Exoskeleton
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Most of the research on rigid exoskeletons has focused on how to further improve the efficiency of the exoskeleton to further reduce the wearer's energy consumption, neglecting the wearer's experience. In this paper, we introduce a rigid-flexible exoskeleton based on active-passive control strategy. By switching the control strategy of the exoskeleton at different stages of the gait cycle, the suppleness of the exoskeleton's interaction with the wearer is improved. In addition, an experiment involving three testers validated the effectiveness of the presented rigid-flexible weight-bearing exoskeleton. The results of the experiment showed that the exoskeleton was able to reduce the wearer's metabolic expenditure by 13.1% when exercising with a weight of 30kg.

articleTitle: Research on the performance of distance measurement system based on binocular vision
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Binocular vision is an important technique in 3D (three-dimensional) reconstruction. Two images captured by binocular camera are used to reconstruct 3D information according to the geometric relationship and optical imaging parameters of binocular camera. In binocular vision system, the focal length, base distance and measuring object distance are mutually restricted, and the measurement accuracy is different under different parameter configurations. In this paper, the parameter selection and measurement performance of binocular vision system are studied. A laser scanning binocular vision measuring device is constructed, and the binocular matching speed is accelerated by actively projecting laser line to the measured object. By extracting the center bright line of the laser bright line fringe in the image for stereo matching, parallax is obtained to calculate the distance of the object. By adjusting the system structure parameters, the influence of the system structure parameters on the ranging performance is analyzed and studied. In this paper, combining experimental analysis with theoretical analysis, the parameter setting conditions of binocular vision system high precision measurement are proposed. It helps to improve the performance of the ranging system by rationally designing the parameters of the binocular ranging system.

articleTitle: Active Disturbance Rejection Control of Microgrid DC-DC Converter Based on AC Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: As an important part of the new power system, the stable operation of microgrid is very important for energy management and power supply reliability. As a key energy conversion device in microgrid, the stability and anti-disturbance ability of DC-DC converter directly affect the performance of the whole system. In order to solve the problem that some complex dynamic characteristics in DC microgrid affect the control effect of DC-DC converter and then affect the power quality of the whole system. In this paper, an ADRC strategy based on Actor-Critic (AC) algorithm is proposed. The self-tuning of LADRC parameters is realized by using the advantage of AC algorithm, and then the accurate control of DC-DC converter is realized. Secondly, the dynamic response characteristics and stability of the system under different control strategies are compared by simulation.

articleTitle: An Improved Small Feature Segmentation Algorithm Based on U-Net Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The segmentation network of small features can be used in the medical field, such as the segmentation of retinal blood vessels, which can help doctors diagnose eye related diseases. However, the current retinal vessel segmentation methods still lack the ability to segment microvessels. In this article, we propose an improved small feature segmentation algorithm for retinal vessel segmentation. Based on the U-Net algorithm, improvements are made to address the characteristics of free flow and rich morphology of retinal blood vessels. Based on a multi-scale dilated convolution module, multi-scale information of retinal blood vessels under different receptive fields is aggregated to enhance microvascular feature extraction. Experiments were conducted on a mixed public dataset. The results showed that our method can accurately identify and segment retinal microvessels, with better segmentation performance. What’s more, the proposed model can also be applied to small feature segmentation in industrial fields, such as crack detection of large-size ultra-thin photovoltaic silicon wafers.

articleTitle: Performance-optimized Multiplex Detection Sensor for Coagulation Indicators in Whole Blood
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This research presents a highly sensitive folded dual-path coagulation sensor design method for convenient heparin detection. The sensor fabrication process involves the utilization of graphene (GR) due to its exceptional physical and chemical properties, especially its outstanding electrical conductivity crucial for electrochemical sensor development. The electrodes are fabricated through a double-sided process on polyethylene terephthalate (PET) substrate using automatic screen printing. Modification of the biosensor involves specific procedures detailed in the paper. This sensor fabrication method provides a new approach for multiplex detection in the field of biomedical engineering, enhancing the sensitivity, accuracy, and range of heparin detection in biochips.

articleTitle: Study on an Adaptive Clamping Device for Passive Safety Delivery of Vascular Intervention Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In practical clinical applications, vascular intervention surgical robots have developed sophisticated human-machine interaction systems, enabling assistance to physicians in performing remote surgeries and providing intelligent visual feedback. However, regarding surgical safety, current research predominantly focuses on force feedback and robot control logic, with clamping mechanisms targeting the locking of catheters and guide wires. Excessive clamping force may lead to surface damage to intervention instruments, while insufficient force delivery may result from slippery surfaces. Therefore, addressing these issues, this study proposed a passive, compliant safety strategy for an adaptive clamping device based on a vascular intervention surgical robot platform. This device can accommodate different diameter catheters and maintain a constant delivery force during the intervention process. Finally, through experimentation, the effectiveness, safety, and stability of the device were demonstrated.

articleTitle: Generating PET images from low-dose data using a cycle PET reconstruction convolutional neural network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: A high-quality PET image usually requires the injection of a sufficient amount of radiotracer, which increases the risk of radiation exposure to the examinee and medical staff. Therefore, performing PET scanning with a reduced injection dose has broad application in clinical practice. However, low-dose PET data can cause problems in the reconstruction process, such as increased noise and degraded image quality. To address these issues, we adopt the idea of a back-projection filter (BPF) based on deep learning methods to reconstruct images. First, the raw data is back-projected (BP) to generate a low-dose BP (LDBP) image, as the PET sinogram is quite large. Second, a cycle PET reconstruction convolutional neural network (CPR-CNN) is introduced to realize a reconstruction process from a LDBP image to a deep learning-based full-dose PET (DL-FDPET) image. CPR-CNN employs two reconstruction models to separately learn bidirectional mappings between pairs of input images to enhance the image reconstruction performance. Our proposed CPR-CNN achieves comparable results in maintaining resolution and denoising of DL-FDPET images.

articleTitle: Research on key techniques of path planning for Pinecone picking robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Pine tower picking robot is a modern agricultural machinery equipment, its main function is realized pick the pine tower automatically on the pine tree. This robot is generally composed of mechanical arm, grasping device, visual recognition system, control system and other parts, through the telescopic robot arm and grasping device cooperation, can accurately grasp and pick the pine tower.

articleTitle: Design of a Needle Guidance Based a Variable Stiffness Continuum Manipulator for Brain Surgery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Owing to their continuously bending backbone, continuum robots are able to perform dexterous movements and accurate manipulation, allowing them suited for unstructured environments such as surgical applications. However, controlling their stiffness and payload capability are still challenging. This paper presents a novel design of continuum robot for needle guidance in brain surgery. The design composes of a series-connected rigid spherical joints, and a central cable acting as a backbone to adjust stiffness of the robot. Additionally, this cable offers a mechanical lock to precisely reach the target pose for the needle during Intracerebral Hemorrhage (ICH) evacuation surgery. A design studies are conducted by optimizing certain parameters to evaluate the performance of the robot in terms of variable stiffness and locking. The design analysis is performed, while respecting the constraints of stress and deflection. On the other hand, a friction analysis based on contact point estimation approach is derived to ensure the configuration lock. The performance of the proposed design is evaluated by using Multibody Dynamics software. Moreover, experimental validation of the robot is carried out to verify its variable stiffness and payload capacity. The results demonstrate that the continuum robot has an acceptable load-carrying capacity and displacement deflection error. The displacement deflection error range from 0.78 mm to 0.48 mm at payload of 500 gm and tension force range from 350 N to 800 N.

articleTitle: Structural Design and Simulation of a Bionic Sea Turtle Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This article introduces the challenges in maintaining ocean photovoltaic platforms and proposes a solution: using a bionic robot with the shape of a sea turtle to address the issue of ocean current fluctuations during the maintenance of ocean photovoltaic platforms. This method, through bionic design and optimization of structural parameters, achieves a more stable and energy-efficient movement of the robot in the marine environment, thereby improving the operational efficiency of ocean photovoltaic platforms and reducing energy consumption. The article also presents the kinematic and dynamic models of the robot, and conducts fluid simulation experiments and thrust simulation experiments. The innovation of this article lies in the application of bionic design to marine engineering. Through simulated comparisons of different flipper-shaped structures and thrust experiments, optimal structural model parameters are obtained. The experimental results validate the stability and effectiveness of the robot's movement, providing broad prospects for its application in areas such as marine platform maintenance and underwater pipeline inspection.

articleTitle: Multimodal Iontronic Tactile Sensor with Intelligent Decoupling Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The iontronic tactile sensor is a promising device for the robot to perceive temperature and pressure information. However, there was no suitable method to decouple the multimodal information from readout signals, due to complicated impedance response features. Hence, we fabricated a film as a sensing layer to make a tactile sensor. Then, the impedance response features, stimulated by temperature and pressure, were analyzed. After that, a machine learning method was used to decouple the readout signals, where three neural networks were compared. Furthermore, we conducted a primitive hot water weighting experiment to demonstrate the decoupling performance. This study provided a method to get temperature and pressure information from a single iontronic sensing layer, which has potential benefits in various scenarios such as human-robot interaction and health care.

articleTitle: DADETR: Feature Alignment-based Domain Adaptation for Ship Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Ship target detection technology is crucial for ship intelligence, maritime security, and military applications. Deep neural networks, trained with high-quality data, have shown impressive results in this field. However, due to the biased distribution of datasets, the data used to train the model often cannot fully reflect the various complex situations in real-world applications. if models trained on specific datasets are directly applied to target datasets with different distributions, the detection performance of the models will be greatly reduced. To address these issues, we propose a domain adaptation algorithm consisting of an image-level domain adaptation module and an instance-level domain adaptation module. In the image-level domain adaptation module, domain query vectors are utilized to aggregate global context information from source and target domain, facilitating image-level feature alignment. Meanwhile, in the instance-level domain adaptation module, the alignment of token features output by the encoder and decoder enables local and instance-level feature alignment. Results on four representative datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in weather adaptation and synthetic-to-real data adaptation scenarios.

articleTitle: Data Augmentation for Continuous Excavation Trajectories Based on DGAN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Artificial intelligence technology represented by machine learning is shining brightly in the industrial field. A key challenge for excavator automation in the construction industry is the lack of high-quality open source continuous excavation datasets. We use an advanced generative adversarial network called DopplerGANer to enhance real-world continuous excavation trajectories. This results in a synthetic yet realistic dataset for model training. Our analysis involves the use of statistical techniques to verify the similarity and diversity of the synthetic data to the original data. In addition, we use standard operating evaluation metrics to evaluate real trajectories and synthetic trajectories in a simulation environment. The results show that the synthetic trajectories not only closely mimic the original data but also provide an improved range of variation. This research lays a solid foundation for the development of reinforcement learning applications in future excavator automation.

articleTitle: Chebyshev Polynomials Expanded Adaptive Control Strategy for Real-time Force Tracking of Electro-hydraulic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Real-time force tracking control of electrohydraulic systems is extensively utilized in industry for various application purposes. To improve the real-time force tracking accuracy of electro-hydraulic systems, a Chebyshev polynomial extended adaptive control strategy consisting of a feedforward inverse model controller and a Chebyshev polynomial extended adaptive filter is proposed. By utilizing the acquired inverse model of the PI controlled electro-hydraulic system, a feedforward inverse model controller is formulated, where the inverse model is obtained via zero magnitude error tracking technology on the basis of system model identified by system identification technology. A Chebyshev polynomials expanded adaptive filter is further incorporated into the previously mentioned feedforward inverse model controller to form the proposed adaptive control strategy. Comparative experiments are conducted on an electro-hydraulic system, and the effectiveness of the proposed adaptive control strategy is shown by the experimental results.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Velocity of Two-Layer Generalized Parallel Manipulators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for analyzing the input-output velocity equations of two-layer generalized parallel manipulators that have interconnected coupling sub-chains. These manipulators have velocity equations that are influenced by additional coupling sub-chains. For planar generalized parallel manipulators, constraint equations and loop closure are used to derive velocity matrices. Velocity matrices for spatial mechanisms, including spherical mechanisms, are derived from velocity loop equations. Using screw theory, the velocities of passive joints are eliminated to obtain the overall velocity matrix of inputs and outputs. For planar mechanisms, iterative Jacobian calculations are conducted, while constraint wrenches are modified for spatial mechanisms during Jacobian matrix derivation. Finally, the velocities of a series of generalized parallel manipulators are enumerated to demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this proposed approach.

articleTitle: Chipless RFID Sensors for Crack Angle and Direction Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: A novel sensor design for chipless RFID is proposed to detect the width and direction of metal cracks. The sensor is a circular microstrip patch antenna and a multi-arc patch antenna structure. The operating frequency band of the sensor is 2.5~4.5 GHz. 5 resonant frequencies are generated in the resulting RCS spectrum through simulation experiments, and the first four resonant frequencies are encoded and designed. The metal crack direction and width are judged by the frequency offset degree and coding information, which can realize the detection of 0°, 40°, 90°, 120° and 150° cracks. The sensitivity is up to 196.6 MHz/mm.The proposed sensor adopts passive design with low cost and has good application prospect.

articleTitle: Parameter optimization of pulse generator based on genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Pulse generation devices play an important role in hydraulic components, pipeline reliability testing, and other aspects. Among them, the pulse generation device with open-loop control has a simple structure, high reliability, and broad application prospects. In the conventional hydraulic system design process, pressure, flow rate, and power matching methods are often used for parameter design. It is difficult to accurately match the performance and energy consumption goals of the pulse generation device during the design process, which can easily cause significant energy loss or pulse waveform not meeting testing requirements. This study uses genetic algorithm to optimize and match the key parameters in the pulse generation device with small pulse error band range and low system energy consumption as optimization objectives. Using AMESim software to simulate and compare the optimized parameter neighborhood, the results show that the parameter design is effective and reasonable, with an error controlled within 4.9% compared to the standard waveform. The system energy consumption is not higher than 0.25kW in the 10mm diameter pipeline test.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Bionic Amphibious Mother and Child Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In recent years, bionic amphibious robot technology has emerged in the fields of underwater exploration, marine resource development, and emergency rescue. To address the complexity of tasks in these domains, a mother-child robot system is introduced. In this paper, the structural composition of the mother and child robot is described in detail, including the functions of each component between them. Additionally, the forward kinematic model of the mother robot is established. Finally, the propulsion mechanism of the mother robot is analyzed by fluid simulation. The results show that the speed and stability of the mother robot are significantly affected by using different water jetting methods: higher speeds and enhanced stability are achieved with backward and downward water jet propulsion, while oblique downward 45° water jet exhibits efficient thrust generation. In the context of the child robot, the high vorticity generated by the propeller affects the robot's stability, requiring complex control to continuously adjust posture and speed to maintain stability.

articleTitle: The Design and Research of Resistance Instrument in Ship Towing Test
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Based on the requirements of ship resistance towing test, a strain gauge type of resistance instrument has been designed, which consisting of the frame, towing component, course component, measuring component, etc. The towing component is responsible for the towing movement of the ship model, and the course component is responsible for constructing different course angles in the test requirements. An automatic brake mechanism has been equipped in measuring component, which can ensure the stability and accuracy of the tension sensor in towing test. The strength limit on the key components of the resistance instrument has been calculated by finite element analysis software, the optimization has been used in vulnerable components, and the instrument strength and reliability has been insured in the test.

articleTitle: Diagnosis and Causal Analysis of Depression Based on EEG Features and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Depression is a serious mental illness that imposes a substantial burden on both individuals and society. There is a growing interest in employing learning-based methods utilizing bio-signals for the autonomic diagnosis of depression. However, the extent of bio-signal features' contributions in these models and the causal relationships among them remain underexplored. This study developed machine learning models for depression diagnosis utilizing electroencephalogram (EEG) data, with a focus on estimating the contributions of EEG features, including alpha interhemispheric asymmetry, activity, and mobility, within the learning-based frameworks. Additionally, the causal relationships among the most representative features were discussed. The experimental results showed that XGBoost had the best performance with the highest prediction accuracy among three learning-based models. Experimental findings also revealed that the interhemispheric asymmetry features provided the larger contributions in diagnosis of depression, than the features of activity and mobility. With three different causality analyses methods, the study identifies stable and tight causal relationships between the prefrontal and parietal asymmetry, and the depression. These findings provide a new perspective and basis for the efficient and reliable diagnosis of depression, which is helpful to improve the accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: The Research of Intelligent Unmanned Mooring Device for Smart Port
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The intelligent unmanned mooring device adopts a multi-link mechanism and vacuum adsorption design, which can perform heave, surge, and sway actions to adapt to the mooring postures of different ships. The use of flow control valves and accumulators in hydraulic circuits can achieve appropriate dynamic response and oscillation reducing effects on ship oscillation without manual intervention and power consumption. By using multiple sets of distance sensors to detect the position and angle of the ship, and controlling the extension and rotation of multiple sets of mooring devices in parallel mode, the ship’s position can be autonomously and intelligently aligned during mooring. It is an intelligent, environmentally friendly, safe, and efficient mooring device suitable for use in smart ports.

articleTitle: Research on Autonomous Navigation System of Agricultural Quadruped Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The SLAM is the key technology in the field of robotics, it can use lidar to scan the environment and extract feature points, realize the autonomous positioning and map building robot. In recent years, with the continuous development of robotics and lidar technology, laser SLAM has been widely studied and applied. This paper mainly from the quadruped robot path planning, environment perception, positioning and navigation and other key issues are deeply studied and discussed. First of all, the application field and basic principle of agricultural quadruped robot based on SLAM technology are analyzed and studied. Then, the main algorithm function and system implementation of agricultural quadruped robot based on SLAM technology are analyzed in detail. Finally, a more reasonable design algorithm of autonomous navigation system of quadruped robot is proposed, and the algorithm is applied to the robot for testing. After testing, the function of autonomous navigation system of quadruped robot meets the design requirements.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Prefabricated Deformation on Sealing Performance Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This study establishes a thermal-mechanical coupling model for marine stern shaft mechanical seals and proposes a micro-nano treatment strategy for static and dynamic rings to reduce deformation and enhance sealing performance. By developing a thermal-mechanical coupling analysis model under operational conditions, we determined the steady-state clearance of the seal. Based on the clearance, a pre-taper treatment was applied to the contact surfaces of the rings, achieving more uniform deformation, lower end face temperatures, and balanced pressure distribution under the same conditions. These optimizations significantly improved sealing efficiency across various operational conditions while maintaining adaptability to sudden changes. This research provides valuable insights for optimizing pre-deformation strategies to enhance sealing performance in similar applications.

articleTitle: Deformation of Regular Prismatic Tensegrity Structures under Pressure by The Analytical Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The tensegrity structure is a stable self-equilibrium system composed of continuous tension members and discrete compression members. Because of its light and simple characteristics, tensegrity structure has attracted wide attention. In this paper, an analytical method to study the deformation of regular prismatic tensegrity structures under pressure is proposed. The geometry length of all elements in the self-equilibrium state can be obtained by structural parameters. Assigning the bar's force density, the force density of all components can be obtained according to the force density relationship, and the prestress and natural length of members can also be calculated. The internal forces of the members are redistributed after applying an axial external load, and the shape -changed structural parameters can be obtained by solving the nonlinear force density equation. The proposed method only needs to solve the three variables of height, radius and torsion angle of the prismatic unit, which greatly reduces the calculation amount. This method can quickly calculate the accurate solution of the shape-changed structural parameters and is effective for analyzing regular prismatic tensegrity under an axial loading.

articleTitle: A Novel Fall Detection Methodology Based on Feedback-Fusion and Optimal-Allocation Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In order to offer timely rescue measures for elderly and reduce secondary hurt caused by fall, a novel fall detection methodology based on Feedback-Fusion and Optimal-Allocation (FF-OA) model is proposed. First, K-Means++ algorithm is shaped to re-cluster the anchor to increase detection precision, because the initial anchor is unsuitable for all fall detection dataset. Second, Feedback-Fusion model is used to add a feedback to the Third Stage in Cross-Stage Partial Network (C3) to form the C3-F model, and its feature information is sent back for further fusion processing after each bottleneck stack, which solves the problem small feature of the dataset is ignored in training to cause that targets cannot be identified precisely. Third, Optimal-Allocation model is used to eliminate the detection errors of fuzzy labels caused by anchors overlap in the process of target detection. Minimum loss function is applied to select the optimal anchor for input image to detect fall correctly. Then, hardware platform is designed and implemented to collect the pictures and videos to test detection performance of the model. After being trained and tested, precision and recall of the novel methodology are increased by 2.88% and 2.38% respectively, and mAP@0.5 is increased by 1.42%. Besides, its detection precision is increased to 83.15% and its confidence is increased above about 85%. This methodology is able to provide timely assistance for the elderly, and effectively reduces the risk of dangerous situations caused by the fall, which obviously improves their safety and quality of life.

articleTitle: Train Coupling Robot Based on Extended Implicit Self-Correction Generalized Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: We propose A controller based on generalized predictive control is used to control the robot, so as to realize the precise tracking and control of the motion trajectory of the unhooked robot. As a nonlinear walking mechanism, the train coupler robot must ensure that it can accurately catch up with the coupler to be picked up and move in sync with the coupler after catching up. Therefore, a trajectory tracking control algorithm must be designed to control the actual operation process based on the given ideal displacement curve to ensure that the robot can operate safely and stably. Generalized predictive control has the advantages of solid robustness, broad applicability, simple parameter adjustment, strong predictive ability, and fast response speed. The Elman neural network is a dynamic feedback-type recursive neural network that combines local memory units with local feedback links, with good adaptive, self-organizing, intense learning, fault-tolerant, and anti-interference capabilities. In addressing the modeling difficulties caused by the nonlinear characteristics of the train coupler robot, a generalized predictive control algorithm is adopted for tracking control. The use of the Elman neural networks helps to address the problem of modeling nonlinear systems. Specific experimental data indicates that this algorithm can ensure the robot operates safely and smoothly, reaching the target position and velocity.

articleTitle: Health Management System for the Industrial Robot Control Cabinet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: To address the demand for higher reliability brought about by the comprehensive, integrated development, and normalized operation of robot systems, particularly focusing on the associated controllers, this study investigates the fault diagnosis and health assessment methods for typical coupled software and hardware systems. In response to the current issues such as insufficient monitoring parameters, low diagnostic accuracy, and lack of quantitative evaluation methods, we first outline the typical fault mode trees of coupled software and hardware systems. Then, by integrating information on the operational status of software and hardware, we design a two-step fault diagnosis algorithm based on prior knowledge to effectively reduce false alarms. Additionally, we establish multi-level health assessment parameters and models. Finally, we implement a health management system based on the above methods and deploy it on an industrial robot control cabinets, verifying the effectiveness of our design approach.

articleTitle: Ultrasound-Guided Localization System for Pericardial Effusion Puncture Robot Utilizing Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The precision of pericardial effusion puncture surgery is crucial for ensuring patient safety and enhancing surgical outcomes, yet traditional approaches rely heavily on the physician's experience. With the advancement of interdisciplinary medical fields, robots for pericardial effusion puncture surgery guided by ultrasound have shown great potential in improving surgical precision and safety. This paper introduces a dataset of ultrasound images of pericardial effusion, a deep classification network, and a semi-supervised residual network (SSRNet), along with a pericardial effusion localization system for ultrasound-guided puncture robots that integrates these two networks. The experimental results indicate that our proposed system achieves an accuracy of 0.992 in classifying segmentable types of pericardial effusion ultrasound images and a Dice coefficient of 0.9868 for semantic segmentation of pericardial effusion and the heart. The system, combining both models, also reached an accuracy of 97.5% in experiments. Therefore, this research not only provides precise localization for robotic pericardial effusion puncture surgery but also offers insights for future research in this field.

articleTitle: A wheelchair differential control method based on the coupling of control signal and environmental information
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: We propose a wheelchair differential speed control method based on the coupling of control signals and environmental information, which firstly determines the motion state of the wheelchair based on the displacement offset, so as to generate the corresponding control signals; then ultrasound, vision and IMU sensors are used to collect distance, image and angle information respectively, and the environmental information is fused based on fuzzy control to get the integrated environmental factor; Finally, the control signals and Integrated environmental factor are coupled to calculate the expected speeds of the left and right wheels under different motion states. The method fully reflects the environmental information and realizes the full coupling between the control signal and the environmental information, establishes the differential speed model of the wheelchair considering the environmental information, ensures the safety and reliability of the wheelchair during operation, and realizes the intelligent control of the wheelchair.

articleTitle: A distributed drive articulated robot control system based on steering control strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In order to improve the motion control characteristics of articulated rock-drilling robot, an articulated robot chassis structure with encoder expansion link and distributed electric wheel is designed, and a steering control strategy based on push rod pose feedback is proposed. Based on Adams/Simulink co-simulation, the steering control strategy model is built. The motion of the articulated rock drilling robot in various working conditions is analyzed by co-simulation experiment. Compared with the traditional control strategy, the steering time of the articulated rock-drilling robot by the steering control strategy is increased to 13.87%, and the steering distance is reduced to 16.95%, which effectively improves the steering ability of the robot.

articleTitle: A mortar scraping robot for a whole wall in construction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: One of the challenging research issues in building construction is using robot for reducing people's labor intensity. This paper develops a cement mortar scraping robot which can scrape a whole wall in one time without operator invention. In this paper, the mechanical and electrical structure of the robot is described, and the algorithm of the omnidirectional movement algorithm is given. The robot is tested in construction site, and the result shows that it can reduce people's labor intensity and improve work efficiency significantly.

articleTitle: Neural network-based compensation of End position and attitude error in digital twin model of industrial robots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This paper takes the IRB-120 robot manufactured by ABB as an example and focuses on how to solve the discrepancy between the digital twin model and the end position of existing industrial robots. In this paper, a digital twin model is established using theoretical parameters, and a PSO-RBF neural network is used to compensate the error between the digital twin model and the actual robot end position and orientation. The training of the neural network takes the joint angles obtained from the inverse solution of the theoretical kinematic model as the output data, and the theoretical joint angles obtained by the twin model through the fieldbus as the input data. This implements the training process of the neural network. The twin system predicts the theoretical joint angles of the robot in real time and uses these predicted angles to drive the virtual model to ensure that its final position is consistent with that of the actual robot. Experimental validation shows that this approach reduces the error between the end position of the twin model and the end position of the actual robot from 1.4573 mm to 0.0012 mm. In addition, the orientation RPY angles were corrected from 0.0037°, 0.0091° and 0.0032° to 0.0006.

articleTitle: A Snake-Inspired Collision-Free Path Planning Algorithm and Experiments for Hyper-Redundant Manipulators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The detection of complex and confined spaces has always been a significant challenge in specialized operations and the industrial sector. Hyper-redundant Manipulators , with their high flexibility and high fault tolerance, hold promising application prospects in complex constrained spaces. However, the hyper-redundant structure poses substantial challenges to its inverse kinematics, making it difficult to achieve precise control and trajectory planning in restricted spaces. This paper presents a Self-motion Searching and Clawing (SSC) algorithm to fast plan the collision-free path for the hyper-redundant manipulators. First, The algorithmic strategy of SSC, inspired by the movement of snakes, is introduced, and a physical experimental system is constructed to verify its efficacy. Second, the gravity compensation function is implemented to ensure the control accuracy of the experimental system under the interference of gravity. Third, various experiments are conducted to verify and analyze the capability of exploring the complex environments. As a result, both the straight pipe and the narrow curved pipe are successfully explored to the target positions without collision.

Author Keywords: a Self-motion Searching and Clawing algorithm (SSC)

articleTitle: Predefined-time Fast Tracking Control for Hovercraft with Comprehensive Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In order to meet the rapid converge requirement when tracking the desired speed and heading, a predefined-time tracking control method for the hovercraft with system uncertainty is proposed. Firstly, considering the uncertainty of the parameters of the hovercraft model and the dynamic uncertainty caused by unknown disturbance, a dynamic mathematical model with uncertainty description is given. Secondly, super-twisting sliding mode observer is developed to estimate the comprehensive uncertainty in speed and heading channel. Finally, combining backstepping method and predefined-time stability theorem, predefined-time heading and speed controller are designed. The effectiveness and superiority of the method are verified by two digital simulation examples.

articleTitle: The Application of RFID Tags in Library
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The application of RFID in the library of Tianjin University of Technology has been introduced based on the basic principles of RFID technology, including book cataloguing, self-borrowing and returning books, book anti-theft, book inventory, book location, etc. The problems and solutions of RFID technology in library application are studied. This paper expounds the application status of RFID technology, and provides references for libraries which applying for RFID technology. Finally, the development direction of library automation technology is prospected.

articleTitle: Gait Trajectory Control Technology of The Lower Limb Exoskeleton Rehabilitation Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: To aid in the rehabilitation training of patients with severe lower limb movement disorders, a wearable lower limb exoskeleton rehabilitation robot system is proposed. Mechanical and dynamic models of the lower limb exoskeleton rehabilitation robot were established, and based on these models, a control system was designed. Dynamic compensation based on the exoskeleton model was introduced into the PID control loop, improving the traditional PD controller to a computed torque control (CTC) based PD controller. Through simulation and physical experiments, it was demonstrated that the designed controller exhibits good performance, enhancing the stability and robustness of the control system, meeting higher control precision requirements, and achieving more precise trajectory tracking control effect. The system can assist patients in passive training and promote the rehabilitation of lower limb motor function.

articleTitle: A novel passive lumbar exoskeleton that provides multiple traction forces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: A novel wearable passive exoskeleton mechanism is proposed and a prototype model is designed to address the problem of excessive spinal compression force that can easily result from the daily work activities of workers that require stooping. The exoskeleton utilizes the principle of leverage to provide two traction forces to reduce spinal compression force. Theoretical models of kinematics and statics were done and finite element simulation was utilized to depict the trend of the two traction forces provided by the exoskeleton. The biomechanical model of the human body was done to show the change of spinal compression force and joint torque under the double traction forces, and the results showed that there is a good reduction of spinal compression force and joint torque, and the exoskeleton has a spinal protection performance, which provides a novel idea for the future design of lumbar exoskeletons oriented to spinal protection.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of Suspension Structure through Vibration Equivalence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Given the challenges in controlling the large suspension structure during physical vibration tests due to its large mass, volume, and complex connection structure, we propose an experimental platform system using an equivalent mass block vibration load. This system treats the airborne cantilever structure as a combination of a spring damping system and an equivalent mass block. By dynamically modeling the cantilever structure under the influence of a head auxiliary support manipulator, we derive vibration response functions and control laws for suppressing vibrations at the suspension structure’s auxiliary support point. Building on this model, we establish a vibration load simulation platform by deriving an equivalent dynamic model and control law based on displacement similarities between the mass block and auxiliary support point. Through experiments involving vibration response and suppression control of the mass block, we validate the equivalence of our simulation system.

articleTitle: Reducing Physical Load for Desk-Height Tasks by Supporting Kneeling Posture with a Lower Limb Exoskeleton
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Performing manual tasks at desk height can cause musculoskeletal disorders, posing a significant burden on individuals worldwide. This study aims to propose an ergonomic solution by adopting a kneeling posture, which alleviates strain on the lower back. Additionally, it evaluates the effectiveness of an exoskeleton designed to support the lower limbs in maintaining this kneeling posture. A simple human model was created from motion capture data to simulate loads on the lower back in three postures: kneeling, sitting, and standing. The simulation findings suggest that a kneeling posture can reduce back strain when working at desk height. However, this posture may increase strain on the lower limbs. To address this issue, an exoskeleton designed to support the lower limbs in the kneeling posture is evaluated for its effectiveness in this study. This paper assesses the exoskeleton’s impact on static stability and muscle activity in the lower back. A comparison was also made between kneeling with the exoskeleton, standing, and sitting postures. Myoelectric sensors were used to monitor the muscle load on the lower back and lower extremities of six participants as they performed tasks in each posture. The results indicate reduced muscle activity, highlighting the potential effectiveness of using the kneeling posture with the exoskeleton for performing manual tasks at desk height.

articleTitle: Research on 2D Nesting Optimization Combining Improved no-fit polygon Method and Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This paper presents a two-dimensional nesting program that integrates an improved no-fit polygon method with an enhanced genetic algorithm, aimed at optimizing the arrangement of irregular convex polygons in sheet metal layout. The program leverages the global search capability of the genetic algorithm, iterating to enhance the nesting efficiency by encoding layout solutions and applying operations such as natural selection, crossover, and mutation. We introduced the concept of dynamic search spacing, allowing the algorithm to adjust the granularity of the search during iterations based on the number of iterations already performed, thereby accelerating convergence speed in the initial phase and enhancing the quality of solutions in the later phase. By employing the improved no-fit polygon method, the search range was narrowed. Through a series of benchmark tests, our algorithm demonstrated significant improvements in material utilization rates and maintained competitiveness in computational time. This study provides an efficient nesting strategy for sheet metal layout.

articleTitle: Jumping Locomotion of Quadruped Robot During Running Based on Multiple Model Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Continuous jumping motion is an indispensable part of the flexible movement of quadruped robot, and jumping is often an effective way to break through the dilemma when the robot crosses the complex rough or uneven road surface. In this paper, a quadruped robot control framework is proposed to continuously jump during running on a flat terrain. The framework switches motion modes by using a central Pattern generators (CPG)-based finite state machine(C-FSM). Multiple model fusion (MMF) method is used to realize bound gait movement of quadruped robot. The four legs of the robot are controlled by the CPG to generate periodic motion, the spring loaded inverted pendulum (SLIP) model is used to achieve flexible control and avoid disadvantages of position control. The foot force is calculated by offline optimization to control the robot jumping. In the simulation experiment, the robot can run with bound gait of 1.75m/s and the height of the center of mass (COM) reaches 1.22m, and can run continuously after landing.

articleTitle: Hybrid Control of 3D-Printed Multimodal Soft Pneumatic Actuators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Soft pneumatic actuators (SPAs) offer a promising alternative for biomedical applications requiring high sensitivity and precise manipulation due to their inherent compliance. 3-Dprinted multi-modal zig-zag SPAs exhibit potential in this area by achieving repeatable and precise shape changes due to their chambered design. However, achieving accurate position control remains a challenge. This work proposes a hybrid control strategy for multi-modal zig-zag SPAs that combines feed-forward and proportional-integral-derivative (PID) control to enhance positioning accuracy. A Pseudo Rigid Body (PRB) based inverse dynamic model is employed for the feed-forward component. The effectiveness of the controller is evaluated through extensive simulations and experiments. Results demonstrate that the hybrid control strategy achieves up to 29.5% and 31.6% improvement in accuracy compared to the PID and feed-forward controllers, respectively, within the operational bandwidth.

articleTitle: Levitation Control of Doubly-Fed Linear Motor with Multi-Phase AC Excitation on Mover
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Different from the Transrapid (TR) series maglev that achieves the levitation control with DC excited mover, the stable levitation control of doubly-fed linear motor (DFLM) with multi-phase AC excited mover is achieved in this paper. AC levitation, as opposed to DC levitation, exhibits similarities but possesses more uniqueness. In this paper, the principle of the inherent pitch torque of AC levitation is investigated and a feasible control method to compensate the pitch torque is proposed. The effectiveness of the proposed control method is validated through simulation studies.

articleTitle: Experimental Research on a Water-Jumping Robotic Dolphin Based on Modular Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Research on underwater bionic robotic fish is a major focus in the field of robotics. However, there is still a lack of research on the cross-media movement near the water surface of robotic fish. This paper conducts the experimental research of a water-jumping bionic robotic dolphin. Following the principle of modular design, the body structure of the robotic dolphin is designed from five parts: head, pitch, body, tail, and tail fin. Also, the robotic dolphin’s control system is designed, a hardware platform is built from the four modules of decision-making, communication, execution, and perception, and the propulsion algorithm is designed based on experimental requirements. Finally, an experimental platform is built and experimental research on the robotic dolphin is conducted. The results show that the jumping height of the robotic dolphin increases with the increase of the tail fin swing frequency, first increasing and then decreasing with the increase of the tail fin swing amplitude, and increases with the increase of the water-jumping angle. When the swing frequency is 2.5Hz, the swing amplitude is 30° degree and the water-jumping angle is 55°, the water outlet height reaches the maximum value.

articleTitle: A Innovative RTCP Detection Method for Five-Axis Machine Tools Based on The Serial Length Ball Bars
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: To efficient evaluate the dynamic accuracy of five-axis CNC machine tools, a RTCP (Rotation Tool Centre Point) detection method based on the serial length ball bars is proposed in this paper. A servo system for five-axis CNC machine tools is established, which serves as the theoretical foundation for RTCP detection. The effect of the serial lengths ball bar on the RTCP detection range and speed magnitude of five-axis CNC machine tools is comparatively analyzed. The result indicate that the velocity of the fifth axis tool spindle is not only one of the significant motion characteristics but also an important factor affecting the tool tip point error of the machine tool. As the combination of the fifth axis tool spindle velocity varies, the RTCP detection results become richer, with significant variations in the range of differences. The combination of the serial length ball bars more distinctly reflects the dynamic control precision status and exhibits superior performance in dynamic control precision testing. This method enriches the variations in RTCP detection results, enhancing the detection performance. It opens up new perspectives for RTCP detection of five-axis CNC machine tools and provides innovative detection approaches and theoretical foundations.

articleTitle: Fan Bearing Fault Diagnosis Algorithm Based on Improved VMD and LLe
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In order to enhance the precision of fan bearing fault diagnosis, this study presents a model for fan bearing fault diagnosis based on an improved VMD and LLE. Firstly, the fast Fourier transform (FFT) is utilized to extract the time-frequency graph of vibration signals, and the enhanced VMD algorithm is applied for denoising vibration signals and constructing high-frequency multi-domain feature vectors.
