Current object detection networks lack efficiency and accuracy in crack detection on the WTB owing to the low saliency cracks of the inner surface. Meanwhile, the impact on the accuracy of the crack detection model due to the low dynamic range of a single visible crack image on the inner surface of the WTB cannot be neglected. For the sake of solving the above problems, a new dataset is set, consisting of infrared (IR) and visible (VIS) images. The new network structure is proposed to utilize the above dataset, achieving the fusion of crack information between two modal images (IR-VIS). Moreover, to quantify cracks with width, height, and rotation angles accurately, a rotated bounding box method is introduced. Last but not least, a two-stage training method is designed to improve the training results, which can mitigate the low training speed of the model caused by the complexity of the fusion structure. The experimental study is carried out, showing the IR-VIS dataset is effective for crack detection, and the modified model improved detection performance by 31.59%. In crack detection of the inner surface on the WTB, the modified model outperforms base object detection model in the ablative experiments. Our method can improve accuracy up to 82.02% by fusing IR-VIS images. In addition, our model achieves 75.94% accuracy and runs at 38 FPS speed when paired with the Jetson Nano, a limited computational embedded device.

articleTitle: Active disturbance rejection control of load-side converter for photovoltaic microgrid based on fuzzy theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: DC microgrid load-side voltage supply stability is an important prerequisite for realizing high-level operation of new energy power. In order to maintain the voltage stability of the low-voltage load side, this paper establishes a small-signal model of the low-voltage load-side converter, theoretically analyzes the basic principle of fuzzy self-immunity, and proposes a FLADRC control strategy with parameter self-seeking optimization. Finally, the performance difference between the proposed control strategy and the traditional LADRC control strategy and PI control strategy is analyzed by simulation under different working conditions to illustrate the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Dynamics Evaluation of a Magnetic Actuated Soft Bionic Minirobot with Paired Fin
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This study introduced a combination of mechanical modeling and numerical simulation to investigate the swimming characteristics and dynamic mechanisms of micro magnetically-controlled bionic soft robot with paired fin. The primary focus was on the integrated modeling and simulation of the magnetic torque transmission-soft body deformation and overall motion-fluid response process within the motion chain, including the design of mechanical structures, motion strategies, structural orderliness and stability, and propulsion performance. Meanwhile, this research explored the complex flow disturbances and flow control mechanisms during the swimming of micro magnetically-controlled biorobotic robot, thereby revealing potential hydrodynamic advantages in their locomotion. The contribution of this study was not only significant for the dynamic principles of micro magnetically-controlled flexible robot motion but also provide theoretical and technical support for the optimized design and formation control of biorobotic soft robot and micro/nano medical robots working in the narrow space.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Rotary Constant Tension Mooring Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Aiming at the problems in the mooring process of large ships under bad sea conditions, a design of a rotating constant tension mooring system is proposed in this paper. The calculation of parameters and the selection of key components in the mooring process are carried out, and the accumulator is selected as the power source in the mooring process to reduce the energy loss in the mooring process. The mechanical structure and working mode of rotary constant tension mooring system are introduced in detail. A joint analysis was carried out in AQWA and Simulink, and the analysis results showed that the tension on the rope of the rotary constant tension mooring system was relatively constant compared with the traditional bollard mooring system, so it could effectively improve the stability of the mooring process under the condition of using less energy. It avoids breaking of the cable due to excessive instantaneous tension on the cable during mooring.

articleTitle: DOA accuracy improvement method for moving acoustic array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This paper focuses on the issue of reduced accuracy in Direction of Arrival (DOA) estimation caused by the movement of an acoustic array. The causes of this phenomenon are analyzed using the signal incidence model. An iterative correction method was proposed to mitigate the impact of array motion on direction-finding accuracy when applied to the DOA estimation over multiple iterations. The formulas for array coordinate offset during motion were derived, starting with the linear array, and subsequently generalized to arrays of arbitrary geometry. Based on the derived coordinate offset formulas, a coordinate correction method is proposed. Simulation results for the cross-shaped, rectangular, and circular arrays demonstrate a significant improvement in the orientation accuracy of the array during motion using the proposed correction method.

articleTitle: Member Positioning Method Based on Vector Orientation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This paper introduces a member positioning method based on vector orientation analysis, aimed at enhancing the edge detection accuracy and stability of truss climbing robots in complex environments. Traditional edge detection algorithms like Canny and LSD, though effective in extracting lines from images, are sensitive to environmental noise and changes in illumination, leading to edge displacement and discontinuities that affect positioning accuracy. By integrating the Canny algorithm with the horizontal line angle from LSD and employing vector orientation analysis for precise edge extraction, this study overcomes the impact of environmental disturbances, significantly improving the system's adaptability and recognition accuracy. The research validates the effectiveness of this method under simulated real-world conditions through experimental environment construction, accurately identifying and restoring the edge information of members, thus providing technical support for the safe and stable operation of truss climbing robots. This work not only enhances the accuracy of edge detection but also offers a new solution for member recognition and positioning in complex visual environments.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Comprehensive Testing and Research Platform for Miniature Blowers in Emergency Transport Ventilators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Ventilators play a crucial role in medical systems, with miniature blowers serving as vital components for air supply. The performance and stability of these miniature blowers are pivotal for the operation of ventilators. To comprehensively investigate the vibration characteristics of miniature blowers in ventilators, this paper designs and establishes a comprehensive testing and research platform. The platform aims to monitor the vibration conditions of miniature blowers under various operating conditions, including extreme conditions, and also functions as a simple centrifugal excitation platform, providing a high-frequency excitation source for subsequent optimization studies. Through comparative analysis of experimental data, the reliability of this platform is validated, demonstrating its significant support for research on miniature blowers in ventilators.

articleTitle: One-Step Auto-Registration using Linear Structured Light-based for Neurosurgical Navigation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Neurosurgical navigation system plays a very important role in current neurosurgery. Manual marker-based surgical registration methods provide great accuracy, but involve time-consuming and complex operations that can only be performed prior to sterilization. Neurosurgical navigation system requires a simplified registration process that decreases the difficulty for the surgeon, shortens patient-to-image registration time, and adapts to higher sterile surgical environments. Therefore, this study reports a new contactless automated registration approach using line structured light technology in neurosurgical navigation. The contactless facial point cloud data is acquired by scanning the patient with line structured light. The CT model performs spatial pose enumeration in which all the poses are traversed to find the best of them to match with the facial point cloud, thus realizing one-step automatic registration. Experiments have demonstrated that the average root mean square error is 0.6027 ±0.0453 mm for 0.05 relative sampling length, 120° step size, and 200 iterations. One-step registration offers more convenience, simplicity, accuracy and speed over manual registration. In the future, we will strive for spatial iterative algorithm execution speed enhancement and the integration of this registration technique with augmented reality (AR) to establish the relationship between image space, surgical space, and video streaming space.

articleTitle: An Occlusion Removal Approach for Surgical Instruments Based on the Optical Flow-Guided Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Surgical instrument removal has become increasingly necessary to provide precise information during intraoperative execution. Occlusions in the endoscopic view caused by interactions between surgical instruments and organs can impede a surgeon's ability to accurately assess internal tissue, as well as certain computer-assisted surgical algorithms that rely on endoscopic images. This work demonstrates a novel application of removing surgical instruments from endoscopic video utilizing flow-guided image inpainting methods. A comparative experiment was conducted to validate the advantages of the improved method. Additionally, two task-based experiments including target tracking and image fusion experiments were conducted to further demonstrate its potential as a preprocessing step for other visual algorithms.

articleTitle: Design and Tolerance Analysis of an Androgynous Petal-Shaped End Tool Quick-Change Mechanism for Space Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In order to improve the flexible operation of the end of space manipulators and adapt to the complex operation requirements on-orbit, a quick-change mechanism for end tools using a androgynous petal-shaped docking surface is designed. This mechanism allows the manipulator to swiftly replace end tools, thereby enhancing its operation efficiency on orbit. In this paper, based on the concept of androgynous design, a petal-shaped docking surface is constructed by combining the advantages of the probe-cone docking mechanism and the V-groove positioning mechanism. The petal-shaped docking surface is used for the active end and passive interface of the end tool quick-change mechanism to fulfill the demands of on-orbit maintenance tasks for a space manipulator. This design improvement significantly enhances misalignment tolerance and positioning accuracy performance. Moreover, this paper proposes a misalignment tolerance analysis method based on the position and posture perturbation matrix method. It analyzes the performance of the end quick-change mechanism with a 5-degree freedom misalignment tolerance. Through ADAMS docking dynamics simulation tests and prototype physical experiments, the accuracy of the perturbation matrix analysis results is verified. It has been determined that the androgynous petal-shaped end tool quick-change mechanism designed in this paper meets the misalignment tolerance index of the on-orbit maintenance tasks.

articleTitle: Tactile Sensor using Shape-memory Alloy Wires for Human-like Tactile Perception
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The recent research has revealed that the deformation caused by applied stress to a shape-memory alloy (SMA) generates a change in the electrical resistance caused by the superelasticity. We have also developed a novel micro-vibration actuator driven by periodic electric pulse current, by employing the shape-memory effect of an SMA wire. The actuators are effectively applied to various types of tactile displays to present different tactile sensations on human skin. By effectively employing the physical property of the superelasticity related with the resistance change, the SMA wire is applied to a micro-force sensor with the high sensitivity, while generating micro-vibration. In this paper, a novel tactile sensing system is proposed by arranging plural SMA-based sensors in an array. For the evaluation of the micro-force sensing ability, experiments are conducted by employing six common objects with different surface texture and stiffness. The result shows the introduced tactile sensor structure has the characteristics to be applicable for human-like tactile perception.

articleTitle: An Alternating Stepping Climbing Machine Based on TRIZ Theory Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The unmanned handling vehicle (AGV) has a wide range of applications in both civil and industrial fields, and can replace manual labor to complete the handling work. In the thesis, we use TRIZ theory to optimize the existing stepping climbing mechanism, design a high efficiency and high stability of the climbing machine, the front of the climbing machine for the double-centered crank rocker mechanism, the use of alternate stepping to complete the climbing movement, improve the efficiency of climbing, the back of a crank slider mechanism to achieve the function of auxiliary pressure to climb the stairs, and with the electric actuator to regulate the position of the center of gravity, to ensure the stability of climbing the stairs. The center of gravity is adjusted with an electric actuator to ensure the stability of climbing. We have carried out theoretical calculations, simulation verification and physical verification to confirm the feasibility of the stair climber.

articleTitle: Distributed Formation Fault Tolerance Control Based on Improved Artificial Potential Field Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of formation fault-tolerant control in the case of large underwater communication delay and serious data packet loss. An improved distributed formation control method of artificial potential field method combined with coherence theory is proposed to solve the problem of insufficient stability of large-scale multi-AUV systems working together and to maximize the use of communication resources of the formation system. The method adapts the maneuverability of underwater robots by designing the potential field function as a buffer shape, and improves the robustness of the formation system by designing a fault-tolerant control algorithm based on graph theory. The theoretical validation and simulation analysis show that the distributed formation control method based on the improved artificial potential field can realize formation reconfiguration and formation obstacle avoidance when the AUV cluster size is large, while the formation control system has a certain degree of fault tolerance.

articleTitle: Road Marking Damage Degree Detection Based on Adaptive Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The clarity of road markings is crucial for safe vehicle operation. Over time, road markings may detach to different extents, making it crucial to promptly assess the degree of damage and repair severely affected areas. To evaluate the degree of damage to road markings, we propose a method that integrates pixel segmentation and region segmentation. Pixel segmentation primarily segments damaged markings at the pixel level, while region segmentation aims to capture the entire region of the road marking image. However, indiscriminate feature fusion during segmentation may decrease the model's sensitivity to target boundaries and its capability to segment small objects. Consequently, we propose an attention-guided adaptive feature fusion method to enhance region segmentation. Experiments show that our model achieves a pixel accuracy of 0.9920 and an average intersection-to-merge ratio of 0.8601 in region segmentation, accurately assessing the degree of damaged markers. The method proposed in this paper is simple, effective, and holds great potential for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Excited ICU Delirium Behavior Detection Method Based on Human Key Points Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Currently, existing human key point detection algorithms have poor adaptability and are easily affected by light intensity in specific scenarios such as delirium early warning in the intensive care unit. Therefore, these algorithms cannot achieve 24/7 monitoring identification. To address these issues, this paper proposes a delirium early warning algorithm based on human key points estimation under infrared vision. The data input into the algorithm is infrared images, which effectively avoids the influence of light intensity on the algorithm's performance and enables 24/7 monitoring detection. The model is lightweight based on the original OpenPose key point recognition algorithm. Simultaneously, the improved OpenPose algorithm achieves a dual benefit: it streamlines parameter usage while enhancing key point recognition accuracy. This paper also proposes a soft mechanism of delirium recognition based on human skeleton sequence, which implements velocity constraints on the identified key points in the time domain to assist delirium recognition. The proposed method was verified by experiments on the self-built infrared vision key point detection dataset of human lying posture. The average recognition accuracy of all key points is 77.3%, and the average recognition accuracy of the improved OpenPose algorithm is 4.9% higher than that of the original algorithm. Based on the human skeleton sequence recognized by the algorithm, it can identify and warn of delirium behavior in severe patients.

articleTitle: Simulation Modelling of Air Cushion Pressure Detector for Piggyback Transfer Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In this study, an air cushion pressure detector is proposed and applied to a piggyback transfer robot. The objective is to enhance comfort during the robot's operation and monitor the magnitude of care-receiver’s chest pressure. Initially, this paper proposes an air cushion structure and determine the comfortable internal pressure by comparative experiments. Numerical simulation of air cushion compression process is performed on this basis. Next, the pressure detector is fabricated utilizing the air cushion, gas pressure sensors, and strain acquisition modules. Finally, a BP neural network mapping model is established using the average internal pressure of the air cushion and the voltage value output from the strain acquisition modules as inputs and the external load as outputs. The proposed air cushion pressure detector can reduce the impact and pressure concentration, which can meet the need of the piggyback transfer robot.

articleTitle: A Novel Method to Reduce Toque Ripple with Variable dc-link Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: There exists commutation torque ripple (CTR) when the brushless DC motors (BLDCM) run under the square-wave mode. The torque ripple may cause vibration and noise. To overcome the problem, this paper presents a novel variable structure boosting unit to acquire regulation function of the dc-link voltage for reducing the torque ripple and achieving smooth electromagnetic torque. In the method, the variable structure boosting unit is charged by the trigger switch in the normal conduction period (NCP) and is used to achieve boosting dc-link voltage in the commutation period (CP), which remains the non-commutation phase current steady to obtain free-ripple electromagnetic torque. The variable structure boosting unit is composed of several discrete components and the design cost is low. The PI controller is used both in the NCP and CP, the controller switching is avoided accordingly. The proposed structure boosting unit is verified with different load condition and the experiment results show the proposed method exhibits superior steady performance. The presented unit is tested under loading condition and it shows desirable performance. Moreover, the frequency spectrum of the electromagnetic torque is analyzed, and results shows the boosting unit can diminish the 6nf harmonics effectively.

articleTitle: Design and Control of an Ellipsoidal Underwater Robot Driven by Four-Vector Propellers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: With the increasing demand for underwater exploration and intervention tasks, the development of efficient and maneuverable underwater robots is essential. This paper introduced a novel ellipsoidal underwater robot(EUR) designed specifically for precise motion control in aquatic environments. The prototype features a unique propulsion system and thruster configuration optimized for underwater navigation. Thrust vectoring was achieved through the rotation of the propulsion unit, enhancing maneuverability underwater. Detailed design aspects and practical realization of the four-propeller driven prototype were discussed. The kinematics and dynamics of the underwater robot were analyzed, followed by the description of the parallel PID control system, including position control, and attitude control algorithms. Simulations and experimental results demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed design in achieving precise underwater motion control. The innovative design concept proposed in this paper will be of great value to the research and development of underwater robotics, which can be used to enhance precise navigation and maneuverability in diverse aquatic environments.

articleTitle: Research on improving the control quality of the flying objects in stabilizing roll angular rate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The paper presents a study on developing a novel roll linearization model and designing control gains through the utilization of a three-loop autopilot to stabilize the roll angle and roll angular rate for unmanned aerial vehicles. The key contribution lies in the introduction of a new linear model that describes the flying object more accurately compared to known models. Additionally, the research demonstrates that the control efficiency achieved when using the new model for controller design is more prominent compared to the old one, especially for flying objects exhibiting high directional stability and operating under flight conditions where the sideslip angle is significantly large.

articleTitle: Wall-Sticking Drone for Non-Destructive Inspection of Oblique Planes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This paper discusses the preliminary design and analysis of a light-duty unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) for remote inspection operations. Due to limitations in payload capacity and energy supply, small drones are often employed in distant visual inspection tasks. We propose a novel UAV landing gear system for non-destructive testing operations on carbon steel spherical storage tanks. The landing gear system employs a servo motor as the power source. It utilizes a combination of slider crank and gear mechanisms for controlling the orientation of the magnetic grippers, enabling adhesion in conjunction with UAV flight. Additionally, the system incorporates a cost-effective and lightweight switchable magnetic adhesion method based on neodymium magnets and silicon steel sheets to reduce weight, which can provide 37.72N per unit. The system’s total weight is approximately 1.6kg, with a payload capacity of 400g. The proposed prototype design has sufficient payload capacity to carry standard non-destructive testing probes, such as ultrasonic and electromagnetic, supported by empirical evidence obtained through our in-house experiments.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Unity-Based Virtual Simulation Verification Platform in Shield Machine Tool-Changing Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: With the wide application of shield machine in underground engineering, the safety and efficiency of hob changing operation become the focus of attention. In this paper, a Unity-based virtual simulation verification platform is proposed and applied to shield machine hobbing knife changing robot. The platform provides strong support for the research and application of shield machine tool changing robot by reproducing the shield machine hobbing tool changing environment, verifying the realtime collision distance of the robotic arm, optimizing the data exchange cycle, and introducing augmented reality hardware interface and other innovative means. This paper describes in detail the construction process of the platform, its innovative points and its experimental validation, providing a reference for research in related fields.

articleTitle: Flocking Control Strategy of Multi-underwater Spherical Robot based on Potential Function
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Underwater robot formation cooperation is an important research content of swarm intelligence on underwater robot. Based on the Flocking algorithm and the dynamics characteristics of the underwater spherical robot, this paper establishes a multi-underwater spherical robot flocking model. Then, through a series of simulation, the reliability and stability of the group movement of underwater robots are verified. Moreover, the effect of flocking is explained by analyzing the trajectory and control quantity. Finally, the application is extended by simulating more robots and more complex scenarios.

articleTitle: The influence of background continuity on "hole" object cognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate whether the continuity of the background will affect the perception of the hole as an object through the object-based attention effect. The stimuli used in the study were similar to those in Albrecht et al.'s study, with the exception that the hole rotated 90 ° clockwise to differentiate it from the background. The results show that when the background is complete, the object-based effect does not appear, indicating that the hole will not be perceived as a separate object. When the background is segmented, the hole will be perceived as an object, resulting in an object effect. Therefore, the continuity of the background and the integration of the hole with the background should influence the perception of the hole as an object. This study further emphasizes the relationship between foreground objects and background regions, which affects the distribution of visual attention.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-based Detection of Deep-sea Hydrothermal Polymetallic Sulfides, Plume, and Their Biological Communities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Because of their rich mineral resources and extreme ecological environments, deep-sea hydrothermal vent areas are significantly valuable both scientifically and economically. Optical imaging is the most direct method for verifying deep-sea hydrothermal activity. Autonomous detection and recognition of hydrothermal activity using optical imaging can significantly improve underwater robot detection efficiency. However, because of the difficulty in obtaining optical images of deep-sea hydrothermal activity and the limited accumulation of data, to date, there have been few studies on the autonomous detection of various characteristic targets of hydrothermal activity. To achieve autonomous detection and recognition of deep-sea hydrothermal polymetallic sulfides, plumes, and their biological communities, this study developed an optical image dataset of deep-sea hydrothermal activity, proposed an improved YOLOv8-based multi-target real-time detection algorithm, introduced the CBAM attention mechanism, and modified the network structure. Experimental results show that the improved algorithm achieves better target detection performance, and the response time reaches 6.8ms, which satisfies the real-time performance for underwater robots to autonomously identify hydrothermal vents.

articleTitle: Design and Characterisation of Electromagnetic Coils in Positioning Device for Vascular Interventional Surgery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The lack of 3D positioning function restrains surgeons from acquiring surgical information and only observes 2D X-ray images for vascular interventional surgery, which affects the safety and success rate of the surgery. It also impedes the development of the surgical navigation. In this paper, a rotating magnetic field-based electromagnetic positioning device is proposed to predict the pose of sensors embedded in the catheter tip. The transmitting coil excites the high-frequency magnetic field. And the sensing coil is induced in the alternating magnetic field. The electromagnetic coils are designed to realize a stable mutual inductance, which are the fundament of the electromagnetic positioning device. A series of calculations and verifications are performed to demonstrate the feasibility of the designed coils.

articleTitle: CatMonitor : LTE Cat-1 based Wildlife Intelligent Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Due to the urgent need for wildlife conservation and monitoring, we design CatMonitor, a LTE Cat-1 based intelligent wildlife monitoring system. Specifically, we leverage LTE Cat-1 based wireless communication technology, in conjunction with embedded devices and cameras, to achieve remote, real-time, and efficient image collection of wildlife habitats. The core components of the system include a data acquisition module, such as temperature, humidity, GPS, and image information, and a data transmission and processing module. The data acquisition module utilizes low-power sensors and camera equipment to ensure a stable collection of information on wildlife activity environments in various wilderness environments. Besides, the system integrates the LTE Cat-1 module, which transmits the collected environmental data information to the cloud server in real time and at high speed. CatMonitor offers user-friendly accessibility, allowing users to remotely monitor and manage the system through web interfaces. The experimental results show that CatMonitor has good scalability and stability, and can adapt to complex changes in the field environment.

articleTitle: Research on Missile Borne Hemispherical Resonance/ Micro Electromechanical System Gyroscopic Navigation Technology Based on Coarse Fine Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This study focuses on the coarse-precision coupling of Hemispherical Resonator Gyro (HRG) and Micro Electromechanical System (MEMS) Gyro for the new requirements of high controllability, high degree of automation, and diversification of combat modes for navigation systems in future wars, with the aim of enhancing the utility of Hemispherical Resonator Gyro and laying the technical foundation for the ballistic applications. Through the in-depth analysis of the error mechanism during the coaxial assembly of the two gyroscopes, this paper establishes an installation error model and optimizes the coupling accuracy of the two through the rotary scheme of the rotary table. The study improves the measurement accuracy by fusing the outputs of the two gyros through dual-channel measurement and Kalman filtering algorithm in order to estimate and correct the bias error of the MEMS gyro. It is experimentally verified that the method in this paper can effectively estimate and compensate the zero bias of the MEMS gyro in a low dynamic environment, thus improving the measurement accuracy of the MEMS gyro and the overall performance of the navigation system. The research results are of great significance to enhance the autonomous navigation capability of tactical missiles in complex electromagnetic environment.

articleTitle: Correlation Analysis Between Waterfowl Swimming Behavior and Propulsion Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This research aims to investigate the potential impact of single-webbed duck foot stroke frequency and amplitude on its propulsion efficiency. Based on the consideration that real duck flippers will open and close, this paper utilizes ADAMS to simulate the motion of duck flippers and CFD for hydrodynamic simulation. The experimental results show that the propulsive force obtained by the flippers is positively correlated with the frequency and amplitude, and the flippers that can be deformed are favorable to the propulsive efficiency. This study provides a new perspective on the physiological and biomechanical study of waterfowl swimming behavior and provides theoretical support for the design of bio-inspired underwater robots and the optimization of water sports equipment.

articleTitle: IMU-based continuous prediction of human lower limb joint angles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Predicting human motion intent is crucial for exoskeleton robots to provide effective assistance. In recent years, many deep learning-based predicting methods have been shown to provide effective prediction of human movement intentions. On the other hand, current researchers often ignore the cyclic and rhythmic nature of human walking. We propose an Adaptive Multi-Oscillator Kalman Filter Prediction (AMOKFP) model that uses kinematic data to predict human movement states over a short period of time in the future. Our approach consists of three stages: gait feature learning, parameter prediction and state prediction optimization. In the first stage, we decompose and learn human motion features. In the second stage, we perform numerical prediction on the learning results from the first phase. In the third stage, we perform optimal estimation on the prediction results from the second phase. The simulation results show that the model has a good estimation performance and the prediction error is stable at 0.13°. The AMOKFP model proposed in this paper can be applied to the control system of lower limb-assisted exoskeleton robots as a part of state perception and involved in the planning of exoskeleton assisting moments.

articleTitle: DH Detector: One-stage detection model with double-head detector and efficient convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This article explores advanced techniques to build a network model, including the use of a double-head(DH) detector: one section of which is responsible for performing classification and the other for object prediction. This is followed by information stitching, which allows the model to learn more appropriate parameters. Subsequently, a CSP structure incorporating an attention mechanism is used to improve the feature extraction capabilities of the model. Finally, dynamic convolution is added to enhance the feature representation. Our model is trained from scratch on the COCO Dataset without taking a pre-trained model, the results of which are listed below. Based on 300 epochs of training, the mAP values for the four versions of DH Detector (s, m, l, x, the network model becomes larger in turn) are 40.8, 46.1, 48, and 49.8(100 epoch), respectively. The experiment results show that this method outperforms other competing methods in terms of both quantity and quality. In addition, the mAP of DH-s and DH-l reached 43.0 and 50.1 at an input image size of 960. A comparison of DH Detector with other algorithms is provided in Figure 1.

articleTitle: Cable Attitude Detection Technology Based on Rotation Matrix
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: We use rotation matrix to detect cable attitude. This paper includes the attitude measurement of the cable in both the 2D and 3D planes. Two-dimensional refers to changing the distance between two piles, three-dimensional refers to the movement of the cable before and after due to external factors, using the six-axis IMU attitude sensor to measure the angle of the x, y, z three-axis direction of the reference point, using the translation and rotation matrix, the coordinates are transformed to the three-dimensional coordinate system (absolute coordinate system) of the starting point, and the coordinates of each reference point are obtained, so as to measure the change state of the cable curve. The more reference points selected in this method, the more accurate the results and the smoother the curve.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Hand Rehabilitation Exoskeleton Based on Compound Drive of Cable and Leaf Spring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: For the post-stroke finger clonus period, the patient's muscle tension increases, and the finger flexion can not be extended as a clonus. A novel hand rehabilitation exoskeleton based on a compound drive of cable and leaf spring has been designed to help with finger rehabilitation. The large stiffness leaf spring helps the patient to complete the extension movement, and the flexion grasping movement is completed under the action of the cable. The structure has good flexibility, which makes the interaction between the hand and the exoskeleton robot safer. Based on the Denavit-Hartenberg (DH) parameters method, the kinematic model of the finger has been built to be used in designing the exoskeleton. The static characteristics of the exoskeleton are analyzed based on the stiffness of the leaf spring. A virtual prototype is built using Multibody to simulate and analyze the change in cable length and leaf spring stiffness. The simulation results demonstrate the accuracy of the kinematic model and the rationality of the design.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of 4-RPUR Parallel Mechanism for Ankle Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Four-degrees-of-freedom (4-DoFs) ankle fracture surgery assistant and rehabilitation robot based on 4-RPUR was developed to help the patients recover movement ability of the ankle. Furthermore, to evaluate the performance of the robot, we use a spatial search method to calculate and depict the workspace images, and analyze the sensitivity of the workspace to different parameters; based on screw theory, a singularity evaluation indicator is proposed, and singularity images are drawn; the robot is subjected to stiffness modeling, constructing a stiffness matrix for the mechanism and establishing stiffness evaluation indicators, and creating performance spectra, with further analysis and discussion on the physical variation rules and physical meanings of the spectra.

articleTitle: Preliminary Design of a Magnetically Actuated Multifunctional Biopsy Capsule Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: We propose a novel magnetically actuated multifunctional capsule robot to perform active locomotion and biopsy functions. The capsule robot is governed by a magnetically actuated system that utilizes three-axis Helmholtz coils to produce rotating magnetic fields in three dimensions. The capsule robot is main composed of a spiral body, screw shaft, nut, annular magnet, cylindrical magnet, bearing, and biopsy needle. We analyze the magnetic torque and force generated by the magnets for application in active locomotion and biopsy procedures. Finally, we prototype the biopsy capsule robot and conduct experiments to validate its ability to perform active locomotion and biopsy procedures within pipelines.

articleTitle: Two-stage Hybrid Insulator Defect Inspection from Aerial Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: To guarantee the stable operation of the electric system, regular inspection of the electrical components, such as electrical transmission lines and insulators, is necessary. With the process of deep learning and computer vision, automatable detection and inspection of insulators becomes possible. However, the defect detection of the insulators is non-trivial due to complicated backgrounds, various occlusions, light conditions, and motion blur. To handle these problems, we propose a two-stage framework to achieve the defect detection of insulators. The proposed framework consists of the insulator detection network and the defect identification network. First, we detect the position and size of the insulator based on modified YOLOv5. Then, the full image is cropped and fed to the defect identification network. To ease the negative impact of low luminance and image blur, we adopt gamma correction and image sharpening on cropped insulator images. This formulation will improve the accuracy of the defect identification network greatly. Quantitative and qualitative results on our collected dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed model.

articleTitle: Flexible Belt Constrained Catheterization Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Currently, vascular interventional technology is the most effective method for treating cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases. Research on vascular interventional robotic technology has become a popular topic. This article proposes a catheterization robot based on two flexible belts constraint, the flexible rod such as catheter, guidewire or balloon can not only be constrained by the flexible belts, but also achieve its purpose of being transported through the interaction force with the belts. Through setting comparative experiment, the results indicate that the proposed catheterization robot in this article meets the relevant usage requirements, and it can also realize the long-stroke transportation of the flexible rod, the delivery error is within 2.0 mm, and the rotation angle error is within 2.0°.

articleTitle: Structural Parameter Selection Strategy of Gripper for Enhanced Gripping Force and Jam Resistance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Grippers capable of grasping and releasing under high loads are crucial for robots performing heavy-load tasks. This research introduces an innovative structural parameter selection strategy to develop such a mechanical gripper. This strategy emerges from detailed modeling and analysis of the mechanical gripper. The strategy significantly improves gripping force and anti-jamming ability by analyzing the screw and guide rail's parameters and the impact of gripping speed on the gripping and locking force. With this strategy, we have developed a mechanical gripper with the maximum gripping force of 311.08N and locking force of 755N. We also installed the gripper on a humanoid robot, enabling it to enter a car with one hand and manipulate the steering wheel. The results further assess the effectiveness of the selection strategy.

articleTitle: A Breeding Animal Detection Method from Images With Grided Heatmaps
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In practical scenarios for detecting objects in images where we cannot collect sufficient effective annotated data, we propose a new method that can utilize pre-trained classification network models to implement object detection tasks. Our method generates multiple scale gridded heatmaps from a pre-trained classification network, which can effectively integrate various pre-trained features of different categories without training. We also utilize similarity segmentation results to further refine the object detection performance. Our experiment results on COCO, VOC and our datasets show that our method can produce better detection results compared to some existing object detection networks when the number of training data is small for other networks.

articleTitle: Torque Estimation Based on An Improved SOGI-FLL for IPMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Applications using motors often require precise control of output torque. However, direct measurement of torque can be costly and unreliable. Therefore, significant research attention has been given to the development of torque estimation methods to overcome these limitations. This paper presents a methodology to design a high precision torque observer for interior permanent-magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) by implementing the discrete-time flux observer based on an improved second-order generalized integrator-frequency-locked loop (SOGI-FLL). In this scheme, an easy-tuning FLL is proposed as the speed estimator without extra signal estimation compared to previous FLL. Additionally, with aim to improve the estimation performance at sampling-to-fundamental frequency ratios, the discretization method of SOGI-FLL is illustrated and its validity is confirmed in frequency domain by Bode diagram. Experimental results show that the estimation accuracy of electromagnetic torque is dependable even at low sampling- to-fundamental frequency ratios.

articleTitle: Based on the Optimization and Performance Evaluation of YOLOv8 Object Detection Model with Multi-backbone Network Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The paper aims to enhance the recognition accuracy of the YOLOv8 object detection model in complex scenarios. To achieve this goal, various high-performance backbone networks, including ResNet50, DenseNet169, ConvNeXt, and EfficientNetv2, are integrated with YOLOv8 to construct four novel detection models: YOLOv8-ResNet50, YOLOv8-DenseNet169, YOLOv8-ConvNeXt, and YOLOv8-EfficientNetv2. These models combine the unique characteristics of each backbone network, aiming to further improve detection accuracy while maintaining YOLOv8's real-time performance. Rigorous experimental validation is conducted on a self-constructed leaf mustard dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that YOLOv8-EfficientNetv2 performs the best among these models, achieving a high accuracy of 95.2% in mAP50 and 85.3% in mAP50:95. Compared with the original YOLOv8, YOLOv8-EfficientNetv2 exhibits improvements of 0.87% and 1.6% in mAP50 and mAP50:95, respectively, significantly enhancing the accuracy of object detection. This research provides novel ideas and methods for the application of YOLO series models in complex scenarios, laying a solid foundation for future object detection research.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis on Lateral Vibration Characteristics of Rotor Considering Electromagnetic Torque
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The air compressors, directly driven by the high-speed permanent magnet synchronous motor, were used in the hydrogen energy transportation, such as hydrogen fuel cell vehicles and hydrogen energy railway trains. The influence of the electromagnetic torque, generated by the deflection angle, on the lateral vibration of the rotor, needs to be studied. This paper presented the dynamic equation of the rotor supported by foil gas bearings. The electromagnetic torque was considered, and the dynamic equations of rotor lateral vibration were established. The numerical calculations of the dynamic equations were carried out. The values of lateral vibration were analyzed. The influence of electromagnetic torque on the lateral vibration was studied, and the results of rotor displacement were obtained. The theoretical analysis conducted in this paper can provide the theoretical basis for research on electromechanical coupling dynamics.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Dynamic Performance of a Novel Egg-shaped Underwater Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: With the increasing demand for ocean exploration and underwater operations, the development of new autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) to adapt to specific marine environments has become crucial. This paper designed an innovative Egg-shaped Underwater Robot (EUR) aiming to optimize its mobility, stability and operational efficiency in complex underwater environments. Compared to traditional simulation robots of various types, the structure possessed the stability of a ball-shaped robot and the characteristics of a streamlined robot. The EUR adopted a unique elliptic structure to reduce underwater drag, improve maneuverability and enhance load capacity. Then, the overall design of the EUR was presented with detailed descriptions of the mechanical structure and electrical system respectively. Next, various motion states of the EUR and experimental validation were simulated by Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), and the experimental results showed that the motion characteristics of the EUR are acceptable, and the design was worthy of further study.

articleTitle: Global Path Planning For AUV Based on Improved Grey Wolf Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Due to the gray wolf optimization algorithm's slow convergence rate and vulnerability to local optima, an enhanced version tailored for AUV path planning is introduced. Firstly, underwater obstacles and ocean current models are established based on the underwater environment, and a fitness function with path length, obstacle constraints, and time constraints is designed for the AUV. Additionally, a nonlinear convergence factor is devised, and the positional update concept from particle swarm optimization is incorporated to expedite the algorithm's convergence rate. Lastly, a Levy flight strategy is incorporated to safeguard against the algorithm's entrapment in local optima. Through simulation experiments, the proposed algorithm is compared with other algorithms. Simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm exhibits accelerated convergence and proficiently identifies optimal solutions.

articleTitle: Underwater Target Recognition and Tracking Based on Bionic Horseshoe Crab Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In recent years, biomimetic robotic technology h-as greatly simplified the complexity of human underwater exploration. In order to realize the effective recognition and tracking of underwater targets by a biomimetic horseshoe crab amphibious robot (BHCR), an algorithm based on lateral suppression principle is proposed. Finally, through image enhancement experiments and pool static target detection experiments, it is confirmed that BHCR can proficiently identify and track underwater static targets by using multi-freedom motion capability and ALin-based tracking algorithm.

articleTitle: Active Impedance Control for Comfort of Piggyback Transfer Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In order to improve the comfort of piggyback transfer robot, an active impedance control method based on position inner loop is proposed. The objective of this control method is to take the ideal axillary force as the outer loop control target and the chest holder angle adjustment as the inner loop control target. By using MATLAB and LabVIEW software, the control program of the piggyback transfer robot is built, and the impedance control system is established. A human-robot interaction experiment is designed to verify the effect of the established active impedance control on the axillary force of the care-receivers.

articleTitle: Enhanced Rocker-based Inverted Pendulum Model for Human Dynamic Analysis in Lower Limb Exoskeletons
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In response to the problems encountered in the application of exoskeleton gait models, we have established a 2-DOF inverted pendulum kinematics model of human gait in our previous research. Gait and stability control during walking is the most important issue in the design of lower limb exoskeletons. In this paper, we builts a dynamics model of human gait based on the 2-DOF inverted pendulum model. It is demonstrated that roll factor plays an important role in the gait dynamics. The experimental results show that the model and the conclusions are correct, which can provide a good theoretical basis for the optimal gait control and stability control of exoskeleton. In addition, we further discuss the influence of human horizontal acceleration on exoskeleton optimization assistance.

articleTitle: Voltage Balance Control Strategy for FC 3-Level Inverter Based on Zero Vector Time Redistribution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This paper proposes a voltage balancing method based on adjusting the action time of the O redundant vector to address the voltage balancing problem of flying capacitor three-level. Firstly, the main reason for capacitor voltage imbalance in the flying capacitor three-level inverter are analyzed from the topology structure. Based on traditional voltage equalization control, a scheme of voltage regulation coefficient for flying capacitors is introduced: sampling output phase current and flying capacitor voltage, adjusting the time allocation of O redundancy state according to the deviation between actual capacitor voltage and expected value, and adjusting the impact of output current on capacitor voltage charging and discharging, in order to achieve voltage equalization effect on flying capacitors. Finally, a simulation model was built in Matlab/Simulink and an experimental platform was established for verification. The results showed that the scheme achieved stable control of capacitor voltage.

articleTitle: InsightSee: Advancing Multi-agent Vision-Language Models for Enhanced Visual Understanding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Accurate visual understanding is imperative for advancing autonomous systems and intelligent robots. Despite the powerful capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) in processing complex visual scenes, precisely recognizing obscured or ambiguously presented visual elements remains challenging. To tackle such issues, this paper proposes InsightSee, a multi-agent framework to enhance VLMs’ interpretative capabilities in handling complex visual understanding scenarios. The framework comprises a description agent, two reasoning agents, and a decision agent, which are integrated to refine the process of visual information interpretation. The design of these agents and the mechanisms by which they can be enhanced in visual information processing are presented. Experimental results demonstrate that the InsightSee framework not only boosts performance on specific visual tasks but also retains the original models’ strength. The proposed framework outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms in 6 out of 9 benchmark tests, with a substantial advancement in multimodal understanding.

articleTitle: LiDAR-based human pose estimation with MotionBERT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Human body pose estimation has a wide range of applications in the field of artificial intelligence and is gradually applied in daily life. However, for some specific scenes and people, privacy and security need to be ensured, and devices such as cameras are no longer the optimal choice, so this paper proposes the idea of using LiDAR technology to acquire human body point cloud images, and preprocessing and segmentation to extract a pure human body point cloud model. First, the useful parts around the human body are extracted by preprocessing the point cloud image obtained from LiDAR scanning. Then, a segmentation technique is utilized to separate the human body from the surrounding objects, keeping only the human body part. Next, the excess noise is removed by filtering process to get the pure human body point cloud model. Finally, the motionBert3d model is used to estimate the pose of the preprocessed point cloud image, and the pose estimation points and the 3D pose estimation model of the human body are obtained, which lays the foundation for the subsequent human motion recognition.

articleTitle: Research on Design and Control Strategy of Multi-winding PMSM for Solar-powered UAV
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: A novel multi-winding permanent magnet synchronous motor (MWPMSM)suitable for distributed energy management systems is proposed to meet the endurance requirements of near-space solar-powered Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV). The system consists of three sets of windings, with each set of windings and its corresponding driver constituting a motor module. One of the motor modules adopts vector control to obtain a set of reference current phases, while the other motor modules adopt a quasi-PR control strategy to track the reference current phase. In this system, the different motor modules can work independently as well as cooperate with each other. The experimental results show that the winding currents of each motor module can ensure phase synchronization, validating the rationality of the MWPMSM control strategy for solar powered UAV and the feasibility of implementing the quasi-PR control strategy.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Swing Suppression Control for Unmanned Multirotor Transportation System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Unmanned multirotors have demonstrated excellent flexibility in complex real-world scenarios, making them promising for aerial payload transportation. However, it is challenging to achieve stable control of the unmanned multirotor transportation system due to its double under-actuated property. Traditional control methods are limited by model complexity and parameter tuning difficulty, resulting in deficient control capabilities. In response to these shortcomings, an end-to-end controller based on deep reinforcement learning is proposed in this article, ensuring that the payload arrives at the target while suppressing the process swing. Based on the Soft Actor Critic (SAC) algorithm and the design of state-action space, the efficiency of the controller is enhanced. By comparing with PID and Fuzzy PID control methods, the proposed approach presents superior payload swing suppression capacity with comparable position control performance.

articleTitle: Design of wireless charging system for underwater robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: 71% of the Earth's surface is covered by water, of which 97% is the ocean. Due to various complex environmental factors such as ocean climate and ocean current disturbances, underwater exploration and inspection technology in the ocean urgently needs to be replaced by underwater robots. Based on the exploration and inspection needs of underwater oceans, underwater robots have advantages such as small size, low danger factor, and suitability for various complex environments. Especially in long-term operations, underwater robots can still maintain high-quality work efficiency. In response to the issue of long-term homework, this article chooses underwater wireless charging technology as the power supply method for underwater robots, aiming to improve their underwater work endurance. This article analyzes and verifies the feasibility of applying wireless charging to the power supply of underwater robots through theoretical derivation, simulation, and experiments. The experimental results show that the application of wireless charging function in underwater robots can conveniently and quickly supplement electrical energy, effectively improving the underwater operation time of underwater robots.

articleTitle: Tunable Low-frequency Sound Absorber via Helmholtz Resonators with Embedded Spiral Tube
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Low-frequency sound waves have the characteristics of long wavelengths, minimal attenuation during propagation, and a tendency to resonate with human organs, causing significant health impacts. To address this issue, a novel type of acoustic metamaterial known as Helmholtz Resonator Embedded Spiral (HRES) acoustic metamaterial is proposed. We first establish the theoretical model of HRES and validate it through numerical simulations. The results show excellent agreement between theoretical predictions and finite element analysis, confirming the absorptive capabilities of HRES at low frequency. The proposed HRES structure not only reduces the thickness of the metamaterial but also significantly enhances tunability of system impedance by introducing additional geometric degrees of freedom. The HRES with deep sub-wavelength thickness (λ/50) achieves perfect sound absorption at 124Hz. With the same thickness of an external Helmholtz cavity, perfect absorption can be obtained in certain frequency in the band from 102Hz to 164Hz via changing the parameters of the embedded spiral. Such capability facilitates the design of broadband sound absorption within the cavity using tunable structures. The research presented in this paper holds potential significance for designing low-frequency, ultra-thin, tunable sound-absorbing materials.

articleTitle: Depression's Effect on Voluntary Facial Mimicry in Adolescents: Insights for Intervention
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Depressed patients have been proven to have deficiencies in their mimicry behavior. This study aims to explore the differences in voluntary facial mimicry behaviors between adolescents with mild or moderate depression and healthy individuals, with the goal of providing insights for the early diagnosis and monitoring of depression. The data include images of eight types of voluntary facial mimicry (VFM) from 10 healthy individuals and 6 patients with depression. Through detailed identification of the participants' facial expressions, this paper further classifies these expressions into three main categories: Positive, Negative, and Surprise, and discusses the differences between these categories. Using a visual analysis approach, the study employs minimized feature extraction from regions of interest (ROI) and validates the effectiveness of pretrained models. The results indicate that while the experimental group showed similar performance to the control group in mimicking happiness expressions, they exhibited significant deficiencies in mimicking anger, fear, and neutral expressions, with an overall accuracy significantly lower than that of the control group. Moreover, although there was no significant difference in the overall accuracy between the control group across the three major categories, there were significant differences in the Positive and Surprise categories when compared to healthy individuals.

articleTitle: A Study of Vertebral Displacement Due to Disc Loading and Its Risks when Using Lumbar Assist Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This paper examines the displacement of the vertebral body caused by the difference in the reduction rate of compression and shear forces on the intervertebral disc, which is suggested by the use of lumbar assist devices, and the risks associated with such displacement. Lumbar assist devices are being developed by various research institutes as a method of assisting workers. Although there are many reports on the effectiveness of lumbar assist devices in terms of performance, there are few reports describing the effects on the spine when the devices are used. Therefore, we calculated the reduction rate of compression force and shear force on the intervertebral disc using a lumbar load evaluation model with a passive-type assist suit, and found that the reduction rate of compression force was greater than that of shear force. In this case, the vertebral body may be displaced significantly in the vertical direction of the vertebral column because the force of the vertebral body holding down the intervertebral disc is weakened. In addition, the vertebral displacement in the shear direction was measured by simultaneously applying compression and shear forces to an animal specimen, and it was shown that the reduction of compression force affects the displacement in the shear direction.

articleTitle: Research on Related Technologies of Multi-needle Die Bonding Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This study aims to improve the solid crystal efficiency of Mini-LEDs by proposing an innovative bonding scheme for a new type of die bonder based on multi-needle technology. Compared with the traditional swing arm die bonder, this new die bonder has significantly improved solid crystal efficiency and precision control. Through the collection and analysis of the position error and angle error of the chips, this study optimized the coverage of the multi-needle design and used a combined branch and bound method and cutting plane method algorithm to plan the solid crystal path. Experimental results show that the multi-needle die bonder can effectively improve the parallel processing capacity of solid crystal operations and significantly improve processing efficiency under certain error requirements. In addition, compared with the traditional single-needle method, the multi-needle technology can significantly reduce the total path length required, thereby further improving work efficiency and reducing costs. This study provides a new technical approach and theoretical support for process optimization in the Mini-LED semiconductor production field.

articleTitle: Research on Seismic Bracing Monitoring System Based on Wireless Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Real-time data acquisition and monitoring of seismic bracings can help to maintain their effectiveness during service life and to improve the seismic resistance and disaster mitigation effects when strong earthquakes occur. In order to monitor real-time states of the seismic bracing, an intelligent monitoring system based on wireless transmission technology was designed. The system used CC2530 Zigbee module to establish a ZigBee wireless LAN, and combined MEMS vibration sensors and strain gauges. Meanwhile, the system used ESP32 to upload the measurement data to OneNET cloud platform through MQTT wireless communication protocol. The function of data visualization was designed so as to realize real-time monitoring of seismic bracing states. The experimental results showed that the proposed wireless monitoring system can reliably execute real-time data collection, storage, display, and hazard warning to guarantee the effectiveness of seismic bracings.

articleTitle: Intelligent compaction quality assessment of vibratory roller using deep neural network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Intelligent compaction technology uses the acceleration signal features of the roller’s vibration drum to assess the compaction quality of the subgrade. Currently, most methods for assessing compaction quality rely on traditional compaction indicators. The existing compaction quality evaluation methods are basically based on intelligent compaction measurement values, however, the compaction quality of subgrade is affected by the interaction of many factors and it is not enough to describe the complex mapping between the drum acceleration signal and the compaction quality by using only a few indicators. This limits the development of intelligent compaction technology. This paper proposes a novel method for assessing subgrade compaction quality based on Gaussian process. A deep neural network is used to extract features from acceleration signals. Based on the features extracted by the network, the Gaussian process is used to accurately evaluate and predict the compaction quality. The results indicate that compared to traditional compaction quality assessment methods, the proposed method significantly improves prediction accuracy, demonstrating clear engineering value for the realization of intelligent subgrade compaction.

articleTitle: Error Calibration Analysis of Long Cantilever Inlet Inspection Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The long cantilever tandem articulated robot has great application prospects in complex curved surface working environments such as aircraft inlet inspection due to its advantages of flexibility and strong obstacle avoidance ability, but it is easy to cause the end position error accumulation. To increase the robot’s precision and decrease end inaccuracy, the robot needs to be calibrated. In this paper, the kinematics calibration method and the neural network calibration method are used to calibrate the long cantilever series articulated robot based on the rotary platform independently designed by the team. Compared with before calibration, the average position errors are reduced to 3.684 mm and 0.304 mm, respectively. It shows that the neural network calibration method has good applicability for this kind of robot.

articleTitle: Method for Enhancing Stability of Tension in Cable-Driven Minimally Invasive Surgical Instruments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This study proposes a method aimed at enhancing the stability of tension in cable-driven minimally invasive surgical instruments. Despite the widespread use of cable-driven instruments due to their lightweight and flexibility, those with hinge joints encounter a significant problem of cable loosening during transmission. This is attributed to the non-circular geometric characteristics of hinge joints, leading to a loss of cable tension during transmission and subsequently compromising the precision at the instrument's end. To tackle this issue, a design solution involving a cam is proposed in this study, aiming to provide a more suitable cable length for hinge joints to reduce cable tension loss. Through a series of analytical procedures and experiments, the method optimizes the mechanical design to mitigate tension fluctuations during surgical procedures. Experimental results demonstrate that adopting the design solution with a cam can improve the stability of cable tension in hinge joints by 71% within a motor rotation angle of 30 degrees. This method offers valuable insights into the development of more reliable surgical instruments for delicate procedures.

articleTitle: A study on gait analysis based on the pose estimation algorithm RTMPose using knee angle as a metric
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Gait analysis can be used to assess a person's fall risk and evaluate the effectiveness of fall prevention training. The knee angle is a crucial metric for assessing gait. This study utilized the markerless lightweight pose estimation algorithm RTMPose to evaluate gait. Firstly, 2D human key point detection was performed based on the video. Then the knee angle change curves during walking and pedaling elliptical machine movement were calculated from the key points for gait analysis. This study analyzed knee angle data from individuals with varying body shapes. The results demonstrated that, compared to OpenPose and YOLOv8, RTMPose can quickly and accurately measure the knee angle and determine the abnormal gait condition. It does not need to wear sensors or rely on special testing environments, which is conducive to objective and effective gait analysis by professional rehabilitation workers.

articleTitle: Lightweight Oracle Bone Character Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv7-tiny
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of difficult recognition caused by the varying scale of oracle characters and the small size of some targets, as well as in order to meet the deployment requirements of application scenarios, a lightweight oracle character detection algorithm based on the improved YOLOv7tiny is proposed. First, Partial Convolution are fused in the model backbone network to reduce the redundant computation and memory footprint of the network model. Second, Asymptotic Feature Pyramid Network (AFPN) is constructed to reduce the problem of detail information loss caused when feature fusion is performed between multiple levels, in order to better capture the features of targets at different scales and enhance the detection of small targets, and reduce model complexity. Finally, a feature fusion network based on the bottleneck residual module is constructed to further reduce the model size and enhance the model deployability, as well as to help the network fuse feature information more efficiently. The experimental results show that the improved model achieved an mAP@0.5 of 90.3%, the number of parameters, computation and model size are reduced by 55.7%, 44.1% and 52.5%, respectively, compared with the base model, and by 75.7%, 74.1% and 74.2% compared to YOLOv8s, respectively. The improved model has been greatly lightweighted and balanced with high accuracy.

articleTitle: Embedded System Design and Implementation of a Humanoid Service Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Humanoid service robots typically possess facial expressions, body movements, and speech communication abilities similar to humans. These capabilities enable them to communicate more naturally with human users and provide various services. Therefore, humanoid robot systems should not only have control systems but also have multi-modal functional systems. The control system needs to address robot joint driving. The modal system needs to implement various modal functions of the robot, such as visual, auditory, natural language processing, etc. This paper proposes a distributed design architecture for a humanoid service robot embedded system, offering a novel approach to building a specific robot platform system. This is achieved through constructing prototypes and conducting experiments on modal functions and body movements.

articleTitle: Parameter Identification and Fault Diagnosis of Servo System Based on Improved PSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The capture of nonlinearity in servo systems during operation is significant for fault diagnosis, which can greatly reduce the probability of system failure throughout the life cycle. To address the problem, a step-by-step identification method based on iterative optimization mutation particle swarm optimization (S-IPV-PSO) is proposed for fault diagnosis. Firstly, an iterative optimization mutation particle swarm optimization (IPV-PSO) is presented to improve convergence speed and algorithm accuracy by optimizing the learning factor and inertia weight coefficient. Secondly, a Hammerstein model is established to identify the parameters for predicting different states of the system by using the IPV-PSO algorithm, where inverse M signal is used as an output to separate between the nonlinear and linear parts of the system. Finally, a servo system simulation with dead time characteristics is built to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively identify fault states and has better convergence speed and recognition error.

Author Keywords: Iterative optimization mutation particle swarm optimization

articleTitle: Active Disturbance Rejection Regulation Control Strategy of Microgrid Load Side Interface Converter Based on TD3 Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: As a new power system structure, microgrid can effectively integrate renewable energy and improve energy utilization efficiency and power quality. In this paper, a linear active disturbance rejection control strategy based on TD3 algorithm is proposed to solve the problem that the DC-DC converter on the load side of microgrid is prone to fluctuation of output voltage caused by disturbance.Through the introduction of deep reinforcement learning strategy, the parameters of the ADRC controller were self-tuning, so that the microgrid could operate stably.The dynamic response characteristics and stability of the system under different operating conditions are compared by simulation. The results show that the stability and disturbance resistance of the control system using TD3-LADRC are better than those of the traditional PI double closed-loop control and LADRC control.

articleTitle: Research on Mechanical Properties of Steel Girth Welds of X80 Pipeline in Service
