publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In order to reduce the failure of circumferential welds of oil pipelines and improve the safety of oil and gas pipelines in China, a series of mechanical properties of circumferential welds of in-service Sino-Myanmar natural gas pipelines were studied, and the tensile bearing test of circumferential welds with cracks was carried out through prefabricated cracks. The results show that the tensile strength, bending resistance and hardness of the girth weld meet the standard requirements. But the impact test results of girth weld center and heat affected zone show that the toughness is poor. In addition, with the increase of defect height, the bearing capacity of the girth welds with defects without fatigue precracking shows a linear decline trend, while the bearing capacity of the girth welds with fatigue precracking shows an accelerated decline trend. With the increase of the simulated crack depth, the failure stress of the small sample with defective girth weld showed a decreasing trend. The tensile strength of the samples without defects is basically higher than the failure stress of the samples with defects. But the impact test results of girth weld center and heat affected zone show that the toughness is poor. In addition, with the increase of defect height, the bearing capacity of the girth welds with defects without fatigue precracking shows a linear decline trend, while the bearing capacity of the girth welds with fatigue precracking shows an accelerated decline trend. With the increase of the simulated crack depth, the failure stress of the small sample with defective girth weld showed a decreasing trend. The tensile strength of the samples without defects is basically higher than the failure stress of the samples with defects.

articleTitle: Safety-Critical Control for Nonholonomic Tractor-Trailer Systems Using Control Barrier Functions and Differential Flatness
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This paper presents a safety-critical control method for nonholonomic tractor-trailer systems subject to safety constraints and physical constraints. Safety is a fundamental issue in autonomous mobile robot design. To ensure the safety of the tractor-trailer system while achieving the control objectives, hard constraints are integrated into Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) to generate a safe set for the tractor-trailer system to avoid obstacles. Furthermore, CBFs are naturally harmonized with Control Lyapunov Functions (CLFs) to design a desired safe trajectory for the system. We optimize the decay rates of the CBFs and CLFs to mitigate the conflict between CBFs and CLFs and improve the obstacle avoidance performance. The concept of differential flatness is used to design and simplify the controller, which enables the system to track the desired safe trajectory. Finally, the effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: A subwavelength absorber with labyrinthine structure and adjustable low-frequency properties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The investigation of sound absorption through metamaterials with deep subwavelength thickness has garnered significant attention in the field of noise control. In this paper, An adjustable low-frequency subwavelength absorber with a labyrinth cavity and embedded aperture is presented, in which the built-in plates is designed to be scalable. The structure enables nearly perfect absorption at a remarkably thin thickness of 12 mm, exhibiting an absorption coefficient of 0.99 at 243 Hz. Notably, the thickness of the designed structure amounts to only 1/117th of the longest operational wavelength. The sound absorption performance is thoroughly examined through both theoretical analyses and numerical simulations using COMSOL. Furthermore, the tunability of the acoustic absorber was analyzed based on the length and size of the aperture as well as the length of the built-in plates. significantly enhancing the system's ability to match impedance. This research may have applications in low-frequency acoustic absorption and offers insights for designing low-frequency acoustic absorbing metamaterials.

articleTitle: A Novel Performance Evaluation and Optimal Design Method for Lower Limb Exoskeleton
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In order to gain a comprehensive understanding of the influence of lower limb exoskeleton (LEE) on human gait characteristics, a human-machine system simulation method combining gait experimentation with AnyBody software simulation was employed. The kinematic parameters and biomechanical parameters of the subjects were collected through the gait experiment. The AnyBody software was employed to construct the human body model and the human-machine system model. A comparative analysis was conducted on the kinematics parameters and biomechanical parameters of the two models. The maximum extension moment of the hip joint was reduced by 0.51 Nm/kg when walking with the LEE. It is evident that the LEE exerts a compensatory effect on the hip joint. The LEE exerts the greatest influence on the muscle strength of the medial gastrocnemius. The muscle with the greatest muscle activation in the lower extremity is the rectus femoris (0.76), which indicates that the LEE is the most likely to cause fatigue or injury to the rectus femoris. The gait characteristics observed during walking with the LEE were consistent with those of a normal gait, indicating that the design of the LEE is reasonable.

articleTitle: Development of a Novel Actuation Mechanism For a Legged Robot With Mono- and Bi-articulated Drive and Parallel Elasticity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Bi-articular actuation in animal legs is a key feature in increasing the stability of the postural control and the toe output. In addition, the parallel elasticity of the mono- and bi-articular muscles increases the toe stiffness and improves the legs’ robustness. In this study, we proposed a novel actuation mechanism for a legged robot, which has mono- and bi-articular drive functions and parallel elasticity inspired by a biological muscle-tendon complexes group. We developed a prototype of one-legged robot equipped with the proposed actuation mechanism. The effectiveness of the parallel elastic mechanisms and mono- and bi-articular drive was validated through forward jumping simulation. The experimental result using the prototype demonstrated the robot achieved forward jumping motion of more than twice its leg length.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Levitation Gap Sensors for High-speed Maglev trains
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The levitation gap sensor is an indispensable component of the high-speed magnetic levitation train system. It relies on nondestructive testing technology to precisely determine the relative position of the suspension system by detecting the long stator cogging structure. In this paper, a new coil structure is proposed based on the molecular current theory and magnetic field mirror method to mitigate the cogging effect, thereby accommodating the reduced size of the stator slot. Additionally, electromagnetic analysis is employed to arrange the two groups of coils in a 90-degree staggered phase to weaken the cogging effect further. The LDC1612 inductive detection chip is utilized to detect and address changes in the detection coil's inductance. Finally, the feasibility of the coil structure is verified through experiments.

articleTitle: Research on Control Strategy of AC/DC Bi-Directional Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: AC/DC bidirectional converters play an important role in the stable operation and coordinated distribution of new power systems, so it is necessary to study the control strategy of AC/DC bidirectional converters. The control strategy of AC/DC bidirectional converter can be categorized into current vector control and voltage control. In this paper, PQ control in current vector control and VF control in voltage control are studied. Simulation models of the two control methods are established to analyze the advantages and disadvantages of the two control methods.

articleTitle: Maximum Deformation Prediction of the Girder of Gantry Crane Based on the Grey Wolf Optimizer-Stacking Ensemble Learning Surrogate Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Maximum deformation of the girder of gantry crane can indicate the health status of the girder. Due to the movable loads, the position of the maximum deformation of the girder is changeable, so that measuring maximum deformation is difficult with limited sensors. Numerical simulation is challenging to achieve real-time monitoring owing to high computational complexity and time-consuming computation. To address the aforementioned problems, this paper proposes a stacking ensemble learning surrogate model (SELSM) to predict the maximum deformation of the girder of gantry crane. Moreover, the grey wolf optimizer (GWO) is used to optimize the parameters of the SELSM (GWO-SELSM). The results of experiment show that the GWO-SELSM outperforms the single surrogate models and existing combination of surrogate models for mean square error (MSE) and R-square (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). The proposed model can be used to accurately predict the maximum deformation of the girder of gantry crane online.

articleTitle: A Relative Optimal Evaluation Algorithm Based on Shipborne Anemometer Layout
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In maritime military activities, the real-time information of sea surface wind field is very important to improve the capability of air and sea cooperation in combat. Accurate wind speed and direction data on the surface of the ship can provide important guarantee information for the takeoff and landing of the shipborne aircraft. The buildings on the ship and the layout of the shipboard anemometer will have an impact on the anemometer measurement results, so it is crucial to study the optimal layout of the shipboard anemometer. In this paper, a relative optimal evaluation algorithm based on shipborne anemometer layout is proposed based on the simulation model established by CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics). Firstly, the correlation between the anemometer and the target anemometer at different positions is used as the main evaluation index, and the average absolute error of the wind direction of the anemometer is combined to obtain the optimal position of the anemometer. Secondly, according to the selected optimal location, eight anemometer layout schemes are proposed. Then, in order to finally arrive at the relatively optimal anemometer layout scheme. The improved multi-sensor fusion algorithm is used as the evaluation method, and the average relative error of wind speed and the average absolute error of wind direction are used as the evaluation criteria. The final results show that the layout of the fifth scheme (four anemometer) is: (0m, 8m, 11.5m), (0m, -8m, 11.5m), (-4.4m, 8m, 11.5m), and (-4.4m, -8m, 11.5m) is the relative optimal layout scheme of the anemometer.

Index Terms: Absolute Value Of The Correlation Coefficient

articleTitle: Lane-Keeping Assistance System Based on Fast Lane Line Detection Network and Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The lane-keeping assistance system is one of the essential active safety technologies for autonomous vehicles. This paper introduces a lane-keeping system based on a fast lane line detection network and model predictive control. A camera is utilized to capture the visual data of the road ahead and analyze it to extract lane lines. Based on this, a model predictive lateral controller is developed to obtain the appropriate steering angle required for lane keeping. A joint simulation using CarSim and Simulink was conducted to verify the feasibility of the lane-keeping system. At low speeds, the lateral deviation of the vehicle when steering is a maximum of 0.2 m. The steering deviation at high speeds does not exceed 0.45 m to ensure the vehicle's stability. The results indicate that the vehicle deploying the lane-keeping assistance system in the paper can drive along the lane center trajectory smoothly and accurately.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Novel Intelligent Acupuncture Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Acupuncture treats systemic diseases through the conduction of meridians and acupoints, and applies certain manipulations. However, acupuncture has problems such as subjectivity in artificial acupoint selection, difficulty in standardizing acupuncture techniques, and poor uncertainty in acupuncture stimulation. With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology and medical robotics industry, acupuncture, a traditional medicine, has ushered in new development opportunities. the model of the needle applying mechanism is constructed, and then the static structure analysis and modal analysis are carried out to verify the rationality, feasibility and reliability of the structural design. Then the model is abstracted into a mathematical model and presented in a modular way, which is encapsulated into a usable simulation module after adding constraints and load conditions as well as contact settings. Finally, the feasibility, rationality and reliability of the established model are visually tested by the open-loop control in the form of waveforms.

articleTitle: A Novel Coupling Amplification Mechanism for Improving Stepping Characteristics of Stick-Slip Piezoelectric Actuators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Piezoelectric actuators, representing prominent products in the realm of small-sized precision actuators, exhibit advantages such as low energy consumption and high output force, coupled with relatively mature technology. However, existing piezoelectric actuators, despite enhancing motion speed through the utilization of one or multiple displacement amplification mechanisms, face a challenge in significantly increasing the stepping displacement, especially in compact spaces and under low-frequency conditions. To address the challenge of limited stepping displacement, this paper proposed a novel coupling amplification mechanism. The coupling amplification effect of two displacement amplification mechanisms can be achieved using only one piezoelectric stack. Subsequently, the excellent displacement amplification effect of the proposed mechanism is demonstrated through pseudo-rigid body and finite element methods. Finally, the proposed flexible hinge mechanism is applied to the actuator design, effectively improving both the stepping displacement and speed.

articleTitle: Research on Low Voltage Ride-through Control of Permanent Magnet Direct Drive Wind Turbine Generators during Grid Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Low voltage ride-through (LVRT) mandates that wind turbines stay connected to the grid during voltage drops. To satisfy the LVRT criteria for permanent magnet direct-drive wind turbines, this paper proposes a control strategy involving an energy-dissipating circuit on the machine-side and reactive power compensation on the grid. The machine-side energy-dissipating circuit, known as the Braking Chopper (BC) circuit, is utilized, while grid-side reactive power compensation employs the Port-Controlled Hamiltonian Algorithm (PCH). When the grid voltage drops, the BC circuit absorbs excess power generated during the fault to maintain stability in the DC bus voltage, while the PCH provides reactive power compensation. Once the grid voltage returns to normal, the BC circuit is disconnected, and the PCH resumes normal grid-connected operation. Using Matlab/Simulink, a simulation model was constructed, and simulations were conducted. The results demonstrate that the control strategy proposed in this paper enables successful LVRT during symmetrical grid faults.

articleTitle: Structure displacement extraction method based on image feature matching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The structural displacement is an important part of the health monitoring of engineering structures. The traditional displacement identification uses wired or wireless measurement systems for data acquisition, the process of arranging sensors and acquisition equipment is tedious and time-consuming. To solve the problem, a non-contact displacement measurement method based on image matching algorithm is proposed to improve the efficiency of structural displacement recognition. Consumer cameras are used as acquisition devices, the improved ORB feature matching technology is used to track the motion of the target feature points and extract the target displacement. The proposed method is applied to the displacement measurement experiment of structural model, and the results are compared with those of traditional ORB algorithm and grating scale displacement sensor. The results of experiment show that the proposed non-contact measurement method based on the improved ORB image matching technology has high measurement accuracy, and can accurately identify the structural displacement characteristics.

articleTitle: Parameter Recognition of Solar Cell Model Based on ICOOT Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Solar cell model parameter recognition is crucial for accurate photovoltaic power generation prediction, necessitating high accuracy in identification. To tackle this challenge, we introduce the refined Chicken Optimization Algorithm (ICOOT), specifically tailored for solar cell model parameter identification. Initially, we validate the algorithm's superiority by comparing it against existing algorithms, followed by further evaluation using measured data from Radiation Tolerant Cell (RTC) solar cells. After comparing it with four alternative methods, the superiority of the introduced ICOOT model is clearly demonstrated. We demonstrate its practical applicability by selecting French RTC silicon solar cells for parameter identification. A comparative analysis, including Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), is conducted against six other models, highlighting the proposed model's lower RMSE and broader applicability.

articleTitle: Design of a Custom Compact Actuator for Pediatric Rehabilitation Exoskeleton Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Reducing the volume and weight of actuators is crucial for exoskeletons designed for children with cerebral palsy. However, few studies have been conducted to develop dedicated actuators for the exoskeletons of children. Most studies have used a combination of commercial motors and reducers, resulting in a lack of integration and making it difficult to meet the requirements for compactness. Therefore, this study explores the design practices of a custom compact actuator for pediatric rehabilitation exoskeletons and presents an actuator with high torque density and control bandwidth. The compactness of the actuator is improved by fully integrating the two-stage reducer into the motor stator. The motor and reducer of the actuator are designed and simulated using finite element analysis to ensure electromagnetic and mechanical reliability. The customized control hardware and control method of the actuator are also presented. Finally, the actuator prototype is subjected to system identification and load-characteristic tests. The experimental results demonstrate that the actuator has the advantages of a small size, high torque density, and good dynamic performance.

articleTitle: Kinematic Analysis and Experimental Research on Parallel Cable-driven Puncture Surgery Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Aiming at the workspace requirements of clinical prostate puncture surgery, this paper deals with the design of a prostate puncture surgery robot based on parallel cable-driven. A parallel cable-driven mechanism is proposed to optimize the compactness of the end-surgical device. Then, to validate the accuracy of motion and the feasibility of the robot, which simulated and analyzed using the Multibody toolbox. Finally, a prototype is designed and experimentally evaluated to validate that the designed parallel cable-driven puncture surgery robot has well motion accuracy and stability in the workspace. In this paper, a puncture surgical robot is designed. Experiments show that the robot can meet the requirements of surgery and has good motion accuracy.

articleTitle: Vision-Integrated Digital Twin for Industrial Manipulator Unloading
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In response to the evolution of industrial manufacturing and the rise of intelligent systems, the demand for real-time simulation and robust performance has become critical. This paper introduces a Vision-Integrated Digital Twin (VIDT) designed for the unloading of industrial manipulators. Initially, the paper elaborates on the VIDT framework, which features a decouplable structure, enhancing its adaptability across various application scenarios. Subsequently, the paper proposes an innovative 3D parcel box pose estimation algorithm. This algorithm, which utilizes an RGB-D camera, advanced deep learning techniques, and primitive geometrics, facilitates real-time vision-guided unloading. The paper concludes with experimental results that validate the efficacy of the proposed pose estimation algorithm and the VIDT.

articleTitle: Parameterized Design of Heavy-duty Serial Industrial Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Heavy-duty robots are widely utilized in diverse automation production lines, requiring structural adjustments to meet diverse task requirements. However, frequent modifications lead to unnecessary labor and decreased efficiency,as changes in linkage dimensions often necessitate the replacement of core components such as motors and reducers, requiring additional design adjustments to preserve adaptability and efficiency. Consequently, this paper presents a parametric design software plugin for heavy-duty robots developed using ZW3D. The plugin integrates parametric design techniques for linkages and joint structures and includes an algorithm for the selection and replacement of motors and reducers. Testing has shown that the plugin effectively modifies linkage dimensions, adjusts joint structures, and replaces motors and reducers, ensuring that a single alteration prompts comprehensive adjustments in accordance with the design principle of “parametric linkage, one change affects all.” This plugin significantly improves design efficiency, reduces the design cycle, and lowers production costs, thereby demonstrating substantial practical value.

articleTitle: Anti-overturning Method of Mobile Manipulator During Obstacle Crossing Based on Coupling Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The structural characteristics of mobile manipulator aggravate the overturning problem in obstacle crossing process, so it is important to study the stability of mobile manipulator in obstacle crossing process. In this paper, the coupling dynamics of tracked mobile manipulator under two obstacle crossing attitudes are studied, and the stability of tracked mobile manipulator is evaluated based on the overturning moment (TOM) theory. In addition, an active anti-overturning method is proposed to compensate the overturning moment of the whole system based on the dynamics of manipulator. Finally, a multi-body dynamic simulation model of the tracked mobile manipulator is established. The simulation results prove that the proposed active anti-overturning method can effectively compensate the overturning moment of mobile manipulator, the proposed method can improve the stability of mobile manipulator during obstacle crossing.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Genetic Algorithm for Rectangular Layout of Defective Plate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Combining the lowest horizontal line algorithm with defect constraints and adaptive genetic algorithm to optimize the layout of rectangular parts with internal defective plates. The adaptive genetic algorithm is used to optimize the arrangement order of rectangular parts. It adaptively adjusts the crossover probability according to the individual fitness value, which can improve the calculation efficiency of the algorithm and avoid falling into the local optimal solution. Based on the lowest horizontal line algorithm with defect constraints, the lowest horizontal line is updated by judging the position of the defect, so that the rectangular part can effectively avoid the defective part during layout. The algorithm is programmed and simulated in the Python environment. Compared with the classic genetic algorithm, the proposed algorithm improves the maximum utilization rate of the board and the stability of layout optimization in the plate layout problem with two different numbers of defects. This shows that the lowest horizontal line algorithm with defect constraints based on the adaptive genetic algorithm has practical application value in the layout problem of defective plates.

articleTitle: DCT-ISTA: A Network Block to Denoise Raw Vibration Signal with Interpretability for Mechanical Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Mechanical fault diagnosis is a crucial task in the field of high-value equipment prognostic and health management. Despite the numerous applications of deep neural networks in this domain, their lack of interpretability hinders their further adoption. In this paper, we propose a novel interpretable network block named DCT-ISTA for the diagnosis of rotating machinery faults, which is obtained by unrolling the classical Iterative Soft Thresholding Algorithm from the compressive sensing field and integrating prior knowledge from the fault diagnosis domain. DCT-ISTA combines sparse coding with Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT), formulated as a network through algorithmic unrolling, and integrates it as a data denoising method with backbone networks to enhance their performance. We validate the proposed method using simulated data with three different backbone networks. Through accuracy evaluation and analysis of signal reconstruction results, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: Influence of Materials on the Transportation Performance of a Self-running Actuator Based on Ultrasonic Levitation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Ultrasonic levitation (UL) technique holds promising application prospects in the field of actuators due to its oil-free operation, compact structure, and ease of control. This study explores the transportation performance capabilities of a self-running, non-contact actuator utilizing the UL principle, focusing on performance evaluation and material optimization. Initially, the distribution of vibration amplitude was determined using the Finite Element Method (FEM), facilitating the estimation of film thickness. Subsequently, governing equations pertaining to squeeze film pressure were formulated. Incorporating the film thickness and governing equations, air film pressure distribution was ascertained through the Finite Difference Method (FDM). The levitation and driving forces were then calculated based on the force analysis. Furthermore, this paper delves into the impact of the actuator's material on its transportation efficiency. Prediction results show that aluminum yields a higher driving force than titanium at the same input voltage, but titanium surpasses aluminum in generating propulsive force at equivalent amplitude levels. This investigation underscores the significance of material selection in enhancing the performance of UL-based actuators.

articleTitle: Research on The Modeling of The Dispatching System of Forging Workshop and The Scheduling Method of Thermal Connection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In this paper, the thermal connection problem in the production scheduling of forging workshop is studied, and an optimization algorithm is proposed. First of all, we established a mathematical model of the production scheduling of the forging workshop, taking into account the thermal connection between the processes, as well as practical factors such as resource constraints. Then, combined with the genetic algorithm and the tabu search algorithm, an optimization algorithm that meets the needs was designed, and the optimization method achieved the goal of improving equipment efficiency and reducing energy consumption through case verification. This study has certain theoretical guiding significance and practical application significance for optimizing the production scheduling and improving the production efficiency of the forging workshop.

articleTitle: Design of Three-Phase Fully Controlled Type Rectifier Controller for Electrolytic Hydrogen Production System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In recent years, the rectifier technology has developed rapidly, the working index has been improved, the process characteristics are becoming more and more mature, and it has been widely used in many fields. In order to better cope with the volatility and instability of offshore wind-photovoltaic power coupled hydrogen production. In this paper, Clack transform, Park transform and Anti-Park transform are used to transform the coordinate system in the model establishment to achieve the experimental conditions required by the simulation. The Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation (SVPWM) algorithm is used to realize the efficient control of the system. The Proportional-Integral-Differential (PID) control method based on voltage outer loop and current inner loop is adopted. At the same time, LLCL filter with better filtering effect is selected and the model of three-phase full-control rectifier circuit proposed in this paper is built and simulated based on MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: A Novel Vascular Interventional Robot for Cardiac Ablation Surgery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In recent years, force sensing and drive control at the distal end of ablation catheters have attracted widespread interest from scholars around the world. Among them, the challenge of high-precision operation of ablation catheters has attracted much attention. To address this problem, this study proposes a non-fixed modular ablation catheter clamping and pushing mechanism. The mechanism is based on a non-fixed modular design, aiming to avoid common under-clamping sliding errors in catheter operations, and achieves effective separation of the robot body and surgical instruments, allowing the ablation catheter to be quickly replaced and asynchronously sterilized. In addition, we conducted a modal analysis of the clamp-push structure, and the results showed that the modal frequency of the clamp-push structure is very low, so the catheter is not susceptible to the resonance effect of external excitation when it is pushed. This innovative design aims to further improve the accuracy, safety and intelligence of the vascular interventional surgical robot, providing reliable support for the success rate and safety of ablation surgery.

articleTitle: Motion Planning for Steam Generator Tube Sheet Quadruped Maintenance Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The steam generator tube sheet quadruped maintenance robot is a novel mobile robot designed for the inspection of steam generator heat transfer tubes. This paper presents a motion planning method for this type of robot. The trajectory of the robot's base is planned through kinematic solutions search. Additionally, a foothold motion evaluation system is established using the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution algorithm to plan the movement of foothold points. For a given motion path, our proposed method divides the path into multiple straight-line segments, and then performs separate planning for turning foothold points and straight-line foothold points. The experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm is adaptable to steam generator tube sheets and performs well in environments with obstacles since the algorithm proposed has a planning success rate of 100% for the tube sheet robot. The experiments validate the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Thermal Stability Analysis of SiC MOSFET Power Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: SiC MOSFETs, as high-performance power devices with high breakdown field strength and high operating temperature, hold broad prospects in the field of power electronics. Addressing the heat dissipation issue of a specific controller, this study investigates the steady-state temperature under the condition where the thermal power consumption of a single SiC MOSFET is 200W. By simplifying the model of a single SiC MOSFET in COMSOL Multiphysics software, the complexity of simulation boundary conditions and mesh division is reduced. The finite element method (FEM) is used to obtain a relatively accurate steady-state temperature. With the establishment of appropriate cooling methods, the requirement for a steady-state temperature of 100°C is satisfied. The results of simulation also indicate that larger chip distances, solder materials with better thermal properties and thinner thickness, as well as increased substrate thickness, can effectively suppress the steady-state temperature.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Guided Single-Cell Encapsulation through photo-crosslinking for Advanced 3D Culture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Encapsulating single cells in hydrogels provides them with a relatively autonomous and controllable three-dimensional extracellular environment. This environment can facilitate cell interaction and proliferation, making it highly valuable in fields such as tissue engineering and single-cell research. However, traditional methods of single-cell encapsulation encounter limitations in terms of single-cell encapsulation rate and topography control, which hinder of the progress of single-cell encapsulation research. In this paper, we propose a novel method for printing microgel-encapsulated single cells using deep learning-guided DLP printing. By leveraging deep learning algorithms, we accurately capture and translate the real-time positional data of single cells into the printing system’s coordinate framework. Based on the single-cell positional information, a virtual digital mask is created via the OpenCV algorithm, which is then input into the digital microscope to complete the single-cell encapsulation. The single-cell encapsulation rate achieved by this method is 86.3%, which is about 2.87 times higher than that of the traditional method. Experimental results show that our method achieves high accuracy in single-cell encapsulation and the fabrication of microgels with arbitrary shapes, which hold significant importance for biological and medical applications.

articleTitle: Improved Euclidean Clustering and Segmentation Algorithm for Workpiece Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Robots with binocular vision often use template matching to identify the parts to be processed, which requires segmentation of the original point cloud data to obtain a separate target point cloud. The original point cloud has the characteristics of unstructured, dense and remote, and the traditional Euclidean clustering algorithm directly acting on the 3D point cloud has the problem of low segmentation accuracy, and the accurate segmentation of the point cloud target has always been a difficult problem in target detection. In this paper, an improved Euclidean clustering algorithm is proposed, under the constraint that the traditional Euclidean clustering segmentation only considers the Euclidean distance, the voxelized grid method is used to achieve downsampling of the point cloud data, and then the normal vector angle constraint is added, which can effectively improve the problem of low segmentation accuracy of the traditional Euclidean clustering algorithm, and also achieves good results in the actual production process after testing and verification of the public dataset.

articleTitle: FAT-based Immersion and Invariance Adaptive Control for Rigid Body Attitude
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: For the presence of various uncertainties in rigid-body systems, a function approximation technique (FAT) based immersion and invariance (I&I) adaptive control method is proposed for rigid body attitude control in this paper. The system model’s uncertainty terms are aggregated into external disturbances and parameterised using a set of weighted selected basis functions, the weights of these functions are estimated using the immersion and invariance method. Based on the proposed method, a control law based on terminal sliding mode is designed, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through stability analysis. Finally, the feasibility of the method is demonstrated through simulations of rigid body attitude under various uncertainties, and it can be effectively applied in the attitude control of rigid body such as vehicles, spacecraft and robotic arms.

articleTitle: Design of an active suspension mechanism for obstacle traversal of in-pipe robots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The installation and usage of pipelines within modern buildings are increasingly common, rust removal and internal exploration of these pipelines have become highly demanding robotic tasks. However, robots often encounter issues such as getting stuck due to obstacles or slipping on the surface of the pipes due to insufficient friction. This paper introduces a pipeline inspection robot designed for application in nuclear power plants. The robot can change its shape according to the size of the pipe and use high-pressure water to remove rust. The robot has a passable diameter range of 600-800mm, demonstrating strong adaptability. By incorporating an active suspension mechanism, the pressure between the wheels and the pipeline can be adjusted during climbing, while ensuring conformity between the wheels and the pipeline surface when crossing obstacles. This effectively addresses the slipping issue encountered by pipeline robots. Through simulation experiments and analysis, we have demonstrated the feasibility of this mechanism, which exhibits outstanding mobility compared to existing robots.

articleTitle: Research on selective harmonic elimination technology based on enhanced whale optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The key of inverter selective harmonic elimination technology lies in solving nonlinear transcendental equations. This paper takes a two-level three-phase bridge inverter circuit as an example, establishes its mathematical model from its output voltage, then constructs an evaluation function, and verifies the feasibility of the enhanced whale optimization algorithm in a selective harmonic elimination technology through MATLAB/Simulink simulation. At the same time, the simulation results also show that the DC voltage utilization rate of the three- phase inverter controlled by the selective harmonic elimination technology based on the enhanced whale optimization algorithm can reach 1.063, which is superior to the traditional Newton iterative method and SPWM technology in DC voltage utilization rate and harmonic elimination efficiency.

articleTitle: MicroWorm: The Design, Optimization, and Control of a Modular Sub-15 Millimeter Earthworm-Inspired Robot for the Navigation of Various Terrains
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This paper presents the design, optimization, and a novel feedback control loop for the first 14 mm diameter modular pneumatic soft robot that locomotes in multiple terrains by mimicking an earthworm’s motion and mechanics. This paper demonstrates two prototypes of sub-15 mm earthworm robots: The Type A robot that uses a peristaltic gait and the Type B robot that uses an anchoring gait. The validity of the proposed design will be tested through linear locomotion on three terrains: rough, smooth, and pipe. The Type A robot achieved a speed of 1.25 mm/s in a flat terrain and the Type B robot achieved a speed of 1.875 mm/s in a pipeline terrain. The robot consists of actuator modules that emulate earthworm muscles and setae through a Pneumatic Artificial Muscle (PAM)-based Elongation Module and a Radial Expansion Module (REM). Through component testing, each materially optimized Elongation Module achieved a force output of 1.68 N and 10.3% contraction. The Radial Expansion Module was able to exert up to 2.45 N of drag force, achieving a power density of 0.106 N/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. By adopting the peristaltic gait of an earthworm, this paper also proposes a new feedback control loop that optimizes the peristaltic gait by reducing cycle times. The robot has potential applications in exploring the complex and narrow environments in infrastructure collapse and sub-15 mm infrastructure inspection beyond just pipeline inspection. Furthermore, the compliant nature of the robot allows for safe human-robot interaction. It can also be applied to biomedical engineering, exploring narrow human intestines and minimally invasive surgery.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based Skill Acquisition Study for Linearly Heated Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: With the development of science and technology, the manufacturing industry is undergoing a quiet transformation, with artificial intelligence and intelligent robots gradually entering the smart manufacturing. Currently, the traditional shipboard manufacturing industry is undergoing a baptism of robotics and ushering in profound changes to meet the growing demand for productivity, quality and safety. However, traditional industrial robots are limited to preprogrammed movements and lack the ability to perform multiskilled tasks. In particular, programming industrial robots for complex hull steel plate machining processes, especially multipass machining, is challenging. In order to allow the robot to learn skills like a human apprentice, it can learn the skills related to linear heating of ship plates from experienced workers and make autonomous judgments to complete the hull steel plate machining according to the requirements. This study focuses on enabling machines to acquire workers' skills and plan heating lines for ship hull steel plates. We achieve this through demonstrative learning and maximum gradient-based reinforcement learning. It can be seen through data simulation and experiments that the linear heating robot in this study achieves 83.26% accuracy in planning the heating line. This not only provides support for workers in the complex linear heating process, but also further improves workers' operational efficiency and economic benefits.

articleTitle: Simulator and Transplantable Control Architecture Development for an Electric Autonomous Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Developing autonomous vehicles requires a strong emphasis on safety-critical tasks. An effective approach for this challenge is to create a simulator with precise vehicle parameters. This allows control algorithms to be safely developed and tested in a virtual environment, leading to a shorter development period. This paper proposes the procedure for developing a simulator for an autonomous vehicle in ROS Gazebo. System identification based on Dynamic Mode Decomposition with Control (DMDc) is conducted for vehicle parameter characterization. A controller framework is proposed with swappable control algorithms and control targets among simulators and real vehicles. The simulator’s and real vehicle’s behavior triggered by the same control input is compared for simulator effectiveness and accuracy validation. Different control algorithms are applied to vehicle GNSS-INS based navigation development. The demo video can be found at: https://youtu.be/S_OjyMRzqWk

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach to Movement Intention Estimation Using Rollator-user Interaction Force
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Rollators have gained popularity as rehabilitation and assistive robots due to their simplicity and compact size. Equipped with sensors and actuators, robotic rollators can provide guidance, assistance, and rehabilitation training during walking. However, existing assistance and training primarily support straight walking, presenting a challenge in providing intuitive assistance during turns. This research introduces an approach for predicting user intention during walking solely using the interaction force between the rollator and the user. A Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network-based machine learning method is proposed for establishing a movement intention model, accurately estimating the intentions of “Straight Walk”, “Turn Left” and “Turn Right”. Experimental results with elderly participants demonstrated a high accuracy of 92.85% in estimating movement intentions.

articleTitle: Review on Development Status, Challenges and Development Trends of Surgical Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Surgical robots are an important branch of medical robots. This paper analyzes the current development status of surgical robots from the perspective of application field classification, summarizes the challenges of various surgical robots such as laparoscopic surgical robots, orthopedic surgical robots, vascular intervention surgical robots, natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (NOTES), and other specialized surgical robots, and predicts and prospects the future development of surgical robots, which provides intelligent support for domestic companies to develop the surgical robot industry. The research results indicate that surgical robot technology is in a period of rapid development, which has helped improve surgical accuracy and treatment effectiveness.

articleTitle: Image Dehazing Method Based on Diffusion Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In this paper, we design a distribution transformation-based method for accelerating image dehaze for diffusion models. The distribution transformation architecture solves the problem of blind transformation of the distribution of the diffusion model during image dehaze processing by providing additional constraints for the model. The efficient use of the dual network structure in the model inference process is achieved through a redesigned fusion sampling method. Meanwhile, in order to ensure the consistency of the output data distribution, the data are distribution normalised after each fusion sampling. The accelerated sampling strategy proposed in this paper optimises the network structure employed by the model and effectively reduces the computational burden of the model, while maintaining the image quality and improving the inference efficiency. Experiments on multiple synthetic and real foggy image datasets show that the network structure proposed in this paper significantly improves the inference speed of the model and achieves a good dehaze effect, with clear details and thorough fog removal in the dehazed image, which effectively restores the background information and the real colours of the image.

articleTitle: A Clamping Perception System Based on Multi-source Sensors for Amphibious Spherical Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Robots replacing divers to collect and search underwater is a widely concerned field at present. In order to enable the robot to better complete the grasping task underwater, building a grasp perception system suitable for the robot is helpful for the robot to complete the autonomous grasping task. This paper presents a grasp perception system based on an amphibious robot platform. This system mainly uses four kinds of sensors. They are IMU, pressure sensor, binocular camera, and ultrasonic distance sensor. In order to control the robot to maintain the balance posture in grasping, we combine the data of IMU and pressure sensor, so that the robot can get more posture information. The accurate relative position information between the robot and the target is obtained in real time by fusing the data of binocular camera and ultrasonic ranging. Underwater experiments showed that the robot had good perception ability.

articleTitle: Curve Parametric Modeling of Planar Soft Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Soft robots, due to their flexibility, adaptability, and gentle handling over rigid robots, have shown better potential in numerous applications requiring operating in constrained spaces. Most of the soft robotic prototypes are of a linear form that can be modeled as a curve in space and are found in manipulators and limbs of locomoting robots. Planar soft robots have been proposed recently that are modeled as a surface and deform in 3D. Research on planar soft robots has been less extensive due to the challenges associated with modeling surface deformations efficiently. We present a curve-parametric approach for the deformation modeling of planar soft robot modules. Along with the Bezier patch method to approximate the surface at 30 Hz. Experimental evaluations on a prototype were developed and tested to validate that the proposed model can reasonably approximate the planar robot boundaries and the surface derived from it.

articleTitle: Two-stage detection algorithm of train key bolts based on YOLO and Faster R-CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: With the development of economy, subway trains have become the first choice for most people to travel. Bolts play an important role in connecting subway trains, so rapid detection of bolt loosening and falling off is a very forced problem to be solved. In the field of computer vision, small target recognition has always been considered one of the most challenging problems. Based on Faster R-CNN and YOLOv8, a two-stage algorithm named JY-YOLO algorithm is proposed in this paper. In the first phase of the algorithm, Faster R-CNN has used the input images of any size of subway to locate and segment the key areas where the bolts are located -Axle Box Cover and Shock Absorber. The segmented image will be fed into the second stage neural network FasterYOLO ResBlock_CBAM in different channels to accurately locate the location of the bolt and detect whether it falls off or becomes loose. The accuracy of the algorithm for each item is more than 98.9%, and it can accurately locate the bolt fault.

articleTitle: Backstepping Sliding Mode Control of Underactuated Unmanned Surface Vehicle Based on Finite Time Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Addressing the challenge of the unmanned ship's susceptibility to external environmental disturbances and the impact of model parameter uncertainty on its control system is paramount. Herein, leveraging the motion characteristics of the unmanned vessel, we establish both its kinematic and dynamic models for a three-degree-of-freedom underactuated system. A finite-time observer-based backstepping sliding mode control approach is crafted to anticipate model uncertainties and environmental perturbations. Incorporating the LOS (line-of-sight) guidance law into the controller design aims to mitigate controller input chatter and enhance convergence speed and tracking precision. Furthermore, a first-order filter signal is employed as a substitute for the virtual control law, thereby circumventing differential explosions triggered by its derivative. Validation of the control algorithm's feasibility and practicality is achieved through rigorous simulation experiments.

Author Keywords: LOS line of sight guidance law

articleTitle: Research on Segmentation and Clustering Algorithms of 3D Point Clouds for Mobile Robot Navigation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The segmentation and clustering of 3D point clouds play a pivotal role in the navigation of mobile robots. In this study, algorithms for segmenting and clustering 3D point clouds were investigated to enhance the navigation capabilities of mobile robots. Firstly, the algorithm proposed by Himmelsbach based on line-fit is widely used in 3D point clouds segmentation. However, the original method has the problem of under segmentation. Therefore, an improved algorithm combining line-fit, noise removal and non-uniform partition method based on Concentric Zone Model was proposed to solve the above problem. Secondly, Euclidean clustering is a commonly used obstacle clustering algorithm, but it is difficult to determine the appropriate distance threshold, which requires a considerable amount of time to adjust the parameter to achieve satisfactory clustering results. A new approach to determine a reasonable distance threshold and prevent excessive clustering was proposed in this paper. Finally, the results of segmentation and clustering experiments showed that our improved segmentation algorithm has higher accuracy and segmentation speed, and our improved Euclidean clustering algorithm has better clustering performance and convenience of threshold parameter setting compared to the original algorithms.

articleTitle: High Precision Portable Bioimpedance Spectrometer for Enhanced Clinical Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) serves as a pivotal non-invasive technique to evaluate both physiological and pathological states of human tissues. Traditional devices often fall short due to poor frequency resolution and phase accuracy, limiting their clinical utility. Addressing these deficiencies, this study introduces a portable, high-precision bioimpedance spectrometer that markedly enhances these crucial metrics. The device employs a Direct Digital Synthesis (DDS) chip, generating signals from 10 kHz to 1 MHz, and features integrated IQ demodulation paired with a 24-bit high-precision analog-to-digital converter (ADC). This setup enables the capture of detailed amplitude and phase information across a wide frequency spectrum. Augmented by a custom-designed band-pass filter and controlled via a STM32F407 microcontroller, the spectrometer improves signal quality and supports real-time data processing and interaction. Demonstrating over 95% accuracy in fixed frequency output mode, the spectrometer provides precise delineation of human tissue bioimpedance, capturing critical amplitude and phase data essential for comprehensive clinical analysis. These technological advancements not only refine the capabilities of bioimpedance measurement tools but also significantly broaden their practical applications within the healthcare sector.

articleTitle: Development of a sEMG-Controlled Portable Exoskeleton System for Home-based Upper Limb Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: As the aging population increases, the number of patients with upper limb hemiplegia is also increasing year by year. The robot-assisted elbow rehabilitation in improving upper limb function abilities in sub-acute hemiplegic patients is promising. In this paper, a surface electromyography (sEMG)-controlled portable robotic system for home-based upper limb rehabilitation is designed. According to the structural parameters of human body, a gear-driven wearable upper limb exoskeleton is designed and analyzed. The sEMG signal is adopted as the control signal to realize the natural and smooth human–robot interaction. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed system, the passive training experiment and the sEMG-based bilateral training experiment are carried out respectively, which also shows the feasibility of the proposed rehabilitation system in assisting the movements of the affected upper limb.

articleTitle: A Single-arm Mode for Operating Steering Wheel in Robot Driving
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: To deal with the incompatibility of efficiency and versatility in steering wheel operation in robot driving task, this paper proposes a single-arm mode for versatile and efficient steering wheel operation. In order to identify the applicable mode in operating the steering wheel, the steering wheel operations of the humanoid arm under the grasping modes and pressing mode are compared by referring to the modes of human single-arm operation. In the comparison, a quadratic programming (QP) problem integrated with the collision-free control is constructed. The pressing mode is proved to be applicable by comparison, which is versatile and able to realize the efficient steering wheel operation. In the implementation, the control strategy is divided into three steps of identification, pressing and turning. The strategy is committed to the accurate trajectory and pressure in the operation. In the experiment, the humanoid robot completed the anthropomorphic operation of the steering wheel that is close to the human level. The effectiveness of the pressing mode and the control strategy for this mode is assessed.

articleTitle: Electrode Deviation Evaluation of sEMG during Wrist Motion Classification using SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: With the escalating aging population, the number of individuals suffering from upper limb hemiplegia is steadily rising each year. The upper limb rehabilitation robot plays a vital role in solving the above problems. As an essential bioelectrical signal, Surface Electromyography (sEMG) is widely used in rehabilitation training. However, in practical applications, the deviation of sEMG electrodes often has a bad effect on the accuracy of signal acquisition. The focus of this paper is to delve into the impact of sEMG electrode deviation on signal acquisition and to propose a viable solution strategy. We collected the standard signals and the signals of electrode deviation, respectively, and fused the data. Specifically, we used the Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm to address the issues caused by electrode deviation. The experimental results show that the SVM algorithm effectively solves the errors caused by sEMG electrode deviation in classification problems.

articleTitle: Bias-compensated Pseudolinear Kalman Filter for Acoustic Sensor Tracking with Colored Measurement Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The bias-compensated pseudolinear Kalman filter (BC-PLKF) has the advantages of closed form and low computational complexity for bearing-only target tracking. However, it is challenging to directly apply it to acoustic tracking with colored measurement noise. First, in acoustic tracking, the unknown propagation delay included in measurement is highly coupled with the target state, preventing the bearing measurements from being represented as pseudolinear measurement equations. Second, the augmented process noise is correlated with the measurement matrix that includes an unknown delay. In this paper, a recursive BC-PLKF algorithm for delayed measurement with colored noise (BC-PLKF-DC), using a two-stage estimator is proposed. The first stage employs colored noise augmented BC-PLKF (BC-PLKF-C) by neglecting delay to produce a coarse estimate. The second stage estimates the target state considering the effects caused by the delayed measurements. In this stage, a new pseudolinear measurement model with a special measurement error is built by approximating delay time as a linear function using the first stage estimate. But when the colored measurement noise is augmented onto the target state, the new bias arises from two sources. Then a new bias estimate is obtained, and we develop the closed-form BC-PLKF-DC algorithm by compensating the bias for the PLKF estimate. Illustrative examples demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms BC-PLKF and BC-PLKF-C.

articleTitle: A Pneumatic Soft End-effector with multiple Grasping modes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In recent years, research on soft end effectors has attracted considerable attention due to their high flexibility, good security and adaptability to unstructured environments. Among them, soft pneumatic actuators exhibit advantages such as easy manufacturing, high extensibility, and high adaptability. This study combines soft pneumatic actuators with motor drive to achieve a switching between internal and external grasping modes and adjustment of grasping space, enhancing the adaptability of soft end-effector to different grasping conditions. In the design process of the soft pneumatic actuators, a method for material parameter identification for finite element analysis is proposed, followed by optimization of the effector design parameters. This study has a certain reference value in the design of multi-mode soft end-actuators.

articleTitle: A Control Method for Assisted Stair Climbing Exoskeleton Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Aiming at the demand of assisting power during stair climbing in human attachment, a control strategy of active assisting power in support phase and passive following in swing phase based on force feedback is proposed according to the structural characteristics of lower limb exoskeleton robot. Based on the human-robot interaction force information, a PID control algorithm is applied to realize the passive following control of the swing phase. Aiming at the requirements of the active assist of the support phase on the joint angle and the size of the assist, a composite control method with PID control as the outer loop and sliding mode control as the inner loop is proposed. In order to solve the sliding mode vibration problem, the equivalent sliding mode control algorithm is used, and the sign function in it is replaced by the saturation function. On this basis, the experimental system was built and the experimental study was completed, and the experimental results show that the proposed method can reduce the energy consumption during the human weight-bearing staircase.

articleTitle: Generating Synthetic X-ray Image Methods for Vascular Interventional Surgery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The scarcity and difficulty in acquiring vascular interventional surgery data have hindered the development of this field. To address this challenge, we propose a novel application of the Deep Digitally Reconstructed Radiographs(DeepDRR) method for synthesizing X-ray images of vascular interventional surgery with guidewires. By merging predefined-shaped guidewires with computed tomography(CT) scan images, composite CT images containing guidewires can be obtained. The DeepDRR model is then used to project these images, producing corresponding X-ray images. Experimental results demonstrate that the synthesized X-ray images with guidewires possess a certain degree of realism and can be generated at a relatively fast speed, achieving 2.69 frames per second (FPS). This study establishes a pipeline for synthesizing vascular interventional images, laying a foundation for future research. This will provide high-quality and diverse data support for the development of vascular interventional surgery robots and promote further advancements in this field.

articleTitle: Centimeter-Scale Submarine Robot for Monitoring Coral Reef Ecosystem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Monitoring coral reef ecosystem is of great importance for assessing their health and promoting conservation efforts to protect these valuable and vulnerable ecosystems. Underwater robots provide a feasible approach for long-term monitoring due to their compact size for navigating through narrow passages. However, existing underwater robots face limitations due to their large size, preventing them from entering narrow coral reef caves to gather information. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a highly integrated propeller- driven centimeter-scale submarine robot with a length of 4.4 cm for monitoring coral reef ecosystem. There are two propellers on two sides of the robot, facilitating lift motion, while an additional two propellers are mounted at the tail to enable forward propulsion and turning maneuvers. This robot can realize three degrees of freedom movement, such as circular motion at specific heights or cruising in a spiral paths under the control of external infrared signals. A kinematic and dynamic model is formulated to develop the control strategy. For object monitoring by the proposed submarine robot, distance and displacement measurement algorithms are developed based on a monocular camera. These algorithms have been experimentally evaluated, demonstrating a calculation error of less than 5%.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Linguistic Style between AI Chatbot and Human in Chinese Civil Servant Interview
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Structured interviews are a crucial method for talent selection, tailored to the specific requirements of a job and the competencies of candidates. These interviews are conducted using a set protocol, with standardized questions and evaluations designed to determine a candidate's suitability. In China, civil service exams commonly employ this method to assess candidates' behavioral strategies in public service roles. The performance of AI in such tasks could significantly indicate its potential to assume responsibilities traditionally held by civil servants. In this study, we utilized a lexical analysis approach based on corpus research to compare the vocabulary characteristics used by an AI chatbot (Large Language Model, GLM-4) and human experts in structured interview training. This comparison focused on their responses to simulated questions from civil service examinations. Our preliminary findings highlight distinct linguistic differences in word usage, thematic keywords, and readability between the human experts and the GLM-4 bot. This research not only examines the role of AI in enhancing interview training skills but also explores the wider implications of integrating AI into public administration. The insights gained could inform future strategies on the incorporation of AI technologies in public sector operations, potentially transforming aspects of state governance.

articleTitle: Research on Emotional Cognition of Game Players Based on Functional Brain Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: EEG emotion recognition based on audio and video stimulation has made some progress, but there are few researches on EEG emotion recognition based on video game stimulation. Video games, due to their high interactivity, can be an effective emotion recognition tool. Therefore, this paper uses four types of games that represent 4 different emotions (high arousal positive valence, high arousal negative valence, low arousal positive valence, low arousal negative valence) and collects the EEG signals of 15 subjects during the game. For EEG feature extraction, this paper extracted five functional brain network features, namely Pearson correlation coefficient, phase-lock value, phase lag index, Granger causality and mutual information. The results show that the combination of CNN model and the phase-locked value feature of beta band has the best classification effect, and the average accuracy of each subject is reached 93.86%. In addition, it is found through visualization that the emotion-generating regions based on video games are mainly concentrated in the frontal and occipital lobes of the brain.

articleTitle: Enhancing Moving Object Segmentation with Spatio-Temporal Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Sensing moving objects accurately can provide information about dynamic changes in the environment, while further segmentation can help autonomous systems make smarter decisions and better SLAM. Effective utilization of spatio-temporal information is paramount for LiDAR Moving Object Segmentation (LiDAR-MOS). We propose an efficient approach for attaining more accurate point cloud segmentation results by leveraging spatio-temporal information from multiple LiDAR scans and their corresponding poses. To be specific, using acquired pose information, we initially transform the point cloud data of the sequence into the coordinate system of the current frame. The aligned point clouds are then discretized to generate a special BEV-occupied representation. Subsequently, we employ a Spatio-Temporal Excitation (STE) module excite the spatio-temporal features of the superimposed representations and put into the spatio-temporal pyramid network (STPN) for dual-head decoding and result fusion. We trained and evaluated our network on the nuScenes dataset. The results of comparative and ablation studies demonstrate the advantage of our designed method.

articleTitle: Research on Noise Reduction Algorithm for Nonlinear Ultrasonic Testing of Microcracks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This study provides a more efficient signal denoising algorithm for nonlinear ultrasonic testing of coarse-grained materials in the future. This article employs numerical simulation techniques to examine the impact of structural noise and Gaussian white noise on ultrasound received wave signals, alongside evaluating various signal denoising algorithms. Through nonlinear ultrasonic testing experiments conducted on aluminum alloy plates containing microcracks of varying sizes and employing relative nonlinear coefficients for characterization, the acquired signals underwent processing using signal denoising algorithms. A comparative analysis of the denoising efficacy of different algorithms was performed based on the processing outcomes. This research contributes to the advancement of more effective signal denoising algorithms for nonlinear ultrasonic testing of coarse-grained materials in the future.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Secure Communication Method Based on P2P for Remote Robotic Surgery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Remote surgery has the advantages of breaking geographical restrictions, shortening the time for patients to see a doctor, and strong scalability. However, compared with conventional local robot-assisted surgery, remote robotic surgery has many problems such as data transmission delay, data transmission reliability and security, which may cause surgical risks. This research studies the remote safe communication method of surgical robot with the self-developed master-slave "intra renal interventional diagnosis and treatment robot" as the object. First of all, in view of the data communication requirements of remote surgical robots and the working characteristics of the master-slave robot system, the problems in the data transmission process of remote surgical robots are fully analyzed and studied. Secondly, in order to meet the requirement mentioned above, the communication system of the remote surgical robot is designed and researched, the server is built to realize UDP hole piercing and server transfer scheme, the P2P communication mode is designed for end-to-end direct connection and the method of data verification and data encryption is studied. Finally, for the communication system designed in this study, with the self-developed master-slave "intrarenal interventional diagnosis and treatment robot" as the carrier, relevant model experiments were carried out to verify the remote operability of the developed communication system.

articleTitle: The Harmonic Optimization of High-Power Converter Based on The LLCL Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: A T-type three-level bidirectional converter based on the LLCL filter was constructed using transformer integrated filtering technology. The dual closed loop control is designed using the grid voltage vector-oriented control strategy, and the principle of controller parameter design based on the LLCL filter model is discussed. Low-order harmonic amplification occurs due to the presence of the ripple current and deadband. The transmission relations of harmonic components in the control loop are analyzed to find out the paths to suppress the lower order harmonics of grid side currents. Quasi-proportional resonance (Q-PR) controller and the second-order bandstop filter were used to remove the introduction of harmonic content in the control loop, effectively filtering out the pulsating voltage of the DC-side voltage without affecting the dynamic performance of the control system and improving the quality of transmitted power.

articleTitle: Bubbles-Swarm Micro Surface Robots for Underwater Inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Manual inspection of underwater facilities, such as those used to store spent fuel or fish farming, is costly and labour-intensive. Therefore, autonomous robots can significantly assist in continuously monitoring these facilities. A swarm robotic system will be more efficient and cost-effective than traditional underwater inspection techniques and expensive remotely operated vehicles. This paper introduces a new swarm robotic platform, Bubble, that can move on water surfaces for underwater inspections. It is a low-cost and open-source micro-robot that enables inspection of extensive underwater facilities, e.g., fuel storage ponds and similar environments, using hundreds of Bubbles. In this work, we used six real robots to implement a swarm exploration for visually inspecting a simulated fuel storage facility. Several scenarios were conducted to test the robots' functionality and collective motion performance. The overall result demonstrated the vast potential for applying Bubbles in various applications.

articleTitle: Modeling and Design of Dynamic Series-parallel Hybrid Lower-limb Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Humanoid robots are required to exhibit exceptional dynamic motion capabilities, particularly in the lower extremities, while undertaking repetitive, high-intensity, or high-risk tasks in human environments. However, the intricate lower limb structure and high limb mass ratio give rise to substantial errors when relying on reduced-order models. This research presents a novel evaluation methodology that effectively analyzes the mechanical properties of lower limb structures during the design phase. This methodology facilitates early detection and optimization of structural issues, thereby enhancing the motion performance and stability of humanoid robots. Furthermore, a novel design approach for the lower limb structure is proposed, employing a series-parallel coupling multistage transmission structure. This design enables the attainment of a compact overall structure and robust power output by integrating the drive structure of the knee and ankle into the thigh and pelvis. Finally, the practical implementation of this method is realized, demonstrating its efficacy in reducing joint load through running simulations.

articleTitle: A Modeling Method Based on Koopman Operator Theory for Omnidirectional Mobile Manipulator System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The omnidirectional mobile robotic arm system is a highly coupled, multivariate, and highly nonlinear system. The traditional modeling approach uses Lagrange method to establish dynamic model, which suffers from issues of complex modeling, unknown model parameters, and insufficient accuracy in modeling. In this paper, a modeling method based on Koopman operator theory is proposed for this system, which is essentially a data-driven modeling method. Specifically, this paper collects data on system dynamic characteristics and transforms complex nonlinear models into high-dimensional linear models. This paper preprocesses the voltage data in the dataset based on platform characteristics and obtains the Koopman high-dimensional linear model, avoiding the complex modeling problems using Lagrange methods. Simulation has been performed, which confirms the accuracy and effectiveness of using Koopman operator theory for modeling omnidirectional mobile manipulators.

articleTitle: A Hand Motion Recognition System Combining Wearable Sensing Gloves and Template Matching Algorithm
