publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Hand motion recognition systems, especially those these using wearable electronic glove, have received growing attention in the field of human-computer interaction and medical rehabilitation. However, two problems still exist: (1) the sensors are usually single, which fails to acquire the multi-sensor information; and (2) Pattern recognition based on deep learning algorithms tend to require a large number of samples to ensure pattern recognition accuracy, whereas obtaining a large amount of hand movement information from a patient is difficult. To address the above problems, this study develops a hand motion recognition system through combining a wearable sensing glove and a new template matching algorithm. The wearable sensing glove employs five Flex sensors and one Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) to obtain the gesture information, followed by realization of the human-computer interaction through the Unity3D software. Meanwhile, a simple template matching algorithm is constructed for the hand gesture recognition, which can recognize 10 numbers and 20 letters in American Sign Language (ASL) with an accuracy of 90.11% and 87.13%, respectively. The proposed hand motion recognition system can basically meet the needs of patients for hand movement recognition.

articleTitle: Improving Formation in Swarm Robotics with a Leader-Follower Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Collective Motion (CM) is a bio-inspired swarm behaviour observed in nature, such as schooling fish and flocking birds. In swarm robotics, CM is attained through the implementation of virtual viscoelastic links that generate attractive and repulsive forces among robots. This study investigates the challenges associated with maintaining formation integrity in specific geometrical arrangements, such as ring configurations. To address this, a Leader-Follower (L-F) approach is proposed to enhance the swarm shape stability. Simulation results demonstrated that the proposed method significantly optimised CM performance, achieving alignment of nearly 99% of the robots within 50 s. This shows the effectiveness of the L-F approach in successfully implementing swarm formation with a significant performance improvement.

articleTitle: Convolution and Transformer based hybrid neural network for Road Extraction in Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Road extraction in remote sensing images has a wide range of applications and is influential in the fields of automatic driving, city planning, navigation, etc. However, there are many shadows, buildings and trees on remote sensing images, which adds a lot of difficulties to extracting roads. In this paper, a hybrid neural network (HCTRNet) based on Convolution and Transformer is proposed for road extraction in remote sensing images. The HCTRNet backbone network has a pair of symmetric encoders and decoders, in which the main feature extraction module is HCTRNet Block. A new Hybrid Token Mixer (HT-Mixer) module is used in HCTRNet Block. HT-Mixer can dynamically utilise the global and local information of the image to incorporate the potential of large receptive fields and strong inductive bias without affecting the input dependency, which can largely improve the model's representation learning capability. After the decoder, this paper designs an Adaptive Feature Fusion Head module (AFFH) to integrate feature information from different scales in the feature layers in the decoding layer to enhance the robustness of the network for better road extraction. Experiments show that HCTRNet performs much better than current state-of-the-art algorithms on the publicly available Istanbul City Roads dataset, improving 10.04% in terms of IoU. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/whq-27/HCTRNet.

articleTitle: Load Prediction of Composite Curing Equipment Cluster Based on Combined EEMD-WOA-LSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: For groups utilizing composite curing equipment, load forecasting is crucial in ensuring productivity, optimizing energy consumption, and reducing costs. This paper aims to enhance the accuracy of load forecasting through the utilization of artificial intelligence algorithms. Neural networks with long shortterm memory (LSTM) are integrated into a combined model for short-term load forecasting, which is based on whale bionic optimization. The whale bionic algorithm is applied to improve parameter optimization accuracy and address the issue of local optimization within long-short-term memory neural networks. Multiple feature components are extracted from the source signal using empirical mode decomposition. The bionically optimized combined model utilizes each feature component as input for prediction, ultimately resulting in improved load prediction results. The enhanced combination model using whale bionics demonstrates reduced prediction error and greater accuracy when compared to the prediction results of RNN model, LSTM model, WOA-LSTM model, and EEMD-ARMA model.

articleTitle: Modelling and prediction of thermal error in rotary axis of machine tools under variable working conditions based on TPE-IndRNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Thermal error of rotary axis is one of the key factors affecting the machining accuracy of 5-axis machine tools. Currently, traditional methods struggle to model thermal error sequences over varying working conditions and extended periods. A spectral clustering method is utilized to automatically select temperature-sensitive points. Furthermore, a lightweight and efficient independent recurrent neural network (IndRNN) model is developed to accurately model and predict the thermal positioning errors of the rotary axis. The proposed model is capable of processing longer time series data. Training and predictive validation were conducted under variable working conditions. This lightweight model not only captures the time lag and thermal errors in temperature data but also exhibits strong generalization capabilities under varying working conditions. Experimental results indicate that the model's predictive accuracy exceeds 95%, with a maximum residual of less than 0.78μrad. It outperforms comparative models such as LSTM, GRU, and BiLSTM in terms of training speed and accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on Smooth Movement Control and Testing of a Wheeled-Legged Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This paper focuses on the application of wheeledlegged robots for extraterrestrial exploration. To address the stability and terrain adaptability issues during planetary surface exploration, a novel motion control strategy integrating body attitude control and support force control is proposed based on kinematic inverse solution. This strategy adjusts the body posture by dynamically regulating the length of each leg to ensure sufficient wheel-ground contact force while traversing rough terrains. The paper also conducts simulation and tests of the wheeled-legged robot in typical terrains. Results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm effectively overcomes terrain variations and enhances stability during the robot's movement.

articleTitle: Virtual Bipedal Passive Walking Control Based on Target Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This paper introduces a target-dynamics based virtual passive bipedal walking control method without reference gaits or energy. The method maps the 2-DOF bipedal robot into a 1-DOF system through input-output linearization at first. Then, the inner-leg angle of the robot is selected as the sole control output to track the target dynamics — a harmonic oscillator, which is found to be the intrinsic characteristic of the passive bipedal walking through numerical simulations and thus any other reference trajectories, e.g. the passive gaits or the energy, are no longer required. Finally, a constant ankle torque and a Port-Controlled Hamilton system based ankle torque are selected as the control inputs respectively. Simulations on different grounds are conduct to evaluate the controller performance. The results show the controller can produce stable virtual passive bipedal walking gaits on varied terrains with high trajectory tracking accuracy and energy efficiency, and each of the two types of input torques exhibits distinct advantages in terms of energy efficiency and adaptability.

articleTitle: Study on the Path Planning Based on A* Algorithm for Vascular Intervention Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In vascular interventional surgery, accurate path planning is essential to improve surgical success and reduce risk. This paper aimed to verify the effectiveness and practicability of the A* algorithm in the shortest path planning of vascular interventional surgical robot systems. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) vascular images were processed in advance to extract features and calibrate obstacles, simulating the path planning problem in vascular interventional surgery. The A* algorithm was then employed to search for the shortest path from the starting point to the endpoint. Based on the planned path, assistance could be provided to surgeons during operative procedures. The experimental results indicated that the A* algorithm effectively navigated obstacles and identified the shortest path. Moreover, through user-interactive design, this paper offered an intuitive operational experience, allowing users to interactively choose start and end points and display the algorithm’s search process and outcomes in real-time. This paper demonstrated the potential application of the A* algorithm within vascular structures and laid the groundwork for the future development of more efficient and intelligent systems for planning and navigating vascular interventional surgeries.

articleTitle: Continuous Control Method for Lower Limb Rehabilitation Robot Based on Self-learning Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Traditional lower limb rehabilitation robots employ discrete control methods, which are unable to decode human intention in real-time. To enhance human-machine interaction capabilities for patients with lower limb motor dysfunction, this study focuses on continuous control decoding of rehabilitation robots based on a self-learning strategy. An online classification model was developed, employing a multimodal brain-computer interface paradigm. The LGBM-LMS classification model was constructed to classify continuous control commands for the robot, converting them into control instructions for continuous control of the lower limb rehabilitation robot via electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. Experimental results indicate that this method reduces computational complexity and model redundancy, with an average recognition rate improvement of 17.82% per group.

articleTitle: A Safety Strategy for Vascular Interventional Surgery Robots based on Interactive Interface and Motion Scaling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Robot-assisted vascular interventional surgery (VIS) represents a significant advancement in medical technology, offering benefits such as reduced radiation exposure and improved surgical stability, thus positively impacting both doctors and patients. However, ensuring surgical safety through effective visual feedback and robust safety strategies remains crucial during VIS. Unfortunately, existing robot systems often fall short in providing intuitive intraoperative information feedback, burdening doctors with redundant data and potentially compromising surgical safety. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a novel host computer interface and an active surgical safety strategy. The proposed interface allows for real-time plotting of received data, delivering intuitive feedback on key intraoperative information. Additionally, the safety strategy dynamically adjusts the motion mapping coefficient between the leader and follower in risky conditions, minimizing collisions of interventional instruments with vessel walls. Following this proposal, an evaluation experiment was conducted to validate the functionality of the host computer interface and the efficacy of the surgical safety strategy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed host computer interface effectively plots intraoperative information in real time. Moreover, in risky scenarios, the safety strategy successfully reduces the displacement of the follower manipulator to 0.5 times and its average following error is 1.30mm, ensuring surgical safety.

articleTitle: Multi-UAV Collaborative Target Consensus Detection Using Enhanced Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Multi-UAV collaborative perception with region coverage has important applications in various fields such as post-disaster rescue, agricultural pest control, and enemy rear reconnaissance. The current region coverage algorithms focus on covering an area with the lowest redundancy and smallest coverage gap. However, simple swarm coverage methods cannot obtain accurate perception information for key target reconnaissance tasks. This paper focuses on the multi-UAV cross-coverage method to improve the accuracy of key target recognition. An improved particle swarm optimization algorithm is proposed under sensing and communication load constraints. Three improvements are implemented: particle velocity update strategy, weight update formula, and particle recombination strategy. The simulation results show the advantages of the proposed algorithm over classical methods and its effectiveness in cross-coverage and target consensus.

articleTitle: Research on defect detection method for thin-walled parts based on point cloud data processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: External impacts for Thin walled components can cause surface depressions and result in serious consequences. In order to detect these depressions , this article performs point cloud filtering and simplification prepossessing on the obtained defect point cloud, and uses the defective point cloud to fit a standard point cloud model; We used a point cloud feature description algorithm based on Fast Point Feature Histogram (FPFH) and the Nearest Point Iteration (ICP) algorithm to perform coarse and fine registration on two point clouds. Finally, we calculated the Euclidean distanceto defect the registered point clouds.

articleTitle: Study on the Improved Water Flow Prediction Based on Classification-Regression Approach for Amphibious Spherical Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Inspired by the lateral line systems found in aquatic organisms, an artificial lateral line system (ALLS) for underwater robots was developed. This technology was integrated into Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) to enhance their environmental awareness and navigation. This paper was focused on improving water flow prediction performance for a amphibious spherical robot (ASR) equipped with a ALLS comprising 12 pressure sensors. To address the challenge of the initial method relying on polynomial fitting based on data from a single sensor, which encounters difficulties when the flow direction falls between sensor angles. Two strategies were explored: increasing the quantity of sensors and implementing a Classification-Regression approach. Experimental simulations using Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) software were conducted to investigate the effectiveness of these strategies. Experimental results indicated that the classification-regression method significantly enhanced prediction accuracy compared to the original approach and offered a cost-effective alternative to increasing sensor quantity. This research contributed to the advancement of underwater robotics by enhancing perception capabilities, which were crucial for navigating challenging underwater environments efficiently.

articleTitle: Multiple Demand Response Models for Integrated Energy Systems Based on Electric-Heat Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Optimal scheduling of power networks can improve the balance of power loads and the efficiency of energy utilisation by reasonably allocating power resources and controlling the power transmission process, providing reliable power support for socio-economic development. Therefore, it is also crucial to strengthen the research on day-ahead scheduling of power networks. Firstly, considering the response variability of different demand-side resources, a multi-type integrated demand response (IDR) model taking into account price-type and incentive-type is established, secondly, to reduce the impact of source and load forecast errors on IES operation, a dual time-scale optimisation smoo thing model is constructed, and lastly, the arithmetic simulation is set up with different scenarios for comparative analyses.

articleTitle: Mechanism Design of a Mole-inspired Robot Burrowing with Forelimb for Planetary Exploration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: As one of the burrowing animals in nature, moles have high burrowing efficiency, thanks to their sharp incisors and powerful forelimbs that burrow and scrape the soil. Mapping the burrowing ability of moles into the design of the star soil burrowing robot will be beneficial to the exploration of extraterrestrial bodies and resource exploitation. This paper proposes a mole-inpired burrowing robot with forelimb for planetary exploration. First, we briefly review the current research status of mole-inpired burrowing robots. And then, for the analysis of the skeleton and burrowing movement of moles, the design requirements of the head, spine, forelimb mechanism, and hindlimb mechanism of the robot in this paper were extracted, and the kinematics of the designed forelimb mechanism and hindlimb mechanism were analyzed to obtain the motion trajectories of the robotic limbs. Finally, the torque changes of the robotic forelimbs and hindlimbs at different rotational speeds during one cycle were analyzed using simulation software. The results show that the designed mole-inspired robot burrowing with forelimb is reasonable and can provide a reference for the design of burrowing robots.

articleTitle: Design of a multifunctional end-effector for robotic replacement of TBM disc cutters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The robotic replacement of disc cutters in tunnel boring machine (TBM) is imperative for maintenance tasks' safety and efficiency. One major challenge is to managing the complex and cumbersome fastening components of disc cutters. This paper introduces a multifunctional end-effector that can grip a combined wrench to facilitate the alignment, fastening, and unfastening of cutter bolts, as well as grip the disc cutter. An integrated cutter house design eliminates the need for the robot to handle small bolts and nuts during remote operations. Additionally, a two-segment bolt design aids in the peg-in-hole procedure, ensuring a high success rate for robotic torque wrench alignment with the main fastening bolt. An alignment strategy for remote robot control is also proposed. We constructed a full-scale mock-up of the TBM disc cutter with the proposed cutter house structure to validate the proposed design and methods. Preliminary experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the system's mechanism and strategy in facilitating the swift assembly and disassembly of heavy disc cutters during replacement processes.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Integrated Benefits of Shore Power based on Network Hierarchy Analysis Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: With the continuous advancement of global trade, ships have become a vital mode of transportation in ports across the world. However, the use of auxiliary generators for power supply by ships during port calls has resulted in significant pollutant emissions and noise pollution, posing a threat to the surrounding environment. To address this issue, land-based power supply technologies have been put forward as a solution to decrease emissions and operating costs of ships. In this study, a new comprehensive evaluation model is introduced utilizing The Analytic Network Progress (ANP) method. By combining subjective and objective assignment methods like entropy weight method, a scientific evaluation system is constructed. This model assesses the benefits of port shore power projects from economic, environmental, and social perspectives. It provides decision makers with clear indicators of benefits, facilitating the global adoption of shore power technology. This not only improves environmental quality in ports but also lowers operating costs, ultimately contributing to sustainable development.

articleTitle: FE R-CNN: Feature Enhance R-CNN for Few-Shot Ship Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: With ongoing advancements in navigation technology, ship object detection has emerged as a focal point of current research. However, in real-world scenarios, annotated ship samples are often insufficient. To address these challenges, this paper proposes the Feature Enhance R-CNN (FE R-CNN) algorithm, aimed at enhancing the performance of ship object detection in few-shot scenarios. Firstly, the algorithm utilizes the Feature Refine Feature Pyramid Network (FR-FPN) module to improve upsampling and eliminate the aliasing effect. It leverages bidirectional cross-scale channels to comprehensively extract global multi-scale and semantic information. In the model fine-tuning phase, the Enhance Region Proposal Network (ERPN) module is proposed to effectively reduce the imbalance among the candidate regions for base and novel classes. Simultaneously, the Comparative Learning Branch (CLB) is proposed to increase the difference between features of different classes and the similarity between features of the same class. The synergistic effect of these modules significantly enhances the model's accuracy in locating few-shot objects and its capability in multi-scale object detection. Experiments on our custom maritime ship dataset MSD and VOC2012 show that our method outperforms various advanced algorithms, enhancing the model's applicability in real-world few-shot ship object detection scenarios.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Tremor Signal Recognition Method for a Vascular Interventional Surgery Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Hand tremor seriously reduce the accuracy and safety of robot-assisted vascular interventional surgery. However, the existing methods have some deficiencies, such as phase delay and distortion of operation signal. Therefore, a more accurate and universal method for tremor signal recognition is needed. This paper proposes a recognition method based on residual neural networks. And we use a Geomagic TouchX to collect tremor signal. The sliding window algorithm is used to process the data and make the dataset. Finally, the validation results indicate that the method can recognize normal operation signal and tremor signal, and ensure that the normal operation signal of the surgeon is not affected.

articleTitle: Development of Wearable Lightweight Continuum Manipulator to Enhance Capability of Human Arm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: A wearable continuum robot to supplement human capability is proposed. For this purpose, a light, flexible, and wearable robotic manipulator is designed and a 255-mm-long prototype, with a maximum diameter of 26mm and weight of 58g is fabricated. The prototype consists of two units: a continuum unit, which comprises several rigid links connected via a bar spring and three wires, a drive unit, which is used to tension wires to bend and control the continuum unit, including a control-and- power module. The drive unit contains three small motors and is equipped with pulleys to pull the wires. A model to simulate the behavior of the continuum unit is developed based on the capstan equation. The proposed model is used to estimate the posture of the continuum unit from the tension of wires. Furthermore, the validity of the proposed model is demonstrated experimentally. The results indicate a linear relationship between the bending angle and external force. The results suggest that the proposed model can be used to estimate external forces from the posture of the continuum unit. Object holding functions of the prototype worn on the wrist is demonstrated as an example of enhancement of human arm capabilities by wearable continuum manipulator.

articleTitle: Research on Target Localization Technology based on Depth of field fusion of generative adversarial networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Target positioning is a crucial step in beam target coupling, but the multi channel imaging system of the beam target coupling sensor struggles to obtain reliable target position information due to its small depth of field and poor illumination. This paper proposes a depth of field fusion algorithm based on generative adversarial networks that can merge multiple partially clear target images into a single image with higher clarity, thereby extending the depth of field and improving the accuracy of target positioning. Specifically, we first use OpticalFlow Net to estimate the optical flow to warp the source image and defocused image to a unified camera view, then generate an image with clear target edges using Fusion Net; finally, we extract the target position parameters through post processing methods such as edge detection to assist in high precision positioning. Additionally, to train our network, we created a multi focus pixel misaligned dataset based on the principle of point spread. Experimental results show that our algorithm outperforms existing advanced methods in both quality and effectiveness, being able to control the target positioning accuracy within 2.7μm, meeting the accuracy requirements.

articleTitle: Efficient Sparse LiDAR Data Reconstruction using Compressed Sensing for Real-Time Perception in Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to real-time perception for autonomous vehicles, introducing a LiDAR data reconstruction method utilizing Curvelet transform-based compressed sensing. The study substantiates the heightened efficacy of the Curvelet transform in adeptly managing complex geometric structures, yielding significant improvements in reconstruction quality and processing time compared to existing methodologies. Employing specialized algorithms tailored for reconstruction enhances sparse LiDAR data, thereby improving accuracy and detail in 3D mappings. Through systematic simulations, we validate the efficiency of the Curvelet transform, rendering the LiDAR system more proficient and faster at decision-making. This research contributes to the optimization of LiDAR data processing, representing a pivotal step towards the development of advanced real-time perception systems with potential applications in fully autonomous navigation. The transformative impact of Curvelet-based compressed sensing underscores its critical role in advancing the field of autonomous vehicle technology.

articleTitle: A Three-Dimensional Catheter Distal Force Sensor Based on Fiber Bragg Grating for Cardiac Ablation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This paper presents a three-dimensional force sensor based on fiber Bragg grating (FBG) with small size and high accuracy, which is proposed to be used in cardiac ablation procedures to achieve high-precision force feedback when the catheter tip contacts the tissue. The sensor consists of two hybrid elastomers for monitoring transverse and axial forces, as well as appropriately enhancing the deformation generated in the three directions to improve the sensitivity of the sensor. The structural body is configured with five suspended optical fibers, which are fixed with glue at both ends, and a preload is applied to ensure that the optical fibers are in a suspended state to avoid the chirp phenomenon. The article derives the theoretical deformation generated when the structural body is stressed, and proposes a decoupling method between the stressed temperature and deformation of the FBG fiber. In order to support further correction and improvement of the structural body performance and to further validate the feasibility of the structure, simulations based on finite element modeling were performed. The structure is configured to separate forces in three directions so that their measurements do not interfere with each other, thus maximizing decoupling between force components for highly accurate and high-resolution results.

articleTitle: Motion Planning of Redundant Robotic Arm Based on Human Arm Motion Principles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: How to generate human-like arm extension motion is a challenging problem in the process of human-robot collaboration to understand and judge the robot's motion intention. To address this problem, this paper proposes a multi-task planning algorithm for human-like arm motion based on the energy principle and the joint limit avoidance principle. First, a motion capture device is used to collect human arm motion data to obtain guidelines for human arm motion characteristics. On the basis of analyzing the arm demonstration data, the gravitational potential energy and virtual elastic potential energy models of the arm are established, and the mapping from the virtual variable stiffness of the arm to the virtual variable stiffness of the robot is realized. An end-effector trajectory is generated based on a dynamic movement primitives (DMPs) model and an optimization method, while a spherical linear interpolation (slerp) algorithm is used to generate the attitude sequence. In order to better execute the planned motion, the priority of the motion task is divided, and the design of two priority motion tasks is carried out by combining the gradient projection method. Finally, the humanoid arm motion multi-task planning algorithm proposed in this paper is simulated by simulation experiments, and the experimental results show that the method can generate the corresponding humanoid motions and has better motion accuracy.

articleTitle: Robotic Peg-in-hole Assembly Based on Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning with Hindsight Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In recent years, autonomous robotic peg-in-hole assembly has emerged as a prominent area of research. Due to the challenge of modeling and determining reward functions for peg-in-hole assembly scenarios, imitation learning is a more appropriate option as it enables learning policies from expert demonstrations without relying on environmental reward functions. However, traditional generative adversarial imitation learning (GAIL) methods are not efficient as they generate low-quality samples, resulting in high costs of interaction between the agent and the environment. This paper proposes a novel approach called hindsight transformation generative adversarial imitation learning (HT-GAIL), which employs hindsight experience to transform the samples generated by the generator into expert-like data. This expert-like data are then combined with expert demonstrations for adversarial network training. The proposed approach effectively addresses the issue of low utilization efficiency of generated samples, resulting in faster convergence of the algorithm. To validate the proposed algorithm, we constructed an autonomous peg-in-hole assembly platform using a six-degree-of-freedom manipulator. Comparative experiments were conducted to demonstrate the superior performance of the algorithm. The trained policies achieved success rates of 96%, 88%, and 61% for fit clearances of 1.12mm, 0.80mm, and 0.52mm, respectively, while maintaining assembly forces within 1.18N, 2.21N, and 9.10N, respectively.

articleTitle: A Local-to-Global Point Cloud Registration Algorithm Based on Joint Matching of Multi-keypoints
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Point cloud registration is a fundamental challenge in the field of 3D vision, particularly when dealing with scans that have limited overlapping features. In this paper, a local-to-global point cloud registration algorithm based on multi-keypoints joint matching is proposed. The algorithm incorporates neighborhood keypoints distance constraint and multi-keypoints joint matching scheme to establish robust and weighted correspondences. Furthermore, a fast segmentation and registration method is designed for overlapping regions, utilizing the weighted correspondences. The proposal algorithm achieves the expected results and is superior to mainstream traditional registration algorithms in terms of efficiency and accuracy.

articleTitle: Viability Study of Ammonia as Aircraft Fuel for Airbus A320 with Integrated Carbon Fiber Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The aviation industry stands at a pivotal juncture in its quest for sustainability, driven by the imperative to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and mitigate climate change impacts. This paper introduces a novel design for an aircraft constructed from carbon fiber materials and powered by Ammonia fuel, marking a significant leap towards environmentally friendly aviation technology. The lightweight, high-strength characteristics of carbon fiber are leveraged to optimize the aircraft’s structural efficiency, significantly reducing its weight compared to traditional materials and thus enhancing fuel efficiency. The use of Ammonia, a carbon-free fuel, promises a revolutionary reduction in the aircraft’s carbon footprint by eliminating CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions during flight, addressing one of the most pressing environmental challenges faced by the aviation sector.

articleTitle: Research on Hybrid Job Shop Scheduling Optimization Based on Genetic Algorithms and Simulated Annealing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In modern manufacturing systems and service industries, job scheduling problems are key to optimizing production processes, improving efficiency, and reducing costs. Particularly, the issue of minimizing the maximum processing time has attracted widespread attention. This paper introduces an innovative dual-population strategy and combines genetic algorithms with simulated annealing, aiming to efficiently solve job scheduling problems by leveraging the advantages of both. In this strategy, the main population is primarily driven by genetic algorithms, while the exploration population integrates the simulated annealing process, seeking a good balance between global search and local optimization. The dual-population approach not only expands the search space but also increases the diversity of solutions, thereby enhancing the possibility of finding solutions close to the global optimum. Through empirical validation, this paper's algorithm not only provides an effective new tool for solving complex scheduling problems but also offers useful references for the future application of intelligent algorithms in other fields.

articleTitle: Collaborative Hunting Strategy for Multi-Amphibious Spherical Robots in Underwater Environment with Obstacles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Collaborative target hunting by multiple underwater robots in obstacle environment is a challenging task. This study addresses this problem by proposing a cooperative hunting strategy based on an improved artificial potential field to achieve an efficient hunting task. The algorithm combines the perception and decision-making capabilities of the robots to guide the robots to form an effective roundup formation near the target by generating a suitable potential field in the environment. The robot's path is planned at a long distance, and the hunting potential points are assigned after approaching the target point, and finally the hunting of the target point is accomplished. The simulation results show that the method has good adaptability and feasibility in obstacle environments, and can effectively realize the cooperative target hunting task of multiple underwater robots.

articleTitle: Sequence Similarity Measurement for Multi-Human Motion Ability Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: There has been considerable advancement in human motion ability assessment utilizing computer vision-based approaches. However, the existing research suffer from ineffective assessment methods and inadequate evaluation indicators. For the multi-person target detection task, a human detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv7 is proposed. The TFC structure is designed to pay attention to the important information in the visual picture and solve the problems of small human foreground area and limb occlusion. The MP-SPD module was introduced to address the detection difficulty of low pixel faces with side face targets. For the task of sequence similarity metrics in the process of motor ability assessment, Hidden Markov Model (HMM) is introduced to improve the accuracy and speed of the similarity metrics of limb movement data. In the public dataset MPII, the improved human detection algorithm can improve the mean average precision(mAP50) by 2.98% compared with the original one while the real-time detection frame rate is guaranteed. Experimental results with 20 subjects show that the proposed HMM-based algorithm for motion sequence similarity assessment has millisecond reasoning speed, good generalization ability and robustness. It has obvious advantages in the performance and efficiency of the multi-person motion assessment applications.

articleTitle: Development and Application Validation of networked stool and pee management system
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This paper develops a networked stool and pee management system integrating Internet of Things technology to tackle the challenges associated with fecal care for bedridden elderly individuals. The system is designed to facilitate comprehensive management encompassing bowel dysfunction assessment, rehabilitation training, and cleaning care. Utilizing the MQTT protocol, the research encompasses the system’s architectural design, software development, and application validation, with the objective of enhancing elderly care quality. Following an ethical review, the system will soon enter the clinical trial phase.

articleTitle: A Laser Inertial SLAM System with High Robustness and Low Drift in Complex Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The paper proposes an improved version of LeGO-LOAM that utilizes Patchwork++ for ground segmentation, CVC (Curved-Voxel Clustering) for nonground point cloud clustering to remove noise, and incorporates IMU pre-integration factor. In the environment similar to underground conditions with irregular terrains such as potholes and uneven surfaces, as well as conditions containing a significant amount of noise, irrelevant point clouds and obstacles, the accuracy of SLAM decreases while computational complexity increases. Patchwork++ ground segmentation quickly and accurately identifies rugged surfaces, providing a stable reference plane to enhance the quality and accuracy of point cloud data. CVC precisely clusters nonground point clouds to remove noise, reducing computational complexity. IMU pre-integration improves pose estimation accuracy and system stability. The paper conducts a comparison between the proposed method and cutting-edge SLAM algorithms by utilizing KITTI dataset sequences that replicate the mentioned scenarios. The results clearly indicate that proposed method attains superior accuracy.

articleTitle: Magnetically Actuated Floating Millirobot Platform for Streamlined Flexible Neural Electrode Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Flexible neural electrodes have received increasing interests for implantable brain computer interfaces. However, due to the flexibility and miniaturization requirements, these fine neural electrodes often require a rigid probe as the shuttle to assist the successful implantation. Hence, the primary prerequisites for electrode implantation is the successful micro-assembly of the rigid probe and the electrode with a tiny engaging hole, whereas the conventional manual manipulation is error prone and time consuming. Although there have been recent development in micro-manipulation systems, a specific micro-manipulation system tailored for high-throughput, streamlined manipulations of multiple flexible electrodes is still lacking.. Therefore, this paper proposes a micro-manipulation system of streamlined floating robot for flexible electrode manipulation. The electrodes are deployed on a well-designed Magnetically-actuated Milli-Eelectrode Boat (MMEB), which can be magnetically controlled by a circular rotating magnet. A deep-learning based StreamNet is developed for visual servoing of the MMEB is achieved by accurately detecting the engaging hole from a microscopic vision system. In addition, the Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control (LADRC) is used to ensure stable and precise movement of the MMEB on the water surface. Experiments using phantom electrodes were conducted to evaluate the micro-manipulation process. The results show that the proposed system can achieve accurate locomotion of the engaging hole during both loading and releasing processes, with an average steady-state error is less than 3%.

articleTitle: Classification of Respiratory Sounds into Crackles and Noncrackles Categories via Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: When evaluating the efficacy of expectoration, it is essential not only to consider the subjective perception of patients but also to rely on objective assessment indicators. Crackles, as a crucial indicator for evaluating expectoration effectiveness, have rarely been independently classified in existing research. Additionally, approximately half of pulmonary sounds are incorrectly identified by hospital interns and medical students. To address these challenges, an automatic identification model for crackles is developed. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is employed to classify 1864 instances of crackles and 2291 instances of noncrackles (including rhonchi, wheezes, and normal lung sounds). The model combines pre-trained image feature extractors, respiratory sound data, and a CNN classifier. After training and evaluation, a predictive accuracy of 0.875 is achieved, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve of 0.89. This research aims to provide objective assessment indicators for expectoration treatment for patients through our research findings.

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of a Soft Manipulator Driven by Incompressible Fluid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Underwater operations with robotic manipulator are an emerging field. Compared to traditional robotic manipulator, soft manipulator offer safer environmental interactions and better flexibility. However, when operating in complex underwater environments, factors such as different water depths and the weight of held objects can lead to significant changes in the shape and pressure of the chamber, making the kinematics of the current soft arm inaccurate. To address these issues, we innovatively introduced the assumption of fluid incompressibility, which effectively constrains the kinematic model. We also designed and manufactured a hydraulic-driven flexible robotic arm suitable for underwater operations. Experiments show that the designed soft manipulator achieved more precise motion control under conditions of pressure interference.

articleTitle: VBAKF-based Correction Algorithm for Pure Inertial Solving of Attitude Angles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: One of the key issues to solve the problem of train derailment detection during motion requires accurate information about the pitch angle of the train. In order to solve the problem of inaccurate measurement of acceleration carrier attitude using traditional Kalman filter and complementary filter. In this paper, we propose a method to correct the dispersed pitch angle obtained by pure inertial solution by taking the pitch angle obtained by variational Bayesian adaptive Kalman filter(VBAKF) solution as a reference, and introduce variational Bayesian adaptive filtering method to correct the attitude weight calculated by the accelerometer by designing the acceleration threshold to adapt to the acceleration change; Then ,the data are stored in a queue of size 100s, and the queue is updated every moment to ensure the continuity of the data; Finally, the relative change in pitch angle is obtained by making a difference between the data in the queue for the 0.3s intervals within the queue, aiming at detecting derailment by measuring short-term changes in the train's direction. The algorithm is experimented and the effectiveness of the algorithm is verified by the actual data. The root mean square error from the baseline is within the acceptable range of 0.05°.

articleTitle: Measurement Method and Uncertainty Analysis of POF Dosimeter for 125I Source Dose Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: To address the problem of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">125</sup>I seed source dosimetry in brachytherapy, this paper proposes the use of a polymer optical fiber dosimeter to measure seed source dosimetry parameters and gives the uncertainty analysis. The key factors affecting the accuracy of dose measurement around the seed source are discussed, and the uncertainties of the fiber-optic dosimeter, the initial information about the seed source, and the measurement system device are analyzed. The <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">125</sup>I seed source dose parameters are measured according to the TG-43 standard and the two-dimensional dose distributions are presented using interpolation method. The results demonstrate that the optical fiber dosimeter has the ability to measure dose parameters of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">125</sup>I seed sources.

articleTitle: Bearing Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Multi-Scale Fusion Denoising Capsule Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Rolling bearings are key components in many mechanical equipment, and their performance directly affects the operating status of the entire equipment. However, in actual operating environments, bearings are often disturbed by various noises, which makes it extremely difficult to extract bearing fault characteristics. In response to these challenges, a capsule network model based on multi-scale fusion denoising mechanism is proposed. Multi-scale decomposition of vibration signals is performed to extract feature information at different frequencies, and the signal is denoised using attention thresholds to optimize feature expression. At the same time, the integration of capsule networks enhances the ability of model identification and expression of intrinsic data structures, thereby enhancing the effect of fault feature extraction. Through experimental verification, the model can extract fault features in complex environments, thereby offering a robust methodology for the detection of rolling bearing faults.

articleTitle: PFSC:Pyramid R-CNN for Point-Voxels with Focal Sparse Convolutional Networks for 3D Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In the point cloud 3D object detection task, the point cloud data is unevenly distributed in 3D space. Therefore, whether it is regular sparse convolution or submanifold sparse convolution, there is a significant difference in the detection performance when dealing with objects at different positions using sparse convolutional networks. Therefore, this paper proposes an improvement using focal sparse convolution to break the limitations of traditional convolution methods and enhance the representation ability of sparse convolution. Focal sparse convolution is utilized to replace the currently better-performing two-stage object detection network based on the combination of points and voxels, enhancing the end-to-end training effectiveness and achieving better detection results. And an optional detachable auxiliary network is added, which, during the training stage, combines point features to guide the backbone network in learning the structural information of the 3D point cloud, enhancing the localization accuracy of the backbone network. Extensive experiments have been conducted on the KITTI dataset to validate the proposed method, yielding promising detection results and demonstrating the effectiveness of the approach.

articleTitle: Configuration-Aware Robotic Trajectory Planning Based on Deep Deterministic Policy Gradients for Active Object Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Active object tracking provides a solution simultaneously addressing tracking and camera control, which can be usually implemented by robotic manipulators amounted with the camera at the end effector (e.g., move left, move forward, etc.). Trajectory planning is particularly the key technique for the control of robots during the tracking process. However, traditional trajectory planning methods are unable to achieve active tracking using robotic manipulators with different configurations, leading to poor generality and long training times. To address these problems, this paper proposes an improved trajectory planning method based on deep deterministic policy gradients (DDPG), to implement active object tracking tasks. A plug-in is designed to comply with the configuration of robotic manipulator. To improve generality and training efficiency, a novel reward function is proposed. Several experiments are conducted using a two-DoF robotic manipulator and a UR5 robot in the simulation and the physical two-DoF pantilt-zoom (PTZ). The proposed method can be applied to robots with different configurations. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method is feasible and has faster training speed and better active tracking performance compared with PPO, TD3, and SAC.

articleTitle: Integration of GNSS and Strong Motion Accelerometer based on Robust Adaptive Recursive Noise Kalman Filter by Variational Bayesian Approximations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) allows for precise monitoring of ground displacements, offering accuracies ranging from millimeters to centimeters, and sample rates varying between 1Hz and 50Hz. However, the GNSS observation signal is susceptible to the presence of a complex seismic environment with vegetation cover and strong external dynamic interference, in which case its accuracy and reliability cannot meet the requirements of coseismic deformation monitoring. Strong motion (SM) accelerometers, as a kind of inertial sensor, are capable of recording middle-rate to high-rate ground accelerations without electromagnetic signal interference and demonstrate stable working performance. An accurate displacement series can be obtained by combining GNSS and SM accelerometers. Usually, a Kalman filter is employed to merge GNSS displacements and SM acceleration data, using priori fixed noise values for both datasets. However, due to the time-varying errors introduced by the aforementioned disturbances, employing fixed noise for GNSS displacements is inappropriate. In this study, a recursive noise Kalman filter using variational Bayesian approximations is employed. The GNSS displacement noise covariances' sufficient statistics are adaptively estimated through iterative processes. Additionally, robust equivalent weight functions and adaptive factor scaling based on predicted residuals are incorporated into the estimation process to mitigate outliers. The proposed method's performance is validated through a shake table experiment. In standard shake table test, it shows an accuracy enhancement of up to 21% compared to the conventional Kalman filter, achieving a correlation coefficient (CC) of 0.97. When outliers are introduced into GNSS displacement data, the proposed method yields up to 49% greater accuracy than the Kalman filter, with a CC of 0.96 relative to references.

articleTitle: Integrating DeepRL with Robust Low-Level Control in Robotic Manipulators for Non-Repetitive Reaching Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In robotics, contemporary strategies are learning-based, characterized by a complex black-box nature and a lack of interpretability, which may pose challenges in ensuring stability and safety. To address these issues, we propose integrating a collision-free trajectory planner based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) with a novel auto-tuning low-level control strategy, all while actively engaging in the learning phase through interactions with the environment. This approach circumvents the control performance and complexities associated with computations while addressing nonrepetitive reaching tasks in the presence of obstacles. First, a model-free DRL agent is employed to plan velocity-bounded motion for a manipulator with 'n' degrees of freedom (DoF), ensuring collision avoidance for the end-effector through joint-level reasoning. The generated reference motion is then input into a robust subsystem-based adaptive controller, which produces the necessary torques, while the cuckoo search optimization (CSO) algorithm enhances control gains to minimize the stabilization and tracking error in the steady state. This approach guarantees robustness and uniform exponential convergence in an unfamiliar environment. Theoretical assertions are validated through the presentation of simulation outcomes.

articleTitle: An Efficient Depth-tracking Method for Live Control of Laser Drilling Process with Optical Coherence Tomography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Laser drilling has been widely used for fabricating holes in the semiconductor industry due to high throughput and small heat-affected zone. However, it produces varying depths owing to uncertain external conditions and needs a live control at a few kHz rate to handle the fast material removal rate. Optical coherent tomography holds a capacity of in situ acquiring raw interferogram at a high rate (>80 kHz), but the depth extraction is slow (<0.5 kHz) due to the involved heavy Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). To address it, an efficient depth-tracking algorithm is proposed to save the FFT. It searches the depth in the raw interferogram locally with a known last depth given the two truths that only one depth exists and the adjacent depths would not change significantly. The proposed algorithm was proved to expedite the measuring rate to around 3 kHz with a sub-pixel tracking precision. To further secure the rate from the interrupt of operation system, the tracking process is parallelly implemented with a stabilized 50 kHz in a field programmable gate array. The tests were conducted on probe cards with depth variations introduced by offsetting laser focus. The proposed method exhibited the capacity of maintaining a uniform depth.

articleTitle: Research on Modeling the Output Behavior of Cable Drive Surgical Instruments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery, surgeons operate by controlling surgical instruments inserted into the abdominal cavity. These instruments are generally elongated and narrow. To meet surgical requirements, wire transmission (referred to as "cable-driven" transmission) is commonly used. Cable-driven systems are favored for their small size and light weight. However, due to the complex path of cable transmission within the surgical instruments, the transmission of displacement and force exhibits nonlinear characteristics such as hysteresis effects. Additionally, the coupling effects between different degrees of freedom of the surgical instruments make precise control a challenging research area. This paper improves the displacement/force transmission model of the forceps' closed-loop cable-driven structure and utilizes a feedforward compensation strategy for displacement output compensation. Work on predicting gripping force was also conducted. Through experiments, we have verified that this model can effectively reduce the hysteresis errors in the motion of the cable-driven mechanism, accurately predict the gripping force exerted by the forceps, thereby enhancing the positional accuracy of the forceps and improving the accuracy of gripping force estimation in sensorless scenarios.

articleTitle: A Collision Detection Algorithm of Inspection Robot for Steam Generator Heat Transfer Tubes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Ensuring the operational safety of inspection robot for steam generator heat transfer tubes necessitates continuous internal collision detection to prevent self-collision and external collision detection to avoid contact with the surrounding environment. However, current collision detection algorithms struggle to balance accuracy with computational efficiency and are not fully applicable to the unique conditions of a nuclear power plant. This paper introduces a novel collision detection algorithm specifically tailored for a crawler-type inspection robot for steam generator heat transfer tubes. By translating three-dimensional collision issues into two-dimensional intersection problems, the algorithm simplifies the complexity of collision detection while ensuring accuracy. Simulation results indicate that the algorithm achieves an average computation speed of 0.02 seconds per instance, which is sufficient to meet real-time planning requirements during autonomous operations. Furthermore, even in the presence of motion errors, the algorithm maintains a 100% safety rate, guaranteeing absolute safety of the robot's movement. These findings further validate the feasibility and practicality of the proposed algorithm for use within the nuclear power plant environment.

articleTitle: In-process Monitoring of Penetration Depth and Contact Width During Laser Lap Welding Using Fused OCT Depth and Coaxial High Speed Image
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Electric mobility has emerged as a paradigm shift towards cleaner, more efficient, and sustainable transportation systems. Laser lap welding is being adopted in battery manufacturing due to its unique advantages including high throughput, noncontact access, excellent precision, and small heat-affected zone. An important challenge of laser lap welding is the limited capability for in-process monitoring of penetration depth and contact width of weldment, which determines electrical resistance and joint strength. This requires three-dimensional live information of the molten pool/keyhole. The existing techniques are limited in surface imaging or indirect measurement of penetration depth, hence the precision is limited due to the intrinsic starving-signal in all dimensions. To address this issue, an optical system was designed to couple optical coherence tomography depth imaging with a coaxial high-speed camera to capture the three-dimensional information synchronously. A multimodal deep learning network was created to fuse the two-source data for predicting the depth and contact width. Experiments were conducted with different laser power and welding speeds, and the cross-sections of the weldment were cut and micro-imaged as the ground truth. Compared to the individual sensing systems, the proposed fused system exhibits improved precision on both the depth and contact width.

articleTitle: Investigation of Upper Limb Training Device Integrating Cognitive and Motor Functions Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) is considered a transitional state between normal aging and dementia, often progressing to Alzheimer’s Disease (AD). Understanding the characteristics of brain function in MCI patients and intervening early is crucial for dementia prevention and treatment. Utilizing robotic technology for rehabilitation training is an important approach in rehabilitation therapy. We designed a combined cognitive and motor function upper limb rehabilitation training paradigm for MCI patients. The cognitive task (SC) involves numerical cognition, while the motor task (MT) consists of active upper limb training. Motion data during dual-task (DT) periods were collected from patients, and functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (fNIRS) technology was utilized to assess cerebral cortical hemodynamic responses. The aim of this study is to explore the changes in motion data and cerebral cortical hemodynamic responses of MCI patients during rehabilitation training with the Upper Limb Training Device (ULTD), and to evaluate the effectiveness of this paradigm for the rehabilitation training of MCI patients. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of the neural processes involved in robot-assisted parallel interactive tasks, providing insights for more effective robot-assisted rehabilitation therapy.

articleTitle: CWF-HRNet: Context-aware Fusion for Human Pose Estimation based on High-Resolution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: This study proposes a novel CWF-HRNet, based on dynamic perception fusion, to enhance human pose estimation for volleyball coaching visual aids. It addresses key challenges in real-world teaching scenarios, such as blurred image details, inadequate multi-resolution information fusion, and limb occlusion. The CWF-HRNet integrates the CARAFE upsampling module, which dynamically adjusts pixel contributions using context-related weight matrices based on image content. To improve multi-resolution information fusion, the HL-WASP multi-scale fusion module combines shallow features from different layers, expanding the feature receptive field and enhancing detail capture. Additionally, a context-based dynamic perception module enhances global semantic understanding to address occlusions. Experimental results demonstrate that CWF-HRNet improves evaluation metrics AP, AP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sup>, AP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">75</sup>, AP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</sup>, AP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sup>, and AR by 4.1%, 2.6%, 3.5%, 3.6%, 4.4%, and 3.4%, respectively, compared to the HRNet model, while reducing parameters by 14%. These enhancements underscore the superior accuracy and efficiency of CWF-HRNet in challenging scenarios, making it well-suited for real-time sports training applications.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Evaluation of a Three-Dimension Triphibian Robot Propulsion Unit Based on Electric Ducted Fan Engine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Robots capable of traversing multiple environments impose stringent design requirements on their propulsion units. In order to add flying capabilities to the existing amphibious spherical robot and enhance its maneuverability while optimizing propulsion strategies, this paper proposes a three-dimension triphibian robot propulsion unit based on electric ducted fan engine. The paper begins by introducing the concept of the robot and its significance. Subsequently, it analyzes the design requirements for the propulsion unit based on the functional upgrade. Following this, an evaluation system is designed to conduct thrust tests and verify the power of the propulsion unit, demonstrating the effectiveness of its design. This lays the groundwork for the comprehensive design and experimentation of the three-dimensional triphibian robot propulsion unit.

articleTitle: Cooperative Navigation System of AGV and UAV with Autonomous and Precise Landing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Along with the growing popularity of the unmanned smart factory concept, AGVs and UAVs are beginning to take on a wide variety of complex tasks. Due to the limitations of a single robot’s capabilities, which restrict the application of these robots within factories, the study of heterogeneous UAV-AGV systems has become increasingly important. Given the potential deployment of wireless charging and the use of LiDAR for SLAM, precise landing is a crucial part of this process; however, because of the ground effect and external disturbances, precise landing is a difficulty awaiting resolution. Thus, this paper proposes a system design for the precise landing of a UAV on an AGV. First, we design a customized landing gear for precise landing to reduce the impact of ground effects and external disturbances, which is validated by fluid simulation. Second, we present a marker-based visual servoing system to enable a UAV to accurately land on the precise position of an AGV with a fixed attitude. In the end, preliminary experiments were performed to demonstrate that this work successfully addressed the autonomous, precise landing of UAVs on the landing gear of AGVs. These experiments also demonstrate both the effectiveness and excellence of this approach.

articleTitle: Method for Determining Ultra-Wideband Anchor Coordinates in a Cell-splitting Environment for Positioning a Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: We construct an ultra-wideband (UWB) positioning system for autonomous mobile robots supporting the transport of fruits. We also propose a mobile robot system that uses the UWB positioning system for autonomous movements in environments with posts arranged in a lattice. In a UWB positioning system, the coordinates of the UWB devices in the trellis must be determined in advance. In the proposed system, the UWB devices automatically estimate their own coordinates. The positioning accuracy of the proposed UWB system is verified through experiments.

articleTitle: Study on Improved D* Lite-Based Obstacle Avoidance and Navigation Strategy for the Ellipsoidal Underwater Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Due to the complexity of the underwater environment, it is of great significance to improve the obstacle avoidance and navigation ability of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs). In this paper, the Ellipsoidal Underwater Robot (EUR) platform was introduced first. Then, an improved D* Lite path planning and navigation algorithm was proposed, where the improving strategy includes a risk model and path smooth strategy based on splines. Besides, according to the planned path, a trajectory tracking law for the EUR was developed in order to guide the EUR in the expected direction. Furthermore, the simulation and practical experiments were conducted, and the results consistently demonstrated that the proposed strategy in this paper could effectively plan and guide the EUR to perform path planning and navigation while avoiding obstacles.

articleTitle: Design and tracking performance analysis of a cable pulling rudder loading test mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: In order to meet the general loading test requirements of aircraft control surface in different application scenarios, this paper proposes a cable-pulling loading test mechanism design and performance analysis method for movable rudder surface. Based on the proposed cable actuation scheme, the kinematic and static analysis is carried out in this paper, which lays the foundation for the subsequent selection of key parameters and the development of control algorithms. The active and passive control strategies of the test device are introduced and validated by dynamic simulation to ensure that the desired movable loading target is achieved. Finally, considering the system uncertainty, the distribution characteristics of tracking performance under error propagation were analyzed, so as to provide a basis for improving the system performance.

articleTitle: Joint Estimation of SOC and Operating Voltage of Vehicle 12V Lithium-ion Battery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Vehicle 12V lithium-ion battery is mainly used for automotive startup and low-voltage system power supply, and accurately estimate its state of charge (SOC) and operating voltage in time is essential to vehicle safety. For this, a joint estimation method for SOC and operating voltage of on-board 12V lithium-ion battery is proposed based on the second-order RC equivalent circuit model combined with the vehicle pre-charge conditions. In additional, the adaptive forgetting factor recursive least squares (AFFRLS) method is adopted to obtain circuit parameters, subsequently, double extended Kalman filter (DEKF) algorithm used to achieve SOC online estimation of 12V lithium-ion battery. Furthermore, combined with characteristic current curve under charging failure scenario, strategy for predicting the operating voltage of 12V lithium-ion battery is also proposed. Finally, a 12V 44Ah lithium-ion battery is selected to carry out the validation as proof of concept. The experimental results show that in the temperature range of 0 ℃ ~40 ℃ , the proposed joint estimation method has a maximum error of 1.6% in the SOC estimation and the accuracy of the operating voltage prediction is controlled within ±0.3%.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Dynamic Modeling and Simulation of Guidewire in Vascular Intervention Surgery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: During TACE interventional surgery, the acquisition and delivery direction of the guidewire's shape is a critical step in the surgery. Traditionally, physicians analyze the shape and endpoint location of the guidewire intraoperatively through real-time X-ray fluoroscopy. However, the low resolution of X-ray images combined with the small proportion that the guidewire occupies within the real-time X-ray image window increases visual fatigue for physicians. When vascular interventional surgical robots undertake the task of guidewire delivery instead of doctors, it is particularly important to analyze the shape and visual feedback of the guidewire. We developed a three-dimensional dynamic model of the guidewire based on MuJoCo, simulating the delivery process of the guidewire in the vascular model during interventional surgery within MuJoCo. The experimental results show that our guidewire model can successfully navigate through different vascular branch structures, completing actions such as advancement, retraction and rotation. This can not only be applied to the training simulation of vascular interventional surgeons but also further explore the vascular interventional surgery robots in conjunction with computer vision technology for auxiliary interventions.

articleTitle: Optimization of electrical stimulation parameters based on the primary motor cortex
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Transcranial electrical stimulation refers to the transmission of weak electrical currents to the brain through scalp electrodes to induce neuromodulatory effects. Current usually passes through two large electrodes, generating a diffusion electric field. In this article, we propose a new paradigm where multiple small electrodes with independent current control are systematically optimized to generate targeted and effective stimuli under safety constraints. We used finite element method combined with a model based on human head magnetic resonance imaging to develop a linear system that correlates the applied scalp current with the generated electric field. Then apply optimization techniques to derive yield increasing parameters that maximize intensity or focus at the target location. The results indicate that the optimal electrode structure is closely related to the required electric field orientation and optimization criteria. The two optimization methods used have achieved good results.

articleTitle: A Joint Adjustment Method for Seafloor Geodetic Control Network with Depth Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: The seafloor geodetic control network provides location-based services for marine navigation and positioning. The conventional seafloor geodetic control network adjustment method generally treats the position of acoustic transducers obtained by the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) positioning as known without error. Neglecting the coordinate errors of acoustic transducer can significantly compromise the accuracy of seafloor transponder positioning. Additionally, the high-precision depth information provided by the pressure gauge is not introduced into the conventional seafloor geodetic control network adjustment method. In this method, we propose a joint adjustment method for seafloor geodetic control network with additional depth constraints. The positions of both acoustic transducer and seafloor transponder are treated as unknown parameters, and the position of acoustic transducer is regarded as virtual observation. The high-precision depth observation is likewise introduced to further improve the precision of underwater positioning. Validation involves simulated and field tests. The results demonstrate that our proposed method significantly enhances the accuracy of seafloor transponder positioning. In comparison to the joint adjustment method, improvements range from 2.1cm to 21.4cm. When contrasted with the conventional adjustment method, enhancements span from 2.5cm to 22.0cm.

articleTitle: Motor Imagery and Mental Arithmetic Classification Based on Transformer Deep Learning Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Non-invasive electroencephalography (EEG) signals find widespread application in brain-computer interfaces (BCI), with paradigms such as motor imagery (MI), mental arithmetic (MA) and emotion recognition being particularly common. This study aims to explore feature extraction and classification methods for MI and MA tasks. We employed convolutional neural networks (CNN) combined with Transformer networks and Fasternet Block to extract features. Through our reaearch, we obtained features for MI and MA tasks, and used softmax classification for binary classification of these tasks. We conducted on a publicly available dataset consisting of data from 29 subjects. The experimental results demonstrate that our method achieved high classification accuracy in MI and MA tasks. The final accuracy rates for MI and MA tasks were 88.67% and 91.23%, respectively.

articleTitle: Multi-stage Dynamic Scheduling Optimization for Autonomous Mobility-on-Demand Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
abstract: Autonomous Mobility-on-Demand (AMoD) system is booming in urban transportation, however, the uncertain and complex fleet dynamic scheduling remains one of the main challenges for operators. Therefore, this study proposes a multistage dynamic scheduling approach for shared autonomous electric vehicles (SAEVs). Specifically, considering the matching characteristics of the different tasks, the vehicle order-taking and charging tasks are modelled as bipartite graph maximum weight matching problems with the objectives of maximizing order revenue and minimizing charging mileage. The vehicle repositioning task is modelled as integer programming with the objective of minimizing the vehicle dispatch mileage, and stochastic chance-constrained programming is applied to cope with uncertain user demands. A solution strategy combining the KM algorithm with Gurobi solver and greedy strategy is designed to obtain the real-time scheduling instructions. Finally, numerical experiments based on real travel data validate the advantages of the proposed approach in reducing fleet scheduling costs and improving system operational revenues.

articleTitle: EEG Signal Driving Fatigue Detection based on Differential Entropy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
